title: Engagement Specialist - Adolescent Shelter (3582)
description:
This is a bargaining unit position represented by the OPEIU. All terms and conditions of employment are subject to change in accordance with a collective bargaining agreement.

WORK SCHEDULE: This position is full-time, regular and non-exempt. Shifts will vary and may require working evenings, weekends, and holidays. Day Shift (8:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m.), Swing (4:00 p.m. – 12:00 a.m.), and Grave (12:00 a.m. – 8:00 a.m.).

POSITION SUMMARY: Under the supervision of the Program Manager or Supervisor, the Engagement Specialist is responsible for the daily management of the program site. All housing programs are open 24/7 and per agency licensing and or contract requirements, programs must maintain safe staff and client ratio to provide services to our clients. In conjunction with other staff, the Engagement Specialist’s task is to create a safe and caring environment for vulnerable young people in residence who are preparing to transition to become more self-sufficient. The position requires an individual who can actively contribute to a positive, stable, responsive, and responsible environment for change.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Build trust and rapport with young people experiencing homelessness and housing instability, young people who have experienced sexual exploitation and/or young people who are at risk.
  • Engage, support, coach, and develop young people using healing-centered engagement practices and a strength-based approach.
  • Provide on-site supervision, while maintaining professional boundaries in providing crisis intervention and services to young people. Must learn and apply positive behavior modification techniques and model effective de-escalation, problem-solving and mediation skills. Be willing to intervene in times of crisis using these skills.
  • Complete necessary paperwork and data collection, including intake, enrollment, case notes as needed. Additionally complete incident reports within the required timeframe on any facility damage, medical emergencies or any incident which occurs out of the ordinary functioning of the site.
  • Maintain accurate and timely case records, shift notes, logbooks, and other types of documentation, and enter data into YouthCare’s Case Worthy client management system according to agency standards.
  • Execute Performance and Quality Improvement (PQI) tasks and accreditation standards and adhere to all agency policies and procedures.
  • Comply with the agency’s mandated reporting requirement and report suspected abuse, neglect, or sexual exploitation of minors within the required timeframe.
  • Work cooperatively and collaboratively with all site staff, partners, and volunteers to create a nurturing, dynamic, and constructive environment for young people.
  • Support with coordination of basic needs, inclusion of meals, referrals to systems of support, clothing, etc.
  • Develop and deliver group and individual programming to foster life and social skill development. Programming provides an opportunity for youth and young adults to engage, increase knowledge and skills, and moves young people toward the agency’s four core outcomes - housing stability, financial independence, community support, and wellness.
  • Work collaboratively with other YouthCare programs, families, school district professionals, crisis services personnel, and staff from other agencies in support of youth.
  • Communicate client needs and behaviors to the appropriate staff, and refer young people to appropriate and necessary services, as needed.
  • Oversee the safety and cleanliness of the facility, including disinfecting surfaces and following cleaning protocols. Perform light janitorial work, including vacuuming/sweeping/mopping; taking out trash; and similar tasks, as outlined by site need and agency protocols. Compile maintenance requests and submit them to program leadership/maintenance staff as needed.
  • Participate in regular supervision, client consultations, and staff and agency meetings. Attend and fully participate in meetings, professional development opportunities, and designated training sessions as required.
  • Act as a professional representative of YouthCare and maintain a professional working environment (office, personal workspace, agency vehicle, etc.).
  • Maintains a flexible work schedule (filling shifts on some weekends, early and/or late hours) and must be willing to be cross- trained in providing support with shift coverage in on-call basis for the program and the agency, as required by individual program needs.
  • Maintain annual completion of 24 hours of in-service training.
  • Reliably attend and participate in training and development as needed for your role and the needs of our Agency as a whole such as program requirements, DEI&J, supervision, and others as identified.
  • Contribute to our DEI&J culture by creating at least one SMART Goal related to DEI&J within your control to deliver.

PROGRAM SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Work closely with YouthCare staff and Case Managers in engaging young people in individualized education, employment and life skill plans and activities.
  • With directions from Case Manager, help plan for, direct and/or provide support for recreational, educational, and therapeutic activities that are in alignment with client goals.
  • Educate young people on independent living skills/tasks, including but not limited to personal care and food preparation.
  • Provide transportation for outings and client appointments; operate the agency vehicle in accordance with the law and in a safe manner.
  • Assist in packing client belongings and cleaning and sanitizing exited bedrooms, and prepping bedrooms for incoming clients.
  • At designated times, prepare and cook meals for up to 14 residents and staff.
  • Dispensing medication (as needed) and complete related documentation. Perform medication reconciliation and update medical binder forms according to individual program procedures and timeline.
  • Maintain an awareness of client whereabouts and line of site supervision, as required. Complete room, bed, and safety checks at required intervals and complete required documentation.
  • Engage and participate in all scheduled staff meetings and be an instrumental team member in supporting young people, by communicating effectively with all program staff, program participants, personnel from other agencies and visitors.

This job description is not intended to cover every aspect of your job at YouthCare. We are a team that works together to meet the needs of our clients, and every member of the team is expected to pitch in and help even beyond the specific responsibilities listed in this description.

title: Kia Angitū te Anamata | Summer Internship Programme 2026 - 2027
description:
This opportunity is for registered hapū members of Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei.

Ko wai mātou | Who are we

Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei is a hapū of Ngāti Whātua. We live in and around the Tāmaki isthmus. We hold to our mana motuhake, our history, our culture, our identity, and our reo. Our whakapapa traces to Tuperiri and the hapū Ngā Oho, Te Taoū, and Te Uringutu.

We are tangata whenua in Tāmaki. Our authority over land and sea rests on take tupuna, take raupatu, ahi kā, and tuku whenua.

Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei Trust looks after the collective affairs of our hapū. We have more than 8,000 registered members across Aotearoa and overseas. Ōrākei Marae is our cultural hub.

Te Kahu Tōpuni o Tuperiri describes the protective reach of our ancestor across our rohe.

Te Whiwhinga Mahi | The Opportunity

Kia Angitū te Anamata is the Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei summer internship programme for uri currently completing tertiary study.

This year, we are offering one application process, with placements available across a range of teams and areas of mahi. Placements will be based on available opportunities, organisational needs, and the skills, studies and interests of successful applicants.

As an intern, you will:

  • Complete meaningful mahi within your placement team.

  • Gain practical experience aligned, where possible, with your studies and career interests.

  • Work alongside experienced kaimahi and leaders.

  • Build your confidence, workplace capability and professional networks.

  • Learn more about how Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei works to deliver outcomes for whānau.

  • Take part in programme activities, wānanga and a collaborative group project.

  • Strengthen your connection to Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei kaupapa, people and places.

This is an opportunity to contribute, learn and explore where your skills and aspirations could take you next.

Ko wai koe | About you

We are looking for uri who:

  • Are currently completing tertiary study;

  • Are ready to gain practical workplace experience;

  • Can communicate well and work collaboratively with others;

  • Are open to learning, feedback and new challenges; and

  • Can manage their time, workload and responsibilities with support.

Previous work experience is helpful but not essential. We welcome applicants from a wide range of study areas, backgrounds and levels of experience.

Ngā rā matua | Key dates

  • Programme begins: Wednesday, 18 November 2026

  • Programme concludes: Wednesday, 17 February 2027

  • A two week summer shutdown period will apply over Christmas and New Year.

Applicants must be available for the full programme period.

How to apply

Select Apply Now and complete one application for the Kia Angitū te Anamata Summer Internship Programme.

As part of your application, tell us about:

  • Your connection to Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei and how you would like to grow that connection;

  • What you are studying, your career aspirations and what you hope to gain from the internship;

  • The contribution you hope to make to Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei through your learning, skills, and future career.

Successful applicants will be matched to available placements based on their skills, interests and studies, alongside organisational needs across Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei and Whai Rawa.

Applications close: 13 October 2026

For further information, contact matauranga@nwo.iwi.nz

title: Lead SRE
description:
Company Overview



Docusign brings agreements to life. Over 1.5 million customers and more than a billion people in over 180 countries use Docusign solutions to accelerate the process of doing business and simplify people’s lives. With intelligent agreement management, Docusign unleashes business-critical data that is trapped inside of documents. Until now, these were disconnected from business systems of record, costing businesses time, money, and opportunity. Using Docusign’s Intelligent Agreement Management platform, companies can create, commit, and manage agreements with solutions created by the #1 company in e-signature and contract lifecycle management (CLM).


What you'll do



We are building an internal engineering function dedicated to owning the reliability, code-ification, and continuous delivery of our enterprise security tooling - replacing legacy, one-off consulting work with modern software engineering practices. As our founding Lead Site Reliability Engineer, you will architect and drive the infrastructure-as-code, automation, and operational maturity across our entire security platform portfolio - including SIEM/SOAR, EDR/NDR/XDR, SAST/DAST, CNAPP/CSPM. Partnering closely with Core Platform and DevOps engineering teams, you will establish high availability, self-service developer tooling, and automated guardrails at scale.

This position is an individual contributor role reporting to the Director, Identity and Access Management.

Responsibility

  • Build and manage the underlying infrastructure, monitoring, telemetry, and compute environments to relieve downstream security teams of infrastructure overhead
  • Lead engineering and IaC strategy for Microsoft Sentinel, including ingestion pipelines, workspace governance, detection frameworks, and cost optimization
  • Develop reusable, hardened Terraform and Bicep/ARM modules deployed via automated CI/CD pipelines with integrated policy-as-code gates
  • Architect cross-functional orchestration workflows connecting ITSM, messaging channels, and SIEM/SOAR platforms to streamline evidence collection and incident remediation
  • Stand up automated, on-demand security sandboxes to support offensive security exercises and adversary simulation testing
  • Establish infrastructure and monitoring capabilities to support dynamic safety validation and testing of AI-driven tools prior to production rollout
  • Contribute to an internal developer portal offering visibility into vulnerability metrics, automated fix workflows, and guardrails
  • Streamline compliance reporting by automating evidence gathering against regulatory benchmarks and industry security frameworks
  • Mentor engineers across distributed teams, guide technical roadmap decisions, and champion operational excellence across the organization

Job Designation



Hybrid: Employee divides their time between in-office and remote work. Access to an office location is required. (Frequency: Minimum 2 days per week; may vary by team but will be weekly in-office expectation)

Positions at Docusign are assigned a job designation of either In Office, Hybrid or Remote and are specific to the role/job. Preferred job designations are not guaranteed when changing positions within Docusign. Docusign reserves the right to change a position's job designation depending on business needs and as permitted by local law.


What you bring



Basic

  • 12+ years of experience in SRE, cloud infrastructure, platform engineering, or security engineering with a Bachelor’s degree or 8+ years of experience with a Master's degree
  • 3+ years of experience leading a production platform as a senior or lead engineer
  • Experience with Microsoft Sentinel and Azure Monitor/Log Analytics (workspace topology, connectors, KQL, automation rules, and playbooks)
  • Experience with Terraform (custom modules, state architecture, multi-environment design)
  • Experience building and managing automated release pipelines using Azure DevOps Pipelines, GitHub Actions, or similar platforms
  • Experience with Python development
  • Experience defining SLOs/SLIs, error budget management, observability strategies, incident response rotation design, and blameless postmortems
  • Experience with technical writing and aligning stakeholders across Security, DevOps, and Product engineering

Preferred

  • Experience extending security platform patterns to AWS or GCP environments
  • Familiarity with OPA/Rego, Azure Policy, or static analysis tools like Checkov
  • Prior experience automating compliance controls for SOC 2, ISO 27001, or FedRAMP benchmarks
  • Microsoft SC-200, AZ-500, AZ-400, or HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate
  • Familiarity with ARM or Bicep
  • Experience with C#/.NET, Kubernetes, or container runtimes

Wage Transparency



Pay for this position is based on a number of factors including geographic location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Based on applicable legislation, the below details pay ranges in the following locations:

Washington, Maryland, New Jersey and New York (including NYC metro area): $158,300.00 - $232,575.00 annual base salary

This role is also eligible for the following:

  • Bonus: Sales personnel are eligible for variable incentive pay dependent on their achievement of pre-established sales goals. Non-Sales roles are eligible for a company bonus plan, which is calculated as a percentage of eligible wages and dependent on company performance.
  • Stock: This role is eligible to receive Restricted Stock Units (RSUs).

Global benefits provide options for the following:

  • Paid Time Off: earned time off, as well as paid company holidays based on region
  • Paid Parental Leave: take up to six months off with your child after birth, adoption or foster care placement
  • Full Health Benefits Plans: options for 100% employer paid and minimum employee contribution health plans from day one of employment
  • Retirement Plans: select retirement and pension programs with potential for employer contributions
  • Learning and Development: options for coaching, online courses and education reimbursements
  • Compassionate Care Leave: paid time off following the loss of a loved one and other life-changing events

Work Authorization Notice: Please note that we do not provide visa sponsorship or immigration support for this position. Applicants must already be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time, permanent basis without the need for current or future sponsorship.


Life at Docusign



Working here

Docusign is committed to building trust and making the world more agreeable for our employees, customers and the communities in which we live and work. You can count on us to listen, be honest, and try our best to do what’s right, every day. At Docusign, everything is equal.

We each have a responsibility to ensure every team member has an equal opportunity to succeed, to be heard, to exchange ideas openly, to build lasting relationships, and to do the work of their life. Best of all, you will be able to feel deep pride in the work you do, because your contribution helps us make the world better than we found it. And for that, you’ll be loved by us, our customers, and the world in which we live.

If you experience any issues, concerns, or technical difficulties during the application process please get in touch with our Talent organization at taops@docusign.com for assistance.

title: Sr Site Reliability Engineer
description:
Our Mission

Our mission is to SAVE AND IMPROVE LIVES BY EMPOWERING HEALTHCARE CONSUMERS. Come be part of remarkable.

Overview

How you can make a difference

As a Senior Site Reliability Engineer at HealthEquity, you'll play a critical role in ensuring the platforms our members depend on remain reliable, resilient, and secure. Millions of people trust HealthEquity to manage their HSAs, FSAs, HRAs, and other benefits — and the systems behind that experience need to be available when members need them most, whether that's during open enrollment, tax season, or a routine claim submission.

You'll own operational readiness for key services, drive reliability initiatives that reduce risk and toil across teams, and serve as a technical leader whose decisions directly shape the stability and scalability of our platforms.

What you’ll be doing

  • Leading reliability improvements for critical services and influencing adjacent teams on production best practices
  • Independently driving complex reliability initiatives, including root cause resolution and long-term corrective actions
  • Designing resilient, scalable systems with appropriate failure handling, observability, and recovery strategies
  • Actively participating in architecture reviews to ensure operational scalability and service resilience
  • Owning service-level operational readiness, SLOs, and incident quality for key platforms or services
  • Strengthening operational controls while balancing delivery speed and risk
  • Applying AI to improve debugging, automation, and operational insights — while modeling effective and responsible use for others
  • Mentoring engineers and helping elevate team capability in reliability engineering practices
  • Influencing team practices and coordinating effectively during incidents and cross-functional operational events
  • Participating in on-call as needed, owning production health and SLOs, and improving reliability and MTTR across teams

What you will need to be successful

  • 8+ years of experience with complex production ownership in SRE, infrastructure engineering, or related disciplines
  • Advanced proficiency in distributed systems troubleshooting and performance tuning
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure platforms and tooling (Azure, Terraform, Kubernetes/AKS, or equivalent)
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, or equivalent)
  • Experience with observability, monitoring, and incident management tools (Dynatrace, PagerDuty, or equivalent)
  • Experience applying AI/ML tools to improve debugging, automation, or operational insights (e.g., anomaly detection, automated root cause analysis, AI-assisted coding tools)
  • Strong coding/scripting skills in Python, PowerShell, Go, Bash, or similar languages, with the ability to mentor others in software reliability best practices
  • Demonstrated ability to independently own service-level reliability decisions, incident management, and operational excellence
  • Deep expertise in cloud-native architectures, high-availability systems, and fault-tolerant design patterns
  • Experience analyzing complex systems holistically and making data-driven decisions to improve uptime and performance
  • Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field a plus, but not required

#LI-Remote

title: Aviation Regulatory Adviser/s - Australia-Pacific Partnerships for Aviation (P4A)
description:
Overview

Assignment: Aviation Regulatory Adviser/s (multiple) Counterpart: To be advised Program: Australia-Pacific Partnerships for Aviation (P4A) Location: Home-office based with in-country travel to Pacific Island countries Timeline: Expected 12-18 month contract duration commencing in December 2026, depending on agreed workplan. Deadline for applications: 11:59pm AEDT on 25 October 2026

P4A Program Background

The Australia – Pacific Partnerships for Aviation (P4A) program aims to improve the Pacific aviation sectors’ efficiency and effectiveness in organisational decision-making, governance, safety and reliability, and coordination to enable aviation to better contribute to sustainable development outcomes. It is recognised that the small populations, lack of economic diversification and geographic remoteness of the Pacific constrain its growth and international competitiveness. However, aviation’s intersection with tourism, trade, labour mobility, and access to critical services such as healthcare and education can enable Pacific growth and prosperity. P4A is a five-year Australian Government initiative implemented by DFAT and Adam Smith International.

P4A will be delivered through three key outcome areas, including (but not limited to):

  1. A stronger enabling environment, including improved governance, regulations, policies, and plans that strengthen the Pacific aviation sector and reform unsustainable practices.

  2. Improved Safety, Quality and Reliability through strengthened technical capability and more common approaches that improve aviation operations' safety, quality, and reliability.

  3. Greater coordination, cooperation, and connectivity are needed to maintain connectivity between Pacific Island countries and strengthen regional and bilateral coordination and cooperation in regulatory and operational areas.

P4A will also mainstream cross-cutting sectors to ensure outcomes strengthen child protection and safeguarding, climate change resilience and adaptation, support locally led leadership and improve Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) outcomes.

Assignment Background

The P4A program has offered technical expertise to Pacific partners to assist development of their national State Safety Programme (SSP) and National Aviation Safety Plan (NASP).

The SSP is an integrated set of regulations and activities aimed at improving safety outcomes at national levels and is supported by the NASP which will outline safety priorities, objectives and initiatives related to aviation safety oversight. The NASP will detail commitments and plans to improve organisational capabilities related to aviation safety oversight, reduce aviation operational safety risks and detail for the future intended focus areas, goals and initiatives complementing the SSP and supporting a desired level of safety performance.

Development and implementation of the SSP and NASP are essential to ensuring that States can achieve internationally accepted standards of safety oversight and will enable government to meet its obligations as a member State of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).

Each ICAO State is required to establish a State Safety Programme and National Aviation Safety Plan. Both are essential to ensuring State obligations as an ICAO member State.

P4A support will be led by Regulatory Advisers (Adviser) who will support one or more Pacific counterpart to develop the national SSP and NASP. Key tasks will include coordination with aviation actors across the sector to ensure engagement with the SSP/NASP process, capacity uplift and training, and liaison with other stakeholders to improve national aviation safety oversight capability. The Adviser will work closely with relevant officials and counterparts to support the development of a coordinated State Safety Programme and National Aviation Safety Plan.

Objective

The objective of this assignment is for an Adviser/s to assist Pacific counterparts with the development of national State Safety Programme (SSP) and National Aviation Safety Plan (NASP).

Scope of Work

  • Develop the national SSP and NASP in close collaboration with the relevant regulatory authority and other aviation operators / service providers, taking into account the size of the national aviation sector and its capacity constraints, while ensuring compliance.

  • Consider how a realistic and deliverable SSP/NASP can be appropriately scaled for a small, capacity-constrained aviation system, while ensuring an acceptable degree of compliance.

  • Provide technical advisory to counterparts / other relevant aviation actors.

  • Engage collaboratively and constructively with counterparts and regional organisations, and undertake all work in a collaborative and constructive manner which supports skills transfer and the professional development of counterparts.

  • Ensure that the SSP/NASP considers the appropriate role of relevant regional organisations and the particularities of the national aviation context.

  • Recommend training and capacity-building initiatives in response to needs/gaps identified as part of the SSP/NASP process. This is expected to include Safety Management Systems (SMS) awareness training.

  • Design and deliver training and capacity-building initiatives to boost national compliance with Annex 19 and other relevant ICAO standards, with the aim of ensuring that there are sustainable improvements in capacity in Pacific partners' aviation system.

  • Identify and undertake measures to ensure national ownership of the SSP and NASP, and the long-term sustainability of any capacity-building initiatives.

  • Ensure that the SSP and NASP takes into account regional context and challenges

  • If required, facilitate the establishment of relevant intra-sector committees, working groups or taskforces.

  • Consider improvements in collection, utilisation and sharing of safety related data.

  • Undertake other duties in support of P4A initiatives, as directed.

Deliverables and Level of Effort

Deliverables

  • Capacity-Development Approach: report proposing approach to capacity-building / professional development (timing to be agreed)

  • State Safety Programme (draft and final reports)

  • National Aviation Safety Plan (draft and final reports)

  • Completion Report including (i) work / activities undertaken during the assignment; (ii) approach taken to support development of partner capacity and professional development; (iii) key achievements, learnings and recommendations arising from the SSP and NASP.

  • Brief Monthly reports outlining key activities undertaken during the reporting period, and any emerging or current issues.

A detailed Schedule of Deliverables and Workplan will be agreed during the contract negotiation period, and will include expected in-country travel, home-office inputs and deliverables.

Level of Effort

This assignment is expected to commence in December 2026, for an estimated duration of 12-18 months depending on agreed workplan. An approximate LOE of 0.5FTE – 0.75FTE is anticipated, depending on the agreed workplan. The assignments are expected to be delivered through a combination of in-country inputs and home-office inputs.

Qualifications and Experience

  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in aviation, safety management or a related field, or equivalent industry or regulatory experience.

  • A minimum of 10 years’ significant experience in aviation safety oversight, safety management or regulatory work, including with or alongside a civil aviation authority.

  • Demonstrated experience developing or implementing a State Safety Programme and/or National Aviation Safety Plan in line with ICAO Annex 19 and associated guidance material.

  • Sound working knowledge of ICAO Standards and Recommended Practices (SARPs), Safety Management Systems (SMS) and State safety oversight obligations.

  • Experience scaling regulatory frameworks so they are realistic for small, capacity-constrained aviation systems while maintaining an acceptable level of compliance.

  • Demonstrated ability to design and deliver training and capacity-building initiatives, including SMS awareness training.

  • Experience working in Pacific Island countries, or a similar operating environment, and knowledge of their aviation sector.

  • Excellent report-writing skills, with a track record of producing high-quality technical and strategic documents.

Desirable Qualifications and Experience

  • Experience working collaboratively in a development partner context.

  • Familiarity with regional aviation bodies (e.g. the Pacific Aviation Safety Office) and regional safety oversight arrangements.

  • Experience with ICAO audit processes, such as the Universal Safety Oversight Audit Programme (USOAP), and preparing States for them.

  • Experience improving the collection, analysis and sharing of safety data.

  • Experience establishing and facilitating multi-stakeholder committees, working groups or taskforces.

  • Experience applying Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) principles, and in stakeholder and community engagement.

  • Experience working with multicultural and multidisciplinary teams.

  • Strong mentoring and capacity-building skills, with a focus on skills transfer and local ownership.

How to apply

For all Applicants:

Please submit a CV and cover letter via our online platform.

Your cover letter should detail your expertise, experience, and alignment with the requirements of the P4A program. The cover letter should also outline your daily (8 hour) rate in AUD.

Organisations may nominate an individual consultant. The contracting arrangements should be clear in the accompanying cover letter.

Responses will be evaluated based on demonstrated expertise, relevant experience and the requirements of P4A program.

Applications must be submitted by 11:59pm AEDT on 25 October 2026.

title: Demand Planning Lead (Consumer Electronics) - CN
description:
📱 About Mous

We are Mous. (Pronounced mouse, not moose.) People deserve tech and lifestyle products that are fit for purpose, perform as promised and empower them to be their best. That's why we're building the go-to brand focused squarely on delivering just that. We have consistently built our in-house expertise and spent millions in research and development on our relentless pursuit to make the best products possible.

Over the past 10 years, we have focused on pushing the performance of products
and creating engaging content to guide millions of customers to high-quality Mous products rather than making cheap products for Amazons algorithm. All with the aspiration that we can raise the standards of the industry and provide people with better products.

We're creating products that empower people to be their best, whether they're on a wild adventure or commuting through the city. No matter what your everyday life looks like you can trust our products to remove frustrations, expand your experiences and help you to live without limits.



👨‍💻 About the Role

As Demand Planning Lead, you’ll own the Device Accessories category plan end to end — demand, supply and inventory health across cases, screen protectors, accessories and wireless chargers — and represent the category to the Senior Leadership Team. It’s Mous’s largest category by SKU count and stock value, and the one most exposed to device launch timing: every major iPhone, Pixel and Samsung launch is a live forecasting and ordering decision, made before any sales history exists.

Alongside the forecast, you’ll own the launch forecast and initial order quantity for each device launch, initial and weekly allocation across regions and channels (D2C web, Amazon, retail and Google), re-ordering for existing SKUs, and stock transfers across our hubs and warehouses. You’ll own the category’s inventory health, working with Commercial on pricing and discounting to clear excess and obsolete stock, and the category KPIs — Availability, Forecast Accuracy and E&O. It’s a genuinely cross-functional seat, working with Commercial, Marketplaces, Pricing, Product, Retail, Production, Procurement, Logistics, Data and the Senior Leadership Team across the UK, Pakistan and China. You’ll report to the S&OP Manager in China.

Please note that this role will be situated at our office in Dongguan, China, working on-site from Monday-Friday. The normal working hours will be 9am - 6:30pm CST.

👋 About You

You’re a good fit if you have experience in demand planning, category planning or S&OP for a fast-moving, high-SKU category, and you’ve owned a monthly cycle end to end rather than supported someone else’s. You’ve built launch forecasts with no sales history — downside, mid and upside — and set the order behind them. You’re fluent in Excel across large datasets (1,000+ SKUs, multiple warehouses and channels), you understand what MOQs, lead times, capacity and freight mode actually do to a plan, and you can put a number on the trade-off between availability and E&O — in units, cash and margin — in a way a senior audience will act on.

You hold a data-backed position when Commercial or leadership push for a more optimistic number, and you stay calm when launch week puts many live decisions on the table at once. You make the call and stand behind it, you’re organised and disciplined with files and versions, and you’re comfortable coaching someone who knows the work but needs support to make the call. You’ll be working across three countries and several stakeholder groups, so cultural awareness and collaboration matter here.

🔑Key Responsibilities:

  • New product demand planning — Own the forecast for launches tied to the device calendar (iPhone, Google Pixel, Samsung S-series and foldables). Build the initial forecast with explicit assumptions, set the initial order quantity (IOQ), and present downside / mid / upside scenarios with the cash exposure attached to each, taken through sign-off with Product, Commercial and the Senior Leadership Team.

  • Launch allocation and replenishment — Own the initial launch allocation, linked to production planning, then weekly allocation top-ups and Amazon restocks as the launch curve develops.

  • Launch performance tracking — Track performance by range, colour and channel, and turn it into re-order or no-re-order decisions.

  • Existing SKU forecasting — Own the monthly forecast update for existing SKUs, the quarterly correction against actuals, and the accessories and wireless charger forecast.

  • Re-ordering — Own re-ordering for existing SKUs, checked against supplier MOQs and taken through the order approval process.

  • Inventory health — Run the weekly overstock check and root cause analysis, and partner with Commercial on pricing and discounting reviews to clear excess and obsolete stock.

  • Stock movements — Own weekly allocations, hub-to-warehouse and Amazon transfers, and inter-warehouse transfers.

  • Retail planning — Coordinate retail NPD forecasts and IOQs, retail allocations and re-orders, and web vs. retail stock priority rules.

  • Category KPIs and S&OP — Own Availability, Forecast Accuracy (WAPE / bias) and E&O, and embed the monthly S&OP cycle for the category.

  • SKU portfolio productivity — Simplify the range, remove low-productivity lines and reduce low-MOQ complexity.

  • Cross-functional coordination — Work across Commercial, Marketplaces, Pricing, Product, Retail, Production, Procurement, Logistics, Data and the Senior Leadership Team.

  • Line management — Line manage, coach and develop one Demand Planner.

✔️How will success be measured?

  • Launch forecasts and IOQ recommendations leadership can sign off quickly, because the downside, mid and upside cases and the cash at risk are laid out clearly.

  • Availability protected through launch windows, without over-ordering into the drop-off that follows the launch spike.

  • Excess and obsolete stock trending down, with previous-generation ranges run down before the next device lands.

  • Forecast accuracy and bias improving for both launch and mature SKUs, with misses understood through root cause review rather than explained away.

  • A monthly S&OP cycle that runs to a reliable cadence and consistently produces decisions, not just discussion.

  • Allocations and transfers that put stock in the right region and channel first time, based on stock and in-transit data that has been checked.

  • A Demand Planner growing in confidence and making more of the calls independently.

🤓Skills requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree (Business, Economics, Supply Chain or similar).

  • 5+ years in demand planning, category planning or S&OP for a fast-moving, high-SKU category, including proven ownership of a monthly cycle end to end.

  • New product launch forecasting tied to an external launch date — building scenario-based (downside / mid / upside) initial forecasts and IOQs before any sales history exists.

  • Advanced Excel capability — comfortable handling large datasets (1,000+ SKUs, multiple warehouses and channels), building models, and turning data into clear insight.

  • Able to quantify the trade-off between availability and E&O — in units, cash and margin (CM2 / CM3) — and present it to senior stakeholders for a decision.

  • Working understanding of production and supply constraints (MOQ, lead times, capacity, air vs. sea freight) and warehouse / 3PL / Amazon FBA stock flows.

  • Experience allocating and transferring stock across regions and channels (D2C web, Amazon, retail partners).

  • Fluent written and spoken English and Chinese — able to run meetings in English, handle English reporting, and work directly with UK HQ

🎉 Our Offer

We work fully on-site in our custom Dongguan office so that we can retain the collaborative and vibrant Mous culture that people love.

Why work at Mous?

  • Long-Term Rewards: One month of paid leave after 5 years’ service.

  • Competitive Pay: A strong starting salary aligned with your experience and impact.

  • Dynamic Culture: A collaborative, high-performance, data-driven environment where innovation thrives.

  • Growth & Development: Opportunities to learn, stretch, and grow through new challenges.

  • Professional Development: Training budget plus regular Mousterclasses to share expertise across teams.

  • Charlie HR Perks: Access to exclusive perks and discounts via Charlie HR.

  • Global Collaboration: Seamless remote collaboration with international teams, including weekly all-hands and virtual socials.

🐭Our Values

Get Results – We take accountability, prioritise impact, and push standards higher.
Work Together – We collaborate openly, challenge constructively, and learn from each other.
Enjoy the Ride – We stay agile, embrace change, and enjoy building something special together.

🌈Our Commitment

Mous is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate individuality and are committed to building a diverse team with a wide range of experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds.

title: Delivery Manager
description:
Salary: $100 – $150 per hour

Delivery Manager

Atlas Digital | Canberra

Atlas Digital works with government and private sector clients to plan and deliver technology and digital projects. We’re looking for a Delivery Manager to join our Canberra team.

We’re looking for someone who has managed delivery before, is comfortable working directly with clients and can take responsibility for getting things done. You’ll work alongside our senior delivery and technical people, but you’ll need the experience and judgement to manage your own projects and workstreams.

This could suit someone working at a Big Four firm or another professional services business who is looking for more ownership in a smaller team. That background would be welcome, but it’s not essential.

About the role

You’ll work with clients and technical teams to turn priorities into a clear plan and manage the work through to completion. This includes:

  • Managing project scope, delivery plans, budgets and priorities.

  • Coordinating work across technical teams, business stakeholders and delivery partners.

  • Building strong client relationships and keeping people informed about progress, decisions and issues.

  • Managing risks and dependencies, resolving problems and having the difficult conversations when needed.

  • Making sure meetings lead to decisions, actions are followed through and the team can get on with the work.

We need someone who gets involved and helps resolve problems, rather than just tracking and reporting on them.

What we’re looking for

You’ll have experience managing technology or digital projects, with examples of work you’ve taken responsibility for and delivered. Your current title matters less than the responsibility you’ve held.

You’ll need to be organised, communicate clearly and be comfortable working with both technical teams and senior client stakeholders. You should be able to challenge an unrealistic deadline, work through competing priorities and recognise when an issue needs to be escalated.

Experience with government clients and Agile delivery would be useful. You don’t need to be a technical specialist, but you do need to understand enough about technology delivery to ask the right questions and work effectively with the team.

You must be based in Canberra. You must be able to obtain a baseline security clearance.

Why Atlas Digital?

You’ll be part of a smaller team, working directly with our senior delivery and technical people. You’ll have a say in how we approach the work, build relationships with clients and stay involved as projects move from planning into delivery.

There’s room to broaden your experience and take on more responsibility, with support from people who are involved in the work alongside you.

We’re open to permanent or contract arrangements, with salary or rates agreed based on your experience.

title: Senior Solution Architect
description:
Solution Architect - Enterprise Integration & Data (Permanent)


Digital Strategy & Architecture | Hamilton, New Zealand

The Client


Our client is a well-established New Zealand infrastructure business with a large customer base and a growing programme of partner-delivered technology work. With new leadership and a changing operating environment, they’re strengthening their architecture practice so the technology landscape stays coherent while delivery teams and integrators move quickly.

The Opportunity


This is architecture with real accountability. It isn’t a documentation role, and it isn’t a build role. It suits a solution architect who is comfortable influencing without authority. That means challenging a systems integrator’s design with evidence, keeping the conversation constructive, and knowing when enough analysis has been done to proceed.

You’ll be the architectural thread from discovery through delivery on a mix of internally and externally delivered work, covering integration, data, security and operability. You’ll work inside an established practice with clear principles, an Architecture Review Board and a Technical Design Authority, so you won’t be inventing governance from scratch, but you will help shape it as it matures. Industry experience helps. Curiosity and judgement matter more.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Engaging at discovery to understand the business problem, constraints and outcomes, then shaping pragmatic end-to-end solutions.
  • Evaluating options and making trade-offs, risks and consequences clear to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Writing Architecture Decision Records and taking significant decisions and exceptions to the Architecture Review Board and Technical Design Authority.
  • Reviewing and challenging solution architecture produced by systems integrators and vendors, and spotting gaps against Statements of Work.
  • Staying engaged through implementation to protect architectural intent, while respecting Technical Leads’ ownership of detailed design.
  • Shaping non-functional requirements, including resilience, performance, recoverability, observability and supportability.
  • Producing clear solution designs and diagrams, and contributing reusable patterns back to the wider practice.
  • Keeping across emerging technology, including AI, and what it means for the architecture.

What You’ll Bring

  • Experience as a Solution Architect or comparable technical architect, designing end-to-end solutions from discovery through delivery - Telco Experience would be advantageous
  • Strong practical experience across integration, APIs, event-driven architecture, data architecture and data flows.
  • Experience shaping non-functional requirements and weighing options, trade-offs and dependencies.
  • Confidence working with Product Owners, Business Analysts, Technical Leads and delivery teams, with clear documentation and visualisation skills.
  • Experience with ADRs and architecture governance, and with reviewing designs from integrators or vendors, is strongly regarded.
  • Exposure to ServiceNow, Dynamics 365, ESRI ArcGIS and/or AWS or comparable cloud platforms is a plus.
  • Relevant tertiary qualification or equivalent experience; architecture, cloud or integration certifications are a plus.
  • Based in, or able to work from, Hamilton.

Why Apply

  • Genuine architectural influence on a complex, live technology landscape, not a paper-pushing role.
  • An established practice with clear principles, patterns and proportionate governance, and room to shape how it evolves.
  • A business with new leadership and a strong appetite to grow, with real support for learning a new domain.

How to Apply


For a confidential discussion about this role, contact Adam Roi at Walkersmith or apply with confidence via Seek. We look forward to hearing from you.

What you bring

Life at Docusign

title: Inventory Specialist
description:
The Inventory Specialist is responsible for supporting warehouse operations through the receiving, storage, tracking, staging, and distribution of materials and equipment. This role ensures inventory accuracy, supports project fulfillment requirements, maintains serialized asset tracking, and assists in establishing and maintaining efficient warehouse operations. The Inventory Specialist will work closely with Procurement, Project Management, Engineering, Logistics, and Operations teams to ensure equipment availability and inventory integrity.


Key Responsibilities


Inventory Management & Tracking

  • Receive incoming materials and equipment and verify accuracy against purchase orders, packing slips, and shipping documentation.
  • Inspect incoming shipments for damage, shortages, or discrepancies and report issues as necessary.
  • Properly stage, organize, and store materials in designated warehouse locations.
  • Maintain accurate inventory counts using inventory management software and manual tracking processes.
  • Monitor stock levels and communicate shortages or replenishment needs to management.
  • Conduct routine cycle counts and assist with full physical inventory audits.
  • Reconcile inventory variances and investigate root causes of discrepancies.
  • Process inventory transactions including receipts, transfers, adjustments, returns, and shipments within the company's ERP system.
  • Maintain warehouse bin locations, shelving assignments, and inventory storage layouts.
  • Ensure all inventory items are properly identified, labeled, and traceable.
  • Maintain serialized asset tracking and chain-of-custody records for equipment and materials.
  • Track product movements and inventory status to ensure real-time accuracy.


Project Fulfillment & Equipment Staging

  • Pick, pack, and stage materials and equipment for project deployments.
  • Verify material readiness and completeness prior to shipment.
  • Coordinate project material requirements with Project Managers, Procurement, Engineering, and Operations teams.
  • Ensure project materials are available according to project schedules and deployment requirements.
  • Prepare shipment documentation and coordinate outbound shipments with carriers and logistics providers.
  • Support emergency or expedited material requests to prevent project delays.


Safety & Compliance

  • Follow all company safety policies and OSHA regulations.
  • Utilize proper material handling practices to prevent injury or equipment damage.
  • Ensure inventory storage practices comply with safety and operational requirements.
  • Maintain an audit-ready warehouse environment.


General Operations

  • Communicate effectively with internal departments regarding inventory availability and material status.
  • Assist with logistics, material movement, and operational support activities as required.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives related to inventory control and warehouse operations.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned.

description:
As a Lead Dye Operator at Shawmut, you will provide training and guidance to a team of fellow operators and play a crucial role in ensuring the smooth and efficient operation of our production process. Your attention to detail and leadership skills will be essential as you review the quality of your team's output and align staffing needs to meet production targets. Working closely with the production team, you will prioritize workload, make necessary adjustments to achieve the perfect color and quality, and ensure adherence to engineering requirements during manufacturing. Your ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment, working both efficiently and effectively, will be instrumental to your success in this role.


Responsibilities:

  • Lead a team of dye operators, overseeing their work and ensuring the quality of output meets company standards.
  • Operate dye machines to color fabrics according to specifications, ensuring correct dye formulas and processes are followed.
  • Monitor and facilitate product development trials throughout the facility.
  • Maintain accurate records of dye formulas and production logs, ensuring all documentation is completed correctly and on time.
  • Maintain a safe and clean work environment, following all safety protocols and procedures.
  • Collaborate with planning, production (including dyeing and finishing), laboratory, customer service, and shipping departments to ensure seamless communication of material and product development information.

title: Independent External Consultant
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration


Project Context and Scope

As a country of origin, transit and destination, Nigeria faces complex border-management challenges linked to high mobility and evolving migration dynamics, including risks related to irregular migration, trafficking in persons, smuggling and other forms of transnational organized crime. To address these challenges, the Federal Government of Nigeria, with technical support from the International Organization for Migration (IOM), adopted the Migration Information and Data Analysis System (MIDAS) as the country’s Border Management Information System (BMIS). Following disruption to synchronization between Points of Entry (PoEs) and the central server at Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) Headquarters, the project was designed to restore and strengthen data integration, synchronization and management, while improving forensic document examination capacity.

The project, “Strengthening the Capacity of Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) in Border Security and Management,” runs from October 2024 to September 2026, with a total budget of USD 600,000, and is generously funded by the Government of Switzerland through the Swiss State Secretariat for Migration (SEM). The intervention is implemented by IOM Nigeria in partnership with NIS and other key national stakeholders. Direct beneficiaries include NIS and the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, while indirect beneficiaries are migrants and travellers crossing Nigeria’s international borders. The project covers NIS Headquarters and three international airports: Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport (NAIA), Abuja; Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Lagos; and Port Harcourt International Airport (PHIA), Rivers State.

The project objective is to enhance NIS institutional capacity through support for improved MIDAS data integration and synchronisation as well as enhance knowledge on forensic document examinations for border officials at three (3) targeted PoEs to facilitate migration while combating transnational organized crimes. The project has two outcomes:

  • Outcome 1: Enhanced institutional capacity of NIS through improved MIDAS data management, equipment and border infrastructure support.

  • Output 1.1: Improved MIDAS data integration and synchronization through strengthening border infrastructure at three selected air borders in Nigeria, namely Abuja, Port Harcourt, and Lagos international airports.

  • Output 1.2: Enhanced knowledge and understanding of migration data by NIS officials at these three international airports to guide operational and policy decision-making processes.

  • Outcome 2: Enhanced capacities of NIS officials in forensic document examination processes at targeted PoEs and NIS Headquarters.

  • Output 2.1 NIS officials have the technical tools and operational capacity to conduct forensic document examination at 3 target Points of Entry (PoE).

Key activities include needs assessments; procurement, deployment and installation of hardware, power, networking, software, firewalls and VPN-related infrastructure; MIDAS Performance Monitoring Assessments; migration data-management training; a study visit and training-of-trainers process; development of a forensic document examination curriculum; peer-to-peer step-down training; review of standard operating procedures; and provision of forensic document examination devices. Evaluation scope

3.1 Temporal scope

The evaluation will cover the full 24-month implementation period and all project components from 1 October 2024 to 30 September 2026.

3.2 Geographic scope

NIS Headquarters, Abuja

Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport (NAIA), Abuja

Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Lagos

Port Harcourt International Airport (PHIA), Rivers State.

3.3 Substantive scope

The evaluation will cover the project’s full results chain and all major intervention components, including MIDAS data integration and synchronization, migration data-management capacity-building, and forensic document examination support. It will also examine project design and implementation, partnership and coordination arrangements, monitoring and risk management, and prospects for institutional and operational sustainability.

title: Chief, United Nations (UN) Efficiency Unit (P)
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process.

For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates:

  1. Internal candidates
  2. External female candidates
  3. Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories: Bahamas, Barbados, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu

Second tier candidates include:
All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM.

Organizational Context and Scope

Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Director General for Management and Reform and direct supervision of the Director, Global Shared Services, and in close coordination with relevant Units at Headquarters (HQ), the Global Shared Services Centre and International Organization for Migration (IOM) Offices worldwide, the Chief, United Nations (UN) Efficiency Unit will be responsible and accountable for providing strategic leadership, technical guidance and managerial support to advance efficiency, effectiveness and value for money across IOM’s operations. The Chief, UN Efficiency Unit will lead the Unit’s efforts to identify and promote cross-cutting efficiencies, including through inter-agency collaboration applying the enabling functions of mutual recognition statement, pricing and costing principles and client satisfaction principles.

  1. Lead the UN Efficiency Unit and identify organizational goals and targets to ensure adequate support is provided to achieve results through developing and implementing an action plan based on quality data collection and analysis.
  2. Provide strategic guidance and support the participation of IOM on UN interagency efficiency platforms with the aim of achieving efficiency gains and facilitating joint programming.
  3. Lead oversight and compliance of IOM’s implementation of UN Efficiency initiatives by identifying best practices, lessons learned, opportunities for improvement and reporting on progress.
  4. Represent IOM at UN interagency platforms and ensure consistent, high-quality engagement in system-wide efficiency initiatives.
  5. Advise and coordinate IOM’s engagement at the UN High-level Committee Coordination and facilitate operationalization of decisions by IOM Offices.
  6. Respond to internal and external audits and assessments relating to entity-level UN Efficiency and IOM engagement.
  7. Lead the development of internal reports and visibility materials on efficiency gains, and ensure timely submission to IOM leadership and external bodies.
  8. Coordinate with peers from other UN entities to ensure efficient and complementary approaches and build synergies, and coordinate UN interagency policy, guidance and training material on UN Efficiency initiatives.
  9. Coordinate with IOM business and policy owners to achieve the objectives set in agreed UN efficiency initiatives; and provide analysis, interpretation, and guidance on related-policy matters, propose amendments of administrative instructions and alignment of internal systems to improve efficiency, simplification, or to meet audit recommendations.
  10. Monitor and report regularly to Senior Management on the progress of all efficiency initiatives and gains.
  11. Identify risks and challenges associated with efficiency initiatives and propose mitigation strategies to ensure smooth implementation.
  12. Identify knowledge gaps and build adequate capacity in IOM to strengthen institutional knowledge and implementation capacity across IOM including Operations Management Team (OMT) and United Nations Country Team (UNCT) representation, engagement and participation by IOM staff and strategic positioning of IOM on interagency collaborations focused on achieving efficiencies.
  13. Develop IOM internal Annual Workplans and Budgets guiding the work on efficiency initiatives drawing from the HLCM and other UN Efficiency-related agendas.
  14. Support the Global Shared Services Centre (GSSC) in identifying and implementing measures to optimize services and improve efficiency.
  15. Act as secretariat for the GSSC Board.
  16. Undertake visits to Regional, Country Offices and GSSC to review and assess engagement, provide guidance on specific substantive implementation issues, and represent the UN Efficiency Unit/Office at various relevant workshops and meetings.
  17. Perform other duties as may be assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Master's degree in Business Administration, Management, Economics, Finance, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with ten years of relevant professional experience; or,
  • University degree in the above fields with twelve years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Significant experience in general management as well as resources management;
  • Significant experience in diplomacy including in liaising with UN partners;
  • Experience in writing policy and/or guidelines;
  • Operations Management Team (OMT) experience; and,
  • Experience on Budget and Operations Support (BOS), Community-Based Organization (CBO) and/or Country Programme/Project (CP) would be a distinct advantage.

Skills

  • Excellent communications skills, both oral and written;
  • Demonstrated liaison and negotiation skills;
  • In depth knowledge of resources management;
  • Knowledge of UN Reform and Efficiency Agenda; and,
  • Effective resources management skills, sound knowledge of financial and business administration and of the principles and practices of management.

Languages

IOM’s official languages are English, French and Spanish. All staff members are required to be fluent in one of the three languages.

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

A working knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian and Spanish) is
desirable.

title: Community Health Representative
description:
Reporting to the Supervisor, Health Programs or the Nurse Manager, Iqaluit Public Health, with the support of community, regional, and territorial public and population health staff, the Community Health Representative provides evidence-based and culturally informed health promotion and behaviour change information and education to enhance the health and wellbeing of Nunavummiut. The Commnity Health Representative helps to bridge the health centre and the community, enhancing trust and understanding, leading the integration of IQ into public health work in communities, and collaborating in the development and implementation of culturally informed resources and research.

The scope of the Community Health Representative is to provide evidence-based health promotion education information in the communities, as well as to assist with ensuring that health services and resources offered in communities are culturally informed. The Community Health Representative is a leader in sharing health promotion information which is aligned with Territorial Public Health priorities and is also a liaison between the Department of Health and community members and organizations and strengthens early and continuous connections to formal health care, including by helping to increase community member confidence in the Department of Health. The Community Health Representative incorporates Inuit knowledge, values, culture, language, and IQ principles in their work; participates and contributes to community, regional, territorial and national events, research, programs and initiatives; and works with public and population health staff, health centre teams, and community groups and non-profit organizations to promote health, build capacity and develop communities, ultimately improving health of Nunavummiut.

The knowledge, skills, and abilities required for this job are usually obtained through a high school diploma or equivalent and 1 year experience working in a northern community.

A valid driver’s license, First Aid/BCLS and CHR training, the ability to speak, read, and write Inuktut, and education or experience in a health or education related field are assets.

This is a Highly Sensitive Position and a satisfactory Criminal Record Check, along with a clear Vulnerable Sector Check is required.

The Official Languages of Nunavut are Inuktut, English and French. Applicants may submit their resume in any of the official languages of Nunavut. Fluency in more than one of Nunavut’s official languages would be considered an asset. Knowledge of Inuit communities, culture, land,Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit, Inuktut and experience working in a northern cross-cultural environment are also considered assets.

Acceptable combinations of education and experience may be considered for this position. We encourage you to apply if you have equivalent years of education and/or experience equal to the education and experience requirements listed above.

  • The Government of Nunavut is committed to creating a representative workforce; therefore, priority will be given to Nunavut Inuit who self-identify as being enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement in accordance with the Priority Hiring Policy.
  • Government of Nunavut employees serving a probationary period must obtain and provide written authorization from the deputy head of their employing department. The authorization from the deputy head must accompany your application for your application to be considered.
  • Possession of a criminal record may not disqualify candidates from being considered. An assessment of the criminal record will be measured against the scope and duties of the position. This is only a requirement for positions that require a satisfactory criminal record or vulnerable sector check.
  • Applicants may submit their resume in any of the Official Languages of Nunavut.
  • Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.
  • The onus is on candidates in receipt of foreign post-secondary education credentials to have their foreign credentials assessed through a recognized Canadian education institution. Failure to do so may result in the rejection of their application.

title: Business Banker- Platteville
description:

As a Business Banker, you will be tasked with developing, growing, and maintaining business and agricultural lending relationships. This position is responsible for developing new commercial business/agricultural relationships as well as strengthening and expanding our existing lending relationships ensuring bank risk is mitigated and loan quality meets or exceeds standards.

A locally-owned community bank that traces our Boscobel beginnings to 1871, we believe that if our time is spent aiding our customers, then it has been well spent. We provide value to our customers through exceptional individualized service that exceeds their expectations. And, we strengthen the communities we serve through contributions of time, talent, and financial resources.

We recognize that our success is based on the quality and dedication of our team members. That's why we continually invest in their growth through training and education. We create an enjoyable work environment that empowers our team members and fosters collaboration through open, honest, and sincere communications. Our employees also earn company stock after meeting the eligibility criteria, making us an employee-owned bank.

  • Bachelor's Degree in Business, Finance, Accounting or Economics or equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Three to five years of commercial/agricultural lending experience preferred or sales/relationship building experience required.

WORK SCHEDULE

This is a full-time position working primarily Monday through Friday at our Platteville, WI location.

title: Fitness Trainer
description:
Help people achieve their health and fitness goals in a supportive, community-focused environment.

TLC Health Clubs is seeking a passionate and motivated Fitness Trainer to join our team in Wallington on a part-time basis. If you're passionate about health and wellbeing, enjoy building strong relationships with members, and thrive in a customer-focused environment, we'd love to hear from you. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys a mix of gym floor engagement, personal training, member support, and creating exceptional fitness experiences.

About the Role

As a Fitness Trainer, you'll be a visible and approachable presence on the gym floor, supporting members to safely and effectively achieve their fitness goals. You'll provide exercise guidance, conduct personal training sessions, promote club programs, and deliver outstanding customer service while maintaining a welcoming and professional club environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide supervision, guidance, motivation, and support to members on the gym floor
  • Design and deliver safe, personalised fitness and training programs

title: Lead Analyst, Payment Abuse Operations'
description:
Team Overview

LinkedIn's Trust Operations team is maturing its Payment Abuse function, and we're looking for a Lead Analyst to help take it to the next level. You will lead complex investigations, raise the standard for how we detect and remediate payment fraud, and turn ad hoc practices into scalable controls, workflows, and monitoring. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports, on a global team, with significant cross-functional influence and ownership of outcomes.

The ideal candidate combines deep payments-risk expertise, strong analytical capabilities, and operational leadership to navigate complex business challenges. This individual will lead investigations and strategic initiatives, identify emerging risks and control gaps, influence stakeholders, and serve as a subject matter expert within the Payment Abuse organization.

At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. The work location of this role is hybrid, meaning it will be performed both from home and from a LinkedIn office on select days, as determined by the business needs of the team.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead complex payment fraud and abuse investigations end to end: find root causes and control gaps, and drive remediation to closure.

  • Monitor fraud and chargeback performance against payment network and regulatory threshold, investigate the drivers, and lead remediation when performance trends toward a threshold.

  • Use SQL and data analysis to surface emerging fraud trends, define risk metrics and KPIs, and turn findings into operational and product improvements.

  • Design and strengthen fraud controls, monitoring frameworks, and tooling, including finding opportunities for automation and ML-assisted detection.

  • Strengthen operational rigor by standardizing and documenting SOPs, investigation playbooks, and escalation criteria across the team.

  • Partner with our vendor partner on payments workflows by setting escalation criteria, defining quality signals, and making sure SOPs are applied consistently.

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Payments, Operations, and external payment partners to resolve complex payment-risk challenges.

  • Serve as the escalation point for high-risk cases, and mentor analysts as the team's subject matter expert.

  • Own initiatives from problem identification through implementation and impact measurement, communicating effectively and operating effectively in ambiguous environments.

  • Contribute to operational strategy, regional coverage planning, and the long-term Payment Abuse roadmap.

Basic Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in payment fraud, payment abuse, payments risk, or a related field, including experience leading complex fraud, chargeback, or dispute investigations.

  • 3+ years of experience with payment processors, acquirers, card-network rules, fraud-monitoring programs, chargeback programs, or scheme-compliance and remediation initiatives (VAMP, Mastercard, Auspaynet).

  • 3+ years of experience designing or enhancing fraud controls, monitoring frameworks, and risk mitigation strategies supporting payment abuse prevention, chargeback management, or scheme-compliance programs.

  • 3+ years of hands-on SQL and data-analysis experience, including analyzing large datasets, identifying fraud trends, defining risk metrics or KPIs, and translating findings into operational or product improvements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience operating in a global, high-volume digital payments environment.

  • Experience with alternative payment methods and regional ecosystems, such as SEPA, iDEAL, ACH, and digital wallets.

  • Track record of influencing product, policy, or platform changes to reduce abuse risk.

  • Experience maturing an existing function by formalizing processes, raising quality standards, or evolving its operating model.

  • Experience overseeing work delivered by vendors or managed service providers.

  • Experience mentoring analysts in a payments risk, fraud, or Trust & Safety organization.

Suggested Skills

Payment & Fraud Abuse • Payments Risk • Scheme Compliance & Risk Management • Chargebacks & Disputes • Fraud Investigation • Root-Cause Analysis • SQL & Data Analysis • Control Design • Risk Monitoring & Remediation • Process Optimization • Vendor Oversight • Cross-Functional Leadership • Stakeholder Influence • Mentorship
