title: VN 2026/02-Project Associate
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

Organizational Context and Scope

Under the overall supervision of the Head of Office (HoO) and direct supervision of the National Project Coordination Officer, the Project Associate will be responsible and accountable for the following duties:

1. Assist in the implementation and monitoring of project activities.
2. Retrieve, compile, summarise, analyse, and present information/data on specific project topics.
3. Monitor budget by verifying availability of funds, obtaining necessary approval and updating budget-related information.
4. Act as focal point for administrative coordination of project implementation, involving extensive liaison with diverse organisational units and external parties to initiate requests, obtain necessary clearances, process and follow-up on administrative actions, etc.
5. Draft status reports, identify shortfalls, escalate issues to the supervisor and suggest remedial actions to address delivery gaps.
6. Draft correspondence on project issues; prepare and update reports, briefing notes, graphics, statistical tables, presentation and other forms of documentation.
7. Respond to complex information requests and inquiries, set up and maintain files/records, and organise meetings, workshops and training sessions.
8. Participate in meetings and conferences to assist in coordinating implementation activities with local authorities, partners, United Nation (UN) agencies, intergovernmental and non-governmental organisations, donors and other stakeholders relevant to the project.
9. Assist in monitoring work of Implementing Partners (IP) and report non-compliances to the supervisor.
10. Provides guidance/training to new/junior staff.
11. Perform such other relevant duties as maybe assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

• Bachelor’s degree in Law, Political or Social Sciences, International Relations, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Human Rights or a related field from an accredited academic institution with three years of relevant professional experience; or,
• High School diploma with five years of relevant professional experience.
Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

• Experience in liaising with governmental authorities, national/international institutions, United Nations agencies and non-governmental organisations;
• Experience in working with migrants, refugees, internally displaced persons, victims of trafficking and other vulnerable groups; and,
• Prior work experience with international humanitarian organisations, non-government or government institutions/organisation in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.

Skills

  • Strong organizational and administrative skills.
  • Ability to compile, analyse and present information clearly.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines.
  • Attention to detail and accuracy in documentation and reporting.
  • Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment, both independently and as part of a team

Languages

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English and Albanian is required (oral and written).

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 1

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports

  • Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.
  • Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.
  • Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.
  • Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction.
  • Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings.

Notes

Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Lead Clerk
description:
About Us

Join us at WinCo Foods, where we're more than just a grocery retailer - we're a growing family of over 140 supermarkets in 10 states with over 22,000 employee owners. Our purpose is to make the lives of our customers and employee owners better by offering the lowest possible prices to feed their families. Overview

Job Summary

Assist management with the operations of the store by performing clerk duties in the designated department (grocery or freight), leading by example, and assisting the department manager in general department operations as directed. Answer customer questions and complaints in a professional manner and assure all customers receive fast, friendly service. Perform the duties of a grocery clerk, cashier and/or freight stocker in addition to assisting assigned employees in the performance of their tasks as appropriate, including notifying them of their breaks and lunches. Performs other related work.

Typical Duties and Responsibilities

  • Seeks opportunities to welcome, engage, serve and thank customers. Maintains and encourages an atmosphere of friendly, enthusiastic customer service with an emphasis of taking care of the customer.
  • Provides customer service by performing the duties of a clerk in the designated department (grocery or freight). **Refer to Grocery Clerk, Cashier/Checker and/or Freight Stocker job descriptions for complete list of responsibilities.
  • Performs a lead role in customer service which may include handling customer complaints and requests, approving checks, selling gift certificates, issuing refunds, receiving returned check payments and answering any questions the customer must have.
  • Continuously monitors area activities, including customer traffic flow, coverage of checkout lanes, etc.
  • Maintains cleanliness and eye-appeal of work area, storage area, equipment and retail displays according to company policy and legal regulations; and cleans work area by mopping, sweeping, taking out garbage, etc.
  • Ensures the department/area of responsibility is kept clear of excess carts, baskets, garbage, etc.
  • Monitors arrivals, breaks, lunches and departures of employees in area of responsibility. Communicates with immediate supervisor regularly.
  • Assists immediate supervisor as needed or directed.
  • Assists clerks by providing direction and leadership, demonstrating and performing clerk responsibilities and assigned tasks, and answering employee questions.
  • May monitor cashier money handling procedures and assists with scan system procedures (i.e. UPC codes not on file, scan pricing errors, etc.).
  • May fill department racks/shelves, displays, coolers, handle and use cleaning materials, department machines and equipment, pull cardboard and face the wall and aisles, perform cashiering duties, perform other duties as needed or directed.
  • Maintains a constant awareness of customer and employee safety.
  • Stocks and rotates merchandise in any area of the store as needed.
  • Performs other duties as assigned or needed.

Requirements

Education:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent

Experience:

  • Communicating clearly and professionally, utilizing excellent verbal, written and inter-personal communication skills, establishing and maintaining a good rapport with co-workers, supervisors, vendors, customers and others.
  • Providing leadership, exhibiting interpersonal skills by maintaining composure and professionally addressing difficult and sometimes angry individuals including customers, vendors and co-workers.
  • Applying clear understanding of overall company practices, including in-depth knowledge of polices/procedures, in order to effectively judge and react to customer activity.
  • Demonstrating initiative and self-direction to perform a variety of simultaneous skills (multi-tasking).
  • Conducting visual inspections, reading reports, computer printouts, register and computer screens, etc.
  • Perform basic math (add, subtract, multiply and divide) and compute weights and measures.
  • Perform primary duties efficiently and accurately with honesty and integrity.
  • In Montana and Oregon the minimum age is 18 years old. All other states the minimum age is 21 years old.

Ability to:

  • Consistently provide world class customer service to internal and external customers.
  • Work varied shifts in a 24/7 operation; including night, weekends and holidays.
  • Perform all duties described in the appropriate department specific job description (grocery clerk, cashier and/or freight stocker).
  • Understand overall company practices through previous experience in designated department (grocery or freight) or equivalent.
  • Properly use cleaning chemicals in accordance with manufacture’s guidelines and instructions.
  • Properly handle food products per State and County laws, and WinCo standards.
  • Reach, lift and maneuver objects of varying dimensions and weights up to 50 lbs. frequently.
  • Stand for long periods of time, walk and move rapidly, bend, stoop, twist and turn frequently.
  • Perform duties with mental alertness involving potential hazards with respect to related procedures, machines, equipment and work aides.
  • Understand state & federal regulations if certification is needed.
  • Perform primary duties efficiently and accurately.

Additional Requirements:

  • Must meet age requirements listed above.
  • Food Handlers Certification (Per State Laws)

Machines and Equipment Operated:

  • Refer to appropriate department specific job description (grocery clerk, cashier and/or freight stocker) for complete list.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature of work performed by the employees assigned to this job. All employees must comply with Company policies and applicable laws. The responsibilities, duties and qualifications required of personnel may vary.

EEO/Inclusivity

As the WinCo Foods community continues to grow, our variety of perspectives and wide range of experiences are essential to our strategy and success. We are committed cultivating and celebrating an inclusive environment in which all employees are valued and respected.

title: Process Control Technician, 2nd shift
description:
Job Description

As the Process Controls Technician, you will be responsible for maintaining, troubleshooting, improving, and supporting the plant's process control, automation, instrumentation, and electrical systems to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient manufacturing operations. You will support production, maintenance, and engineering teams by ensuring control systems, instrumentation, PLCs, HMIs, networking, and related electrical systems perform while complying with company policies and regulatory requirements.


Responsibilities

  • Maintain and troubleshoot process control systems, including PLCs, HMIs, SCADA systems, and industrial networks.
  • Support Allen Bradley PLC platforms, SCADA systems, HMI applications, and communication networks.
  • Resolve process control issues that impact production, quality, safety, or reliability.
  • Monitor system performance and identify opportunities to improve control strategies and plant automation.
  • Specify, troubleshoot process instrumentation including: Flow meters, Pressure transmitters, Temperature instruments, Level instruments, Control valves, Analyzers
  • Assist and troubleshoot issues with maintenance and operations technicians for efficient operation of the facility.
  • Support electrical systems troubleshooting and modifications.
  • Ensure instrumentation and electrical equipment operate within design parameters.

Qualifications

  • Associate degree in Electrical Engineering Technology, Instrumentation, Automation, or related field; or equivalent experience.
  • 3+ years of experience in process controls, instrumentation, automation, and electrical systems in a manufacturing environment.
  • Experience with Allen-Bradley PLCs, HMI/SCADA systems, industrial networks, and process instrumentation.
  • Troubleshoot and maintain PLCs, instrumentation, electrical systems, VFDs, and control circuits.
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, P&IDs, loop drawings, and technical documentation.
  • Ability to work 2nd shift - 3:30pm-11:30pm, w/ potential OT

Overview

The Air Operations Agent I is responsible for coordinating the day-to-day air import and export of international freight forwarding shipments out of the USA of international transportation based upon customer requests.

Responsibilities

  • Work with customers to qualify their shipping requirements and obtain all details (regulations, certificates, documentation) necessary for shipment quotation and operating in order to ensure the customer’s request is satisfied.

  • Complete shipment process in Cargowise, including data entry, pickup/delivery scheduling, AES entry, airline bookings, routing, and operational milestone updates.
  • Coordinate the day-to-day air import and export of products, including reviewing orders and documents.
  • Track and communicate all delays, damages, problems, and work to resolve customer issues.
  • Responsible for all aspects of air import and export international operations such as customer service, data entry of shipments, operations and billing.
  • Manage all aspects of tracking shipments to ensure shipment is moving as scheduled and update system immediately upon verification. Identify and rectify if a shipment has deviated from its schedule.
  • Coordinate recovery/delivery schedules with various cartage agents and international partners.
  • Partner with local sales teams to communicate problems to customers, international partners and other stations, as needed.
  • Ensure all customers’ SOP instructions are adhered to and AIT KPIs and guidelines are followed and met.
  • Ensure all shipments are properly billed within company guidelines and timelines.
  • Other duties and responsibilities will be assigned as business demands deem necessary.

Qualifications

  • A team player who works well with others – being respectful to our teammates is a Core Value
  • A strong work ethic with an appreciation for ownership, independence, accountability, and autonomy in your role
  • Growth mindset – being passionate about your craft, always looking for ways to improve yourself and the company, being open to change and doing things differently
  • Customer service focus – we serve a wide variety of customers, both internal and external, and building relationships is a part of our culture

Other Skills We Hope to See:

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 0-2 Years Freight Forwarding experience preferred
  • Basic math & geography skills
  • Ability to analyze numerical data and understand components, relationships, find patterns and draw conclusions.
  • Basic knowledge of CargoWise preferred
  • Basic knowledge of freight movement, air vendors, air space configurations, container loads, special loading constraints, regulatory requirements, pricing, service routings, AIT product offerings, equipment types, incoterms, and shipment profitability.
  • Basic knowledge of country regulations and AIT policies & procedures that minimize risks to the customer and company.
  • Ability to add, subtract, multiply, divide using units of currency, weight, volume, and distance measurements.
  • Acquires job skills and learns company policies and procedures to complete routine tasks.

title: Core Trainer, Portland - Full Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. Job Summary

The trainer should demonstrate knowledge of all job tasks within their assigned department and function and deliver a high-level of accuracy and consistency when performing the work, training colleagues, or reviewing completed work. Core Trainers will be crossed-trained in all areas of the facility. This role plays a critical part in developing colleagues through training, retraining and supporting both new and current team members to ensure operational excellence, accuracy and consistency. The Core Trainer demonstrates a deep understanding of the end- to- end supply chain flow and embodies the genuine hospitality and inclusive culture of Macy’s.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. All schedules contain weekend shifts as part of the requirements. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

What You Will Do

Training Support

  • Support Core and Seasonal Colleagues in assigned departments/functions by training and coaching on essential job tasks to ensure successful job performance.
  • Provide onboarding and operational training for new hires to ensure understanding of operating procedures, safety expectations, quality standards, and productivity goals.
  • Provide refresher training and retraining for existing colleagues who are not meeting operational performance, quality, safety, or productivity standards to reinforce proper operating procedures and improve overall performance.
  • Ensure work instructions, safety guidelines, and quality expectations are consistently followed throughout daily operations.
  • Consult and partner with designated Training Ambassador regarding work instructions, process updates, operational gaps, and training opportunities to ensure consistency and standardization across the facility.
  • Serve as a cross-functional trainer capable of supporting operational training needs across multiple departments throughout the facility.
  • Complete training checklists and conduct follow-up to ensure colleagues successfully complete the training period and achieve operational standards.
  • Perform frequent quality and productivity audits of work processed and provide immediate coaching and corrective feedback when needed.
  • Observe workflows, minimize errors, assess job proficiency, and retrain colleagues as necessary to improve performance and productivity.
  • Partner with Warehouse Managers and Leads to identify operational gaps, problem solve performance issues and implement training solutions that improve execution and productivity.
  • Demonstrate a passion for training and developing others while creating an engaging learning environment that motivates colleagues to succeed.
  • Adapt training methods to support different learning styles and operational demands.

Communication

  • Greet colleagues on their first day of employment and conduct orientation activities including building tours, time clock procedures, and reliability expectations.
  • Act as a point person for colleagues by answering questions related to processes, functions, safety, and operational expectations.
  • Communicate issues, concerns, and performance trends promptly to Managers, or Shift/Functional Directors for quick resolution.
  • Build positive working relationships and effectively influence and motivate others to drive accountability, engagement, and productivity.
  • Maintain strong attention to detail when documenting training progress, identifying performance trends, and communicating operational updates.

Safety Throughout Shift Safety Advocate

  • Demonstrate and reinforce safe workplace behaviors consistent with company safety policies and procedures.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Maintain regular, dependable attendance and punctuality.
  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships and ensures authentic connections with colleagues, customers, and communities.
  • Demonstrate flexibility to support changing business needs, peak operations, and cross-functional training initiatives.

Who You Are

Must be able to:

  • Strong attention to detail is essential to maintain quality, safety, and operational efficiency.
  • Understand and communicate effectively with, co-workers, leads, and facility leadership.
  • Read and understand employment policies and safety rules/procedures in English.
  • Demonstrate an affinity and passion for training, coaching, and developing others.
  • Exhibit strong attention to detail and the ability to consistently reinforce standard operating procedures.
  • Motivate, influence, and engage colleagues to achieve operational productivity and quality goals.
  • Partner effectively with Warehouse Managers, Training Ambassadors and Leads to resolve operational challenges and improve team performance.
  • Demonstrate strong interpersonal, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Positively impact team success in a fast-paced environment.
  • Manage multiple priorities and processes effectively while maintaining operational standards.
  • Work assigned scheduled including days, evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed.

Essential Physical Requirements You Will Perform

  • This position requires lifting, constant moving, standing, and reaching with arms and hands.
  • Involves standing for at least two consecutive hours, lifting at least 50lbs., stooping, kneeling, crouching, and climbing ladders.
  • Reaching, including above eye level, crouching, kneeling, and stooping.
  • Involves close vision, color vision, depth perception, and focus adjustment.
  • Frequent use of computers and other technology, necessary to perform job functions, including handheld equipment.

Supply Chain Only and Colleagues Working in a Supply Chain Facility except in locations governed by a Collective Bargaining Agreement:

Random drug testing for all colleagues will be conducted on a monthly or semi-monthly basis, depending upon factors including but not limited to the size of the facility and the number of colleagues on roll. Colleagues will be randomly selected for testing by a third party. Testing must be completed on the same workday the colleague is informed of selection for testing, absent extenuating circumstances. In all circumstances, testing must be completed within 24 hours of notification.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - Apply Today!

title: Principal Systems Engineer
description:
Salary: $120k - $150k p.a.

Principal Systems Engineer - Enterprise Services

Shape the future of enterprise platforms at Massey University - join our Enterprise Services team.

Be at the heart of secure, reliable and well-governed digital services that support teaching, research and operations.

Lead standards, mentor engineers and help Massey's enterprise services evolve for the future.

Mō tēnei tūranga mahi | About this role

We're looking for an experienced Principal Systems Engineer to help shape and operate Massey's core enterprise systems - AI Platforms, Data Platform including Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft 365 and Power Platform, identity and access, Azure, databases, and Linux. You'll lead on platform design, security, performance, reliability and operational guardrails, keeping our services trusted, scalable and well governed.

Working alongside architecture, security, applications, infrastructure and digital enablement colleagues, you'll deliver joined-up services that support teaching, research, operations and future AI use cases.

Āu mahi | What you will do

  • Lead the technical lifecycle of Massey's enterprise platforms, from design and build through to operation, improvement and retirement.
  • Own platform foundations - configuration, access, monitoring, performance, cost, release, resilience and support.
  • Set practical standards and guardrails that keep services secure, reliable, compliant and easy to support.
  • Partner with technical and business stakeholders to enable trusted collaboration, automation, integration and AI services.
  • Mentor colleagues and champion good practice in platform engineering, governance, automation and service reliability.
  • Provide strategic technology leadership by defining and communicating a clear long-term direction, aligning investment and delivery priorities with organisational objectives, and ensuring technology decisions support future growth, innovation, and operational sustainability.

Ko koe tēnei | Who you are

  • Collaborative and inclusive, able to build trust across technical and non-technical teams.
  • A clear communicator who can explain complex platform concepts in practical, accessible ways.
  • Generous with your expertise - you mentor, support and lift the people around you.
  • Sound judgement and ownership, with the ability to make considered decisions and manage competing priorities.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and challenging change - effective and decisive while direction is still forming.
  • Strong influencing skills, bringing people together to build shared understanding and practical decisions.

Technical Skills and Experience

Essential

  • A tertiary qualification in IT or business management, or equivalent industry experience.
  • Industry-recognised certification at senior practitioner level in systems or platform engineering, cloud, Microsoft 365, Linux or security.
  • Minimum 6 years' experience in a senior or principal engineering role across enterprise platforms such as Microsoft 365, Linux, or equivalent enterprise services.
  • A track record of designing, building and operating enterprise platforms at scale.
  • Hands-on experience across several of: Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams), Entra ID / Active Directory, Power Platform, Azure or equivalent cloud services, databases and data platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, Linux and scripting (Bash/Python/PowerShell), and Microsoft Purview or Defender.
  • Advanced engineering capability across automation, scripting, monitoring, performance tuning, release practices and production support.
  • Strong grasp of enterprise architecture and governance, including security, privacy, compliance, integration patterns and APIs.

Highly Desirable

  • Infrastructure as Code, cloud automation, CI/CD or DevOps practices.
  • Service ownership, disaster recovery, security hardening, data governance or compliance frameworks.
  • Knowledge of strategic IT issues in education, research, public sector or government.
  • Microsoft Copilot or similar AI assistants, including enterprise adoption, safe operation and governance.
  • Cloud AI services such as Azure AI, with an understanding of data privacy and responsible AI.

Ko ngā hua o te tūranga? | What's in it for you?

  • Up to 6.75% employer contribution to the UniSaver Superannuation Scheme.
  • Five university holidays per year in addition to your annual leave.
  • Subsidised Southern Cross Healthcare plan for you and your family.
  • Discounted membership to our fully equipped recreation centre and gym facilities.
  • Staff purchasing privileges and discounts at many commercial and retail businesses across NZ.
  • Access to on-campus crèche/day care facilities for dependents of staff on our Manawatū and Auckland campuses.

This is a full-time position (1 FTE 37.50hrs p/w) with the following location and work options available to the preferred candidate:

  1. Based in Palmerston North, with a minimum of 3 days a week on Manawatū campus.
  2. Based in Wellington, with 1 day a week at the Manawatū campus and minimum 2 days a week at Wellington campus.

The salary for this position ranges from $120,000-$150,000 based on skills and experience.


Massey is a Te Tiriti-led university, upholding the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi in our everyday practice. We work with mutual respect and care, we are future-focused and results-oriented, and we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds who share those values.


Join us and help shape Massey University's digital future. If you want your engineering to matter well beyond the data centre, we'd love to hear from you.

Applications will be reviewed as submitted and we may interview prior to the role closing on Sunday 01 Nov 2026, 11.00pm.

title: Direction of Leadership, Strategy and Programs – Luis von Ahn Foundation
description:
Selection process developed by matteria

Location and Work Mode

Full-time, contract-based position based in Guatemala, with a hybrid and trust-based working model.

Who we are

The Luis von Ahn Foundation is a private foundation committed to building a more inclusive and prosperous Guatemala where all people are equally valued, can thrive, and can fully exercise their rights. Founded in 2021, the Foundation has supported local organizations working across education, women's and girls' equality, democracy and citizen participation, and nature conservation. Beginning in 2027, the Foundation will enter a new strategic chapter focused on strengthening the next generation of Guatemalan leaders.

Our impact

  • Founded in 2021: The Foundation has built its work around supporting local organizations and community leaders in Guatemala.

  • 35 organizations supported: The Foundation has partnered with organizations working to create positive change across Guatemala.

  • 4 areas of focus: Its first strategic chapter supported education, women's and girls' equality, democracy and citizen participation, and nature conservation.

  • Next strategic chapter: Beginning in 2027, the Foundation will focus its grantmaking on leadership development through educational pathways, leadership accelerators, and platforms that elevate exemplary Guatemalan leaders.

Purpose of the Position

Lead the collaborative design, completion, implementation and continuous learning of the Foundation's 2027–2032 leadership strategy. The Director will translate an evolving strategic vision into a coherent portfolio of investments, partnerships and programs that cultivate and accelerate the next generation of Guatemalan leaders.

This is the first leadership hire specifically designed for the Foundation's new strategic chapter and will play a central role in moving the organization from strategy development into implementation.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy & Portfolio Leadership

  • Lead the completion and ongoing refinement of the Foundation's 2027–2032 leadership strategy.

  • Translate strategic priorities into clear investment frameworks, grantmaking criteria, annual priorities and actionable plans.

  • Ensure coherence across the Foundation's leadership pipelines, accelerators and Premio-related initiatives.

  • Identify emerging needs, opportunities, research and promising practices and translate them into strategic recommendations.

  • Help the Foundation make thoughtful trade-offs and maintain focus as the strategy evolves.

Strategy-to-Action & Implementation

  • Translate a partially developed strategy into concrete priorities, programs, timelines and decisions.

  • Move effectively between strategic thinking and hands-on implementation, particularly during the first year.

  • Establish the structures, processes and priorities required to operationalize the new strategy.

  • Maintain ownership and follow-through while navigating ambiguity, evolving priorities and incomplete information.

  • Ensure that strategic ideas lead to concrete action, learning and results.

Portfolio & Grantmaking Development

  • Help develop and launch the Foundation's leadership accelerators and related investments.

  • Develop grantmaking criteria and assessment frameworks for new portfolio organizations.

  • Identify and select high-performing organizations aligned with the Foundation's leadership strategy.

  • Initially support the development of a portfolio of approximately 3–5 accelerator organizations, while contributing to the broader leadership portfolio.

  • Over time, help build and manage an integrated portfolio that may grow to approximately 10–20 organizations.

  • Ensure that individual investments connect to one another and contribute to a coherent leadership ecosystem.

Learning, Evidence & Adaptation

  • Develop learning questions and evidence priorities in collaboration with the Foundation's Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning partner and grantee organizations.

  • Use evidence, feedback and experience to test assumptions and refine strategy.

  • Help define meaningful indicators of progress without turning measurement into a compliance exercise.

  • Synthesize insights from the portfolio into clear strategic recommendations.

  • Foster a culture of experimentation, iteration and continuous learning.

Ecosystem & Network Building

  • Build trusted relationships with organizations and leaders across Guatemala's leadership ecosystem.

  • Convene partners to share learning, reduce fragmentation and identify opportunities for collaboration.

  • Strengthen connections among emerging leaders, alumni, organizations, funders, universities, civil society, government and the private sector.

  • Develop opportunities for collaboration and co-investment across sectors.

  • Represent the Foundation externally in Guatemala and internationally.

Executive, Board & Organizational Leadership

  • Serve as a strategic thought partner to the Executive Director.

  • Prepare concise, evidence-based recommendations for the Executive Director, Board and Founder.

  • Communicate complex issues with clarity, rigor and sound judgment.

  • Translate the realities and nuances of Guatemala into language and recommendations that resonate with a business-oriented Board.

Contribute to organizational planning, annual priorities, budgets and cross-functional

Requirements and competences to work with us

Education

  • Bachelor's degree required; relevant fields may include social sciences, education, public policy, business, economics, international development, organizational development or related disciplines.

  • Advanced studies in leadership development, social impact, philanthropy, public policy, education, management or a related field are desirable but not mandatory.

Experience

  • 8+ years of relevant professional experience, including significant responsibility for designing, leading, growing or improving complex programs, initiatives, portfolios or organizations.

  • Demonstrated experience translating strategy into implementation in complex or evolving environments.

  • Experience in one or more relevant areas such as leadership development, youth development, education, talent development, philanthropy, social innovation or social impact.

  • Experience working across multiple stakeholders and sectors.

  • Experience developing programs, investment strategies, partnerships or portfolios is strongly valued.

  • Experience with philanthropy, grantmaking or working with funders and grantee organizations is desirable.

  • Experience working directly with emerging leaders, youth, cohorts, fellowships or accelerator programs is desirable.

  • Experience with Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning is desirable, but deep technical MEL expertise is not required: the Foundation expects to work with specialized MEL support.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Professional fluency in Spanish and English, both written and spoken.

  • Deep understanding of Guatemala's social, cultural, institutional and, ideally, political context, and the ability to recognize how history, power and inequality shape access to opportunity. Being Guatemalan is not a requirement: what is essential is demonstrated contextual understanding, credibility and the ability to work thoughtfully across Guatemala's different realities and communities.

  • Ability to synthesize complex, diverse and sometimes contradictory information, and to turn a loosely defined strategy into priorities, plans, decisions, programs and measurable progress.

Competencies

  • Strategic thinking and synthesis: identify what matters most, make thoughtful trade-offs and translate insights into clear strategic direction.

  • Strategy-to-action: turn an ambitious or loosely defined strategy into priorities, plans, decisions and measurable progress.

  • Guatemala context and equity: translate an understanding of history, power and inequality into strategy and grantmaking decisions.

  • Executive communication: communicate clearly, concisely and persuasively with community organizations, civil society, government, funders, international partners, the Executive Director and a business-oriented Board.

  • Communication "code-switching": adapt language, level of detail, tone and style to the audience without losing authenticity, substance or commitment to equity and inclusion.

  • Facilitation and collaborative leadership: design inclusive processes, surface diverse perspectives, navigate disagreement and ambiguity, and move groups toward decisions and next steps without needing to be the primary decision maker.

  • Learning and adaptability: curiosity, humility and openness to evidence and feedback, and the ability to recognize when an approach is incomplete and adapt.

  • Relationship and network building: establish trusted relationships across organizations, sectors, perspectives and levels of influence.

Our team profile

  • Clear is kind: transparency and direct communication, particularly during periods of organizational change.

  • Learning over certainty: the new strategy is intentionally designed as a learning laboratory, and the Foundation does not expect to have every answer in advance.

  • Listen before prescribing: entering different communities and organizations with curiosity, humility and a genuine willingness to learn.

  • Equity in practice: equity and inclusion shape how strategies, programs, partnerships and grantmaking criteria are designed, beyond stated values.

  • High standards with humanity: rigor, accountability and results, with respect for partners and the realities in which they operate.

  • Collaboration over ego: facilitating alignment and enabling others rather than always being the person with the answer.

  • Experimentation and iteration: testing ideas, learning quickly and adapting rather than staying abstract or purely academic.

  • Context matters: understanding the nuances of Guatemala rather than applying generic international-development frameworks without adaptation.

Key interests for working with us

This opportunity is particularly relevant for someone motivated by the challenge of strengthening the leadership Guatemala needs for its future. The role will engage with issues including:

  • Expanding opportunity for historically underrepresented populations

  • Youth leadership and development

  • Education and pathways to opportunity

  • Equity and inclusion

  • Indigenous and historically marginalized communities

  • Strengthening local leadership and community-led solutions

  • Building stronger connections across Guatemala's social-impact ecosystem

  • Strengthening organizations and institutions through leadership

  • Developing more effective and learning-oriented philanthropy

  • Contributing to a more inclusive, prosperous and resilient Guatemala

The Foundation's new strategy is grounded in the belief that lasting progress depends on capable, ethical and committed leaders, and that many talented young Guatemalans continue to face barriers to developing their leadership potential.

Reasons to join our team

A unique moment to shape a new strategy. This is the first senior role created specifically for the Foundation's new strategic chapter. The Director will have meaningful influence over how the 2027–2032 strategy is translated into action.

Strategic proximity to decision-makers. The position works directly with the Executive Director and engages with the Board, providing significant exposure to strategic decision-making.

Opportunity to build, not simply operate. The role is designed to evolve. In the first year, the focus will be heavily weighted toward strategy development and operationalization. Over time, the position will increasingly focus on portfolio leadership, relationships, learning and ecosystem building.

Opportunity to shape the future team. The Foundation expects to complement the Director's capabilities with future roles, potentially including a Program Manager and other specialized support.

A learning-oriented philanthropic model. The Foundation is intentionally approaching its new portfolio as a learning laboratory, working with grantees and specialized partners to understand what works and continuously improve.

Benefits. The current package includes:

  • Healthcare support through a healthcare stipend/reimbursement structure.

  • Life insurance coverage.

  • A retirement benefit.

  • Professional development and conference support.

  • Potential relocation support for candidates moving to Guatemala.

Relevant details before applying for this vacancy

Please consider the following before applying:

  • The position is full-time and operates under a contract-based structure.

  • The role requires approximately 25% travel, primarily within Guatemala, with some international travel, including to the United States.

title: Microsoft Power Platform Developer (Power BI / Power Apps / Power Automate)
description:
Title: Microsoft Power Platform Developer (Power Apps / Power BI / Power Automate)

Function: PEO DHMS

Location: Remote

Reports to: Program Leadership


POSITION SUMMARY:

The Microsoft Power Platform Developer supports both the Enterprise Intelligence and Data Solutions (EIDS) and Defense Healthcare Management System Modernization (DHMSM) programs by building and maintaining applications, reporting, and automation that help teams manage products, portfolios, workflows, and program performance.

This role is hands-on and execution focused, with a primary emphasis on advanced Microsoft Power Apps development. The individual will design, enhance, and maintain business applications while also using Power Automate, Power BI, Azure DevOps, and Microsoft 365 to create integrated solutions that support day-to-day program operations and leadership decision-making.

The developer will support requirements across both EIDS and DHMSM and should be comfortable working across multiple teams, stakeholders, and priorities. The role requires someone who can understand a business need, determine the right technical approach, and independently deliver a practical and maintainable solution.

The ideal candidate is an experienced Power Apps developer who also understands how reporting, automation, data, and program processes fit together in a complex enterprise environment.


JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

Power Apps Development

  • Design, develop, enhance, and maintain advanced Microsoft Power Apps solutions
  • Serve as a strong hands-on Power Apps developer capable of independently translating business requirements into working applications
  • Support applications used to manage products, projects, documentation, portfolio activities, and operational workflows
  • Manage and prioritize Power Apps development backlogs and deliver enhancements iteratively
  • Integrate Power Apps with Microsoft 365, Power Automate, Power BI, Azure DevOps, and other approved data sources
  • Troubleshoot application performance, usability, data, and integration issues
  • Design solutions that are scalable, maintainable, and easy for program teams to use
  • Apply sound practices for application security, permissions, data access, and lifecycle management

Power Automate and Workflow Automation

  • Develop Power Automate workflows to connect applications, data, and business processes
  • Automate repetitive tasks and reduce manual effort across program workflows
  • Build reliable and maintainable automation that supports Power Apps and other Microsoft-based solutions
  • Troubleshoot workflow failures and improve existing automations as business needs evolve

Power BI Development and Reporting

  • Design, develop, and maintain Power BI dashboards using data from multiple sources
  • Connect Power BI to Microsoft Azure DevOps and other systems to support portfolio and execution reporting
  • Perform data transformation, modeling, and validation to ensure accuracy and reliability
  • Create clear visualizations that translate program data into useful information for leadership and delivery teams
  • Support reporting requirements that complement Power Apps and broader Power Platform solutions

Azure DevOps Integration

  • Use Microsoft Azure DevOps as a data source and integration point for Power Platform solutions
  • Develop applications and reporting that support portfolio management, delivery tracking, backlog management, and performance measurement
  • Apply a strong technical understanding of Azure DevOps data structures, work items, and reporting capabilities
  • Help connect Azure DevOps information with Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power BI where appropriate

Cross-Program Support

  • Support Power Platform needs across both EIDS and DHMSM
  • Work with stakeholders across multiple teams to understand, prioritize, and deliver requirements
  • Balance competing priorities and adjust work as program needs change
  • Build solutions that can be used across teams when common requirements or opportunities exist
  • Maintain clear visibility into work in progress, dependencies, risks, and expected delivery timelines

SAFe and Portfolio Context

  • Design applications and reporting aligned with SAFe concepts, particularly portfolio management and execution tracking
  • Support leadership visibility into priorities, capacity, schedules, dependencies, and delivery
  • Apply SAFe and portfolio context when designing solutions so that applications and reporting are relevant to actual program operations

Collaboration and Enablement

  • Work closely with program teams, analysts, product owners, and leadership to gather and refine requirements
  • Translate business needs into clear technical solutions without requiring stakeholders to define the technical approach
  • Demonstrate solutions, incorporate feedback, and refine applications as requirements evolve
  • Provide documentation and guidance to support adoption and long-term maintenance
  • Help teams transition to new applications, reporting, and automated workflows


BASIC JOB REQUIREMENTS:

  • 6–8 years of hands-on experience delivering Microsoft Power Platform solutions in complex enterprise environments
  • Strong demonstrated experience designing and developing Microsoft Power Apps, including complex applications used by business or program teams
  • Experience integrating Power Apps with Power Automate, Microsoft 365, Power BI, Azure DevOps, and other data sources
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot and improve Power Apps performance, usability, and maintainability
  • Experience building Power BI dashboards using multiple data sources
  • Experience integrating Microsoft Azure DevOps with Power Platform solutions for reporting, workflow, or metrics
  • Working knowledge of the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe), particularly portfolio and execution concepts
  • Ability to manage multiple development priorities and work across different teams or programs
  • Ability to translate business needs into clear and effective technical solutions
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • U.S. Citizen

KEY COMPETENCIES:

  • Advanced Power Apps development capability
  • Strong technical and functional judgment
  • Ability to independently translate requirements into practical solutions
  • Ability to design solutions that answer real business and operational needs
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
  • Attention to detail and data accuracy
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities across teams and programs
  • Ability to communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Comfortable working in an environment where requirements and priorities may evolve

PREFERRED CERTIFICATIONS:

  • Microsoft Power Platform Developer Associate
  • Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst Associate
  • Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) certification

title: Applications Analyst - Epic Ambulatory (Salaried, Full time)
description:
Organization Overview, Mission, Vision, and Values

Our mission is to improve the health of people in the communities we serve through compassionate, high-quality care, prevention, and wellness education. Washington Regional Medical System is a community-owned, locally governed, non-profit health care system located in Northwest Arkansas in the heart of Fayetteville, which is consistently ranked among the Best Places to live in the country. Our 425-bed medical center has been named the #1 hospital in Arkansas for five consecutive years by U.S. News & World Report. We employ 3,400+ team members and serve the region with over 40 clinic locations, the region’s only Level II trauma center, and five Centers of Excellence - the Washington Regional J.B. Hunt Transport Services Neuroscience Institute; Washington Regional Walker Heart Institute; Washington Regional Women and Infants Center; Washington Regional Total Joint Center; and Washington Regional Pat Walker Center for Seniors.

Position Summary

The Applications Analyst – Epic Ambulatory reports to the Assistant Manager, Epic Applications. This position is responsible for advanced support, troubleshooting, maintenance, build, testing, and optimization of Epic Ambulatory and related outpatient clinical workflows. The role partners with clinic leadership, providers, clinical staff, operational teams, information services, and Epic/vendor stakeholders to improve ambulatory documentation, orders, referrals, medication management, patient access workflows, care coordination, reporting, charging, and cross-application integration; ensure application reliability; and support safe, efficient patient care across the ambulatory enterprise.

Essential Position Responsibilities

  • Maintain advanced knowledge of Epic Ambulatory functionality, including outpatient workflow design, provider and clinical documentation, orders, referrals, medication management, visit workflows, application dependencies, integration points, and downstream impacts across the enterprise
  • Lead ambulatory stakeholders, clinic leaders, providers, clinical and operational teams, internal information services teams, and Epic/vendor partners in developing Epic Ambulatory enhancements, optimization initiatives, and workflow improvement projects
  • Oversee Epic Ambulatory application design, build, configuration, maintenance, and validation to ensure functionality aligns with clinic operations, provider workflows, clinical documentation needs, patient access workflows, and end-user requirements
  • Perform complex analysis, build, implementation, and optimization of Epic Ambulatory workflows to support outpatient clinical documentation, orders, referrals, medication management, visit documentation, care coordination, charging, reporting, and integrated clinical workflows
  • Meet regularly with clinic staff, providers, clinical leaders, operational leaders, patient access partners, and administrative teams to evaluate Epic Ambulatory workflow issues, resolve system concerns, and identify opportunities to improve quality, efficiency, safety, care coordination, documentation integrity, and the end-user experience
  • Lead the development and execution of coordinated testing plans for Epic Ambulatory, including regression, unit, system, integrated, interface, charging, reporting, and user acceptance testing to ensure changes function as expected for end users and connected systems
  • Serve as a leading advocate for Epic Ambulatory users by translating outpatient clinical, provider, patient access, and operational needs into effective system solutions that improve patient care, workflow efficiency, documentation quality, reporting accuracy, and user satisfaction
  • Provide mentorship for team members and assist with team member training, as needed
  • Ensure that programs and services meet accrediting standards for the Joint Commission, Quality, Promoting Interoperability, and other accrediting and governance programs
  • Ensure the safeguarding of protected health information
  • Maintain communication through various resources and tools
  • Monitor help desk software for new tickets and update and provide resolution for existing tickets
  • Lead Epic Ambulatory projects, enhancements, upgrades, optimization efforts, testing activities, and ongoing maintenance initiatives
  • Identify and lead opportunities to improve Epic-supported ambulatory documentation, provider, patient access, referral, medication management, charging, reporting, and care coordination workflows through system optimization, standardization, and process improvement
  • Adhere to all information services policies, procedures, and governance processes
  • Lead incident response and downtime procedures

Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree or clinical license, preferred.
  • Licensure and Certifications: Epic Ambulatory certification required. EpicCare Link certification or proficiency preferred.
  • Experience: Four to six years of clinical applications experience as an applications analyst supporting multiple modules/applications, with direct experience in Epic build, testing, implementation, troubleshooting, and optimization strongly preferred. Experience supporting Epic Ambulatory workflows is preferred, including outpatient clinical documentation, provider workflows, orders, referrals, medication management, visit documentation, patient access workflows, charging, reporting, care coordination, and integrated clinical workflows. Experience with EpicCare Link workflows is preferred. Strong understanding of clinical application dependencies, workflow impacts, testing methodologies, interface and integration workflows, and coordination with technology, interface, data, reporting, operational, ambulatory, and clinical teams is required.

Work Environment: This position will spend 90% of time sitting while performing work in a standard office environment and 10% of time standing and/or walking while pushing, pulling, lifting, and/or carrying up to 50 lbs. This is role is considered a remote position with onsite presence as needed.

The job description is not designed or intended to cover or set forth a comprehensive listing of all activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Washington Regional reserves the right in its absolute discretion to change duties, responsibilities or activities or assign new duties, responsibilities, or activities at any time with or without notice. Employees may be directed to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically presented in this description.

title: Senior Director, Head of Pharmacovigilance Operations
description:
Senior Director, Head of Pharmacovigilance Operations

Build and lead the pharmacovigilance operations that carry Nurix's growing clinical portfolio toward commercialization. You'll own the end-to-end ICSR model, safety systems, vendor oversight, and inspection readiness, with the chance to set strategy while staying hands-on and to build the function and team from the ground up.

Position Description

The Opportunity

  • Report to the Head of PV and define and execute the short- and long-term PVO strategy, goals, and operating model in alignment with the PV department and corporate objectives
  • Grow, mentor, and develop the PVO team, setting priorities and ensuring coverage across a growing portfolio; partner with the Head of PV on departmental planning, headcount, and budget
  • Provide PVO updates and escalate risks, issues, and compliance trends to PV and executive leadership as appropriate
  • Oversee the end-to-end ICSR management framework (intake, processing, in-stream quality review, regulatory submission oversight, and retrospective quality review), ensuring timeliness, accuracy, and compliance with global regulations (21 CFR, EU GVP, ICH E2 series)
  • Define, monitor, and report case processing metrics (KPIs/KQIs), drive root cause analysis and resolution of quality or timeliness issues, and oversee the drug safety mailbox
  • Oversee SAE reconciliation with Clinical Operations and Data Management and Reference Safety Information (RSI) tracking and dissemination, and ensure PVO input into the safety content of clinical documents (protocols, ICFs, IBs/RSI, and CSRs)
  • Ensure the integrity of safety data outputs from the Global Safety Database for aggregate reports, signal assessments, health authority requests, and other safety needs
  • Oversee operational delivery of aggregate safety reports (e.g., DSUR, PBRER/PSUR), and partner with Medical Safety, Regulatory Affairs, and Biostatistics to support signal management and benefit-risk evaluation
  • Own the strategy, validation, and lifecycle management of the Global Safety Database (e.g., Argus or equivalent) and related PV systems, including configuration, upgrades, and E2B gateway/electronic submission
  • Lead system selection, implementation, and transition projects, including safety database migrations and vendor changes, and drive automation and process improvements such as reconciliation tools, intake portals, and reporting and analytics capabilities
  • Lead oversight of outsourced PV activities and the CROs and vendors that support them, establishing governance, KPIs/KQIs, scorecards, and performance reviews, and driving corrective actions when performance falls short
  • Own PV budget planning, forecasting, and invoice review, identifying opportunities for cost optimization without compromising compliance
  • Lead the strategy and management of PV Agreements and Safety Data Exchange Agreements (SDEAs) with license partners, collaborators, and distributors
  • Own PVO inspection readiness and launch readiness, and lead PVO participation in internal audits, vendor audits, and regulatory inspections, including front-room/back-room support and CAPA development and tracking through closure
  • Develop, maintain, and continuously improve PVO and compliance-related SOPs, work instructions, and process documentation, and monitor the evolving global regulatory landscape so PVO processes adapt to new requirements
  • Act as the senior PVO liaison to Clinical Operations, Data Management, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Biostatistics, and Medical Safety, and support PV input into due diligence, in-licensing, and business development activities as needed

What You’ll Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Nursing, or a related field required; an advanced degree (PharmD, MS, PhD, MBA) is preferred
  • Minimum of 12 years of pharmacovigilance/drug safety experience in biotech or pharma, including in a leadership role managing PV operations and people
  • Deep experience in PV operations and ICSR management across clinical development, with commercial readiness experience
  • Demonstrated experience building, scaling, or transforming PV operations, ideally in a growing biotech environment
  • Significant experience managing PV vendors and CROs, including KPI/KQI development, governance, and performance management
  • Experience owning PV budgets, forecasting, and invoicing
  • Experience leading or substantially supporting regulatory inspections and audits (FDA, EMA, or other health authorities), including CAPA management
  • Experience with safety database implementations, upgrades, or transitions
  • Proven experience authoring and governing SOPs, work instructions, and quality system documentation
  • Experience negotiating and managing PVAs/SDEAs with license partners
  • Strong leadership, coaching, and talent development skills, with the ability to build high-performing teams
  • Excellent communication and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively with executive leadership and cross-functional partners
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple products and priorities at once
  • Quality and compliance mindset with strong attention to detail
  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced, evolving environment, including through organizational change

Salary Range: $ $288,100 - $325,700

The posted range applies to roles based in the San Francisco Bay Area and reflects local market conditions. Where an offer lands within that range depends on the candidate’s relevant experience, technical expertise, and how their background aligns with the role’s requirements.

Location: Remote or Onsite – Brisbane, CA

Fit with Nurix Culture and Values

  • Strong team orientation; highly collaborative
  • Solutions and results-oriented focus
  • Hands-on approach; resourceful and open to diverse points of view

About Nurix Therapeutics

Nurix Therapeutics is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of targeted protein degradation medicines, the next frontier in innovative drug design aimed at improving treatment options for patients with cancer and inflammatory diseases. Powered by a fully AI-integrated discovery engine capable of tackling any protein class, and coupled with unparalleled ligase expertise, Nurix’s dedicated team has built a formidable advantage in translating the science of targeted protein degradation into clinical advancements. Nurix aims to establish degrader-based treatments at the forefront of patient care, writing medicine’s next chapter with a new script to outmatch disease.

title: Product Line Project Manager, Global Procurement
description:
Job Description:

The Product Line Project Manager, Global Procurement is the single point of contact for Procurement on assigned projects (NPDI, ETO, SFA, VAVE, sustaining). This is an individual contributor role responsible for establishing a resilient, cost‑effective, and scalable supply chain for new products by driving early supplier engagement, sourcing strategy execution, and procurement readiness throughout the NPDI phase‑gate process.

Responsibilities:

Project Ownership and Cross-Functional Alignment

  • Serve as the primary Procurement representative for assigned projects from early concept through production readiness.
  • Ensure procurement deliverables are planned, tracked, and executed in alignment with NPDI phase-gate requirements.
  • Represent Procurement at NPDI gate reviews, providing clear visibility into sourcing maturity, gaps, and mitigations.
  • Track and report key metrics such as cost, lead time, supplier performance, and launch readiness.
  • Partner closely with Engineering, Program Management, Commodity Management, Quality, and Operations teams to ensure sourcing strategies support overall project objectives.
  • Act as the primary escalation point for procurement related risks impacting cost, schedule, or supply resilience.

Early Supplier Engagement and Sourcing Strategy

  • Engage proactively with Engineering to understand component requirements early in the design process.
  • Engage suppliers early to assess technical capability, capacity, cost drivers, and lead time expectations.
  • Send early RFQs/RFPs ahead of design release and drive competitive bidding to achieve cost targets.
  • Facilitate collaboration between Engineering and suppliers to improve design for manufacturability, cost efficiency, and supply flexibility.
  • Establish strong supplier partnerships to drive innovation, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement.
  • Ensure sourcing approaches align with established commodity strategies and preferred supplier frameworks.

Cost, Risk, and Supply Chain Readiness

  • Support prototype, pilot, and pre-production builds, ensuring on-time availability of materials and services.
  • Ensure sourcing aligns with NPDI resilience expectations (multi‑source, regional manufacturing, avoidance of single‑point failures).
  • Use standardized BOM cost and risk tracking tools to maintain consistency and transparency.
  • Promote reuse of existing, qualified components and architectures where feasible to improve cost, availability, and time‑to‑market.
  • Drive sourcing maturity and readiness prior to product release to minimize disruption during ramp up and production.

Qualifications:

An ideal candidate will bring…

  • Experience in Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, or Supply Chain, supporting new product or engineering driven programs.
  • Experience working closely with Engineering teams during early product development.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to influence across functions without direct authority.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a matrixed, cross functional environment.
  • Experience supporting global supply chains and multiple manufacturing regions.
  • Familiarity with phase-gate or structured product development processes.

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Mechanical, Industrial, Electrical, Electronic), Supply Chain Operations and/or Business is preferred.

Physical Requirements:

  • No Special Physical Requirements

Environmental Demands:

  • No Specific Environmental Demands

Travel Time Required:

  • Ability to work overtime and travel (domestically and internationally) up to 15% is required.
  • Ability to work as per Project priorities and take after hours calls as necessary.

title: IT Help Desk Supervisor
description:
Overview

IT Help Desk Supervisor The RiverWoods Group is currently looking for an IT Help Desk Supervisor to join our team! This role will be based out of Durham, NH and will support our communities in Exeter, Manchester, and Durham. This is an onsite position however hybrid options exist for this role; must be able to work out of any location as needed and also must be able to respond to any onsite need quickly if required. The Help Desk Supervisor will be responsible for overseeing the IT Help Desk functions and Help Desk staff to ensure end users are receiving appropriate assistance in an effective and timely manner. This includes the responsibility of managing all procedures related to the resolution of end user service requests, including the monitoring, tracking, and coordination of Help Desk tickets. The Help Desk Supervisor will also contribute to problem resolution by assisting and coaching Help Desk staff when appropriate. The Help Desk Supervisor will also assist the System Administrator in the execution of higher-level support functions. At RiverWoods, you can expect to find a fun, energetic and friendly team of people who enjoy working together and creating excellence for our residents. Our staff, residents and trustees are partners in open communication in the development of our organization. We are a nationally recognized Fit Friendly company and a non-smoking campus. RiverWoods offers many programs that support employees' personal and professional development and provides internal career growth opportunities.

Responsibilities

  • Coordinate technician activities supporting computers, business applications, voice and data networks, and related hardware and peripherals.
  • Assign and prioritize tickets, monitor progress and backlog, review work for accuracy and timely completion, and coordinate daily staffing coverage within established schedules.
  • Serve as the first escalation point for IT Technicians, provide hands-on assistance with complex issues, and coordinate resolution with Systems Administrators, vendors, and other IT resources.
  • Train and coach staff on assigned responsibilities, new technologies, support procedures, communication, and customer service.
  • Provide regular feedback, and recommend development opportunities to the Director of IT.
  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, knowledge base articles, and standard operating procedures consistent with established IT standards.
  • Identify process improvement opportunities, recurring support issues, and end-user training needs; recommend improvements and implement approved changes.
  • Assist Systems Administrators with designated tasks and provide backup for specifically assigned responsibilities during absences; within established training, procedures, and access permissions.
  • Coordinate Help Desk assignments for projects initiated by IT Project Managers or the Director of IT, and communicate progress, dependencies, and resource concerns.
  • Prepare operational reports on ticket activity, service results, recurring issues, and staffing concerns, with recommendations for service or technology improvements.
  • Coordinate the daily work of support vendors and subcontractors, verify completion of assigned contractual work, and report performance concerns to the Director of IT.
  • Monitor computer supplies and equipment inventory, track purchases within approved limits, and recommend replenishment or replacement needs.
  • Participate in the IT on-call rotation with IT Technicians and provide after-hours and weekend support for identified mission-critical systems.
  • Develop skills in service measurement, staffing plans, budget monitoring, and vendor performance management to prepare for broader Help Desk leadership responsibilities.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Associate degree in information technology or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • At least three years of relevant technical experience supporting computing devices, business applications, voice and data networks, and Microsoft systems.
  • At least one year of experience leading, mentoring, or supervising staff. Leadership experience may overlap with the required technical experience.
  • Experience prioritizing support tickets, coordinating escalations, training staff, and developing technical documentation.
  • Experience with Active Directory, Microsoft 365, and Aruba switches is preferred but not required.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to explain technical issues clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to prioritize work, meet deadlines, and exercise sound judgment.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively, learn new technologies, and adapt to changing priorities.
  • Ability to remain calm and professional when addressing urgent issues, competing demands, and stressful situations.
