title: EL1 Senior Technical Network Engineer
description:
Australian Citizens residing in Australia only respond.

Job details

The Department of Finance is seeking one Senior Technical Network Engineer to provide specialist engineering, operational support and technical leadership for the Identity and Access Management Modernisation (IAMM) project. Duties will include:

  • designing, configuring, maintaining and troubleshooting enterprise network infrastructure and services;
  • providing senior expertise across LAN, WAN, routing, switching, wireless, remote access and network security technologies;
  • leading diagnosis and resolution of complex network incidents, performance problems and service degradation;
  • designing and implementing network segmentation and secure connectivity arrangements;
  • planning and delivering network upgrades, configuration changes and technology refresh activities;
  • providing technical assurance over network services delivered by managed service providers; and
  • developing network designs, diagrams, implementation plans, configurations and operational documentation.

The IAMM Project will modernise Finance's identity and access management capabilities and transition from legacy Microsoft Identity Manager (MIM) and Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) arrangements to a supported, cloud-ready architecture in which Microsoft Entra ID is Finance's primary identity directory and modern identity platform. SAP HR remains the authoritative source of workforce attributes. Downstream on-premises Active Directory accounts and services will be retained only where required for legacy dependencies, prior to MIM reaching end of extended support on 9 January 2029.

The project supports Finance's ICT and Digital Strategy, Cyber Security Strategy, 10-Year ICT Roadmap and Infrastructure Modernisation Program. The project will:

  • Establish Microsoft Entra ID as Finance's primary identity directory and modern identity platform.
  • Reduce reliance on MIM, AD FS and other legacy identity technologies.
  • Strengthen cyber security through modern authentication, Conditional Access, phishing-resistant MFA, Identity Protection and identity governance capabilities.
  • Integrate authoritative workforce identity sources and automate Joiner-Mover-Leaver processes.
  • Migrate supported applications from AD FS to Microsoft Entra ID and Single Sign-On.
  • Improve privileged access, access reviews, entitlement management, group governance, audit and reporting.
  • Provide supported, sustainable operating arrangements, documentation, training and knowledge transfer.

Support the Secure Access Service Edge (SASE), Laptop Refresh and Finance's broader move towards cloud services and Zero Trust architecture.

The Canberra-based role will provide specialist network engineering support across Finance's enterprise infrastructure and contribute to IAMM and related modernisation initiatives where network connectivity, secure access, cloud integration, remote access and service resilience are critical. The engineer will address network dependencies, constraints, risks and operational requirements and provide technical assurance throughout design, implementation and transition.

Note: SASE is being delivered by a concurrent multi-year program and will modernise how users securely access Finance systems and services, moving from traditional network-based access controls to an identity-centric, Zero Trust model.

Key duties and responsibilities

The successful candidate (as Senior Technical Network Engineer) will undertake the following duties and responsibilities:

  • Design, configure, implement, maintain and troubleshoot enterprise network infrastructure and associated services.
  • Provide senior technical practical expertise across LAN, WAN, routing, switching, wireless networking, remote access and network security technologies.
  • Manage and support network connectivity between Finance infrastructure, cloud environments, business systems and external services.
  • Lead diagnosis and resolution of complex network incidents, performance problems, application connectivity and service degradation issues.
  • Design and implement network segmentation and segregation to support security and risk management requirements.
  • Support enterprise firewall policies, secure connectivity, network access and related security services across multiple platforms, including Azure Firewall, Cisco Firepower, DDoS protection solutions and Web Application Firewalls.
  • Assess network vulnerabilities, technology lifecycle risks and configuration issues and implement/troubleshoot appropriate remediation.
  • Undertake network capacity, availability, performance and resilience analysis.
  • Plan and implement network upgrades, configuration changes and technology refresh activities.
  • Provide specialist network engineering input into infrastructure, cloud, cyber security and ICT modernisation initiatives that integrate enterprise networks with cloud and hybrid infrastructure – including Azure ExpressRoute, virtual networks and Application Gateway.
  • Develop and maintain network designs, diagrams, configurations, implementation plans, operational procedures and other technical documentation.
  • Support network monitoring, alerting and proactive identification of service issues.
  • Provide technical advice and assurance for network services delivered by external ICT service providers.
  • Work with technology vendors and managed service providers to investigate and resolve complex technical issues.
  • Support disaster recovery, business continuity and infrastructure resilience activities.
  • Identify opportunities to automate, standardise, simplify and improve network operations through such methods as infrastructure-as-code or configuration automation.
  • Provide technical guidance and knowledge transfer to Finance ICT personnel.

The candidate should address the expected outcomes of maintaining secure and reliable network operations, resolving complex incidents, remediating security and lifecycle risks, delivering agreed upgrades, improving documentation and monitoring, providing technical oversight of external providers and transferring knowledge to Finance personnel.

title: Vendor Admin Lead
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

We are looking for a Vendor Admin Lead to own vendor master data for our global Finance Operations team. Reporting to the Director of Global Accounts Payable, you will be the single point of accountability for who our vendors are and get paid: onboarding, bank-detail verification, supporting documentation vetting, data quality and the controls around all of it. Anthropic's vendor base is growing quickly across the US, Europe and Asia-Pacific, and a clean, verified vendor data is what keeps a fast-growing company scale with the necessary controls.

This role is deliberately separate from invoice processing and payments. You will control vendor records and bank details; you will not book invoices or move money. That separation is the point of the role, and you will own the SOX controls that enforce it and help design the access model that keeps it that way.

This is an opportunity to build a vendor-master function from the ground up and leverage process automation with Claude while supporting the team making AI safe.

Responsibilities

Supplier onboarding

  • Run intake for every new vendor and payee: validate completeness, collect and verify supporting documentation, and enable records in the ERP backbone system against agreed service levels

  • Validate supporting documents; set 1099-reportable and tax flags correctly

  • Confirm third-party risk and restricted-party screening before activation

  • Set up one-time and non-vendor payees with the right record type rather than forcing them through full onboarding

  • Partner with TPRM and IA teams on control requirements and continuous process improvement

  • 1099 annual reporting

Bank details and fraud prevention

  • Own every bank-detail setup and change; validate against a bank letter on letterhead or an approved equivalent (void checks, etc.)

  • Run independent callbacks per policy using contact details sourced independently of the request, and record the evidence

  • Validate international bank formats and addresses (IBAN, SWIFT/BIC, ABA, SEPA, BSB, IFSC, Japanese bank/branch codes)

  • Identify and escalate business-email-compromise attempts and other payment-fraud red flags

Data quality and maintenance

  • Maintain vendor structure: parent/child and remit-to relationships, entity and country records, contacts and payment terms

  • Lead vendor consolidation: eliminate duplicate vendors and bank accounts, execute merges and inactivations in batched, logged, reviewed changes

  • Run periodic health reviews for dormant vendors, stale bank letters, missing tax forms and incomplete records; drive 1099 and TIN readiness for year-end

  • Own periodic vendor deactivation campaigns

Controls and audit

  • Own the vendor-master SOX controls as the named control owner: maker-checker on every create and change, change-log review, evidence retained on every record

  • Prepare the periodic review of bank-detail changes paid, and address Internal Audit and external auditor requests

  • Partner with Finance Systems to design and maintain ERP security roles so vendor master, invoicing and payments stay separated

  • Flag any suspicious vendor set-up activity through the appropriate channels

Process, systems and improvement

  • Own vendor-master documentation, intake checklists, requester guidance and service levels

  • Serve as the vendor-data expert through process migrations, including data conversion and post-migration fixes

  • Partner on automation: AI-assisted intake validation, document extraction, bank-format checks and a vendor self-service portal

  • Report monthly on onboarding volume, cycle time, bank changes, exceptions and data quality, and use the data to improve the process

Minimum qualifications

  • 7+ years in vendor master or AP operations with 3+ years of ownership

  • Owned a vendor master in an ERP end to end — process, controls and data — across multiple entities and countries

  • Hands-on experience verifying bank details and preventing payment fraud: bank letters, independent callbacks, BEC red flags, international bank formats

  • Experience with vendor tax documentation: W-9/W-8 validation, TIN matching, VAT/GST IDs, 1099 flagging

  • Working knowledge of procure-to-pay controls — segregation of duties, maker-checker, change logs, audit evidence — and have performed or owned a SOX control

  • Led a vendor data cleanup, consolidation or ERP migration and can show the outcome

  • The confidence to hold the line with requesters, vendors and senior stakeholders under time pressure while staying clear and helpful

  • Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills with large datasets (dedupe, lookups, reconciliations) and exceptional attention to detail

Preferred qualifications

  • Workday Financials vendor management, and experience with Zip, Coupa or a similar procure-to-pay platform

  • SOX experience at a public company or one preparing to go public

  • Experience supporting APAC and EMEA vendors in a high-growth, multi-entity company

  • Experience designing or reviewing ERP security roles with a systems team

  • Comfort using AI tools to automate validation, follow-ups and reporting

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$190,000—$230,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

title: Mission Operations Engineer - New Grad (Summer 2027)
description:
About Nominal
Nominal is building the connected test and operations platform powering the world's most advanced hardware systems, from spacecraft and autonomous vehicles to next-generation defense programs. Our platform gives hardware engineering teams a single place to ingest data, analyze performance, automate test execution, and collaborate across every phase of development, so they can move faster without sacrificing safety or precision. We’re backed by Sequoia, General Catalyst, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, and Lightspeed. Our team draws from SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Applied Intuition, and other leading companies, united by a common mission: giving hardware engineers the tools to build the future with speed, safety, and confidence.

You'll train users, troubleshoot issues in real time, and build the relationships that turn a deployment into a long-term partnership.



🚀 What you’ll do

  • Write code to ingest and normalize customer data from test stands, DAQs, telemetry streams, and other hardware sources
  • Build custom apps, dashboards, and workflows on Nominal's platform for each customer's specific needs
  • Own outcomes for a set of customer accounts: run discovery to understand their test problems, then deliver solutions that stick
  • Build trusted relationships with engineers and operators, and train their teams as they bring Nominal into daily use
  • Debug issues across the stack in real time, and know when to solve something yourself versus pull in the broader team
  • Turn patterns you see across customers into clear input for the product and engineering teams



🎯 Reach out if…

  • You're graduating in Summer 2027 or sooner and are interested in a full-time position
  • You have hands-on experience with hardware systems — test stands, robotics, aerospace, automotive, or similar — through internships, personal projects, research, or coursework
  • You can write code (Python or similar) to work with real-world data, whether that's parsing sensor logs, building data pipelines, or automating analysis
  • You communicate clearly and can explain technical ideas to people who aren't engineers
  • You're comfortable working through open-ended problems in unfamiliar environments
  • You're willing to travel occasionally to be on-site with customers
  • You have a genuine interest in hardware testing and the industries Nominal serves

Client Onboarding

Client Offboarding

  • Organize unapproved videos within a clearly labeled "Not Yet Approved" folder.

Editor & Production Support

  • Organize specialized footage, including Hero Shots, Rapid Fire content, and other assets that may be used in future projects.

  • Work proactively with the post-production team to prevent production backlogs and keep client work moving efficiently.

Requirements

  • Exceptional attention to detail and organizational skills.

  • Strong ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, and client deliverables simultaneously.

  • Proactive approach to identifying and resolving issues before they create delays.

  • Ability to work independently and take ownership of recurring responsibilities.

  • Strong follow-through and ability to track outstanding work across multiple contributors.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means our post-production pipeline stays organized and predictable. Client deliverables are accurately tracked, folders and assets are easy to navigate, outstanding work is followed up on, and editors have what they need to keep production moving.

You don't need to wait for someone to tell you that something is falling behind—you notice it, communicate it, and help get it back on track.

title: SDM - Photos Alexa Experience, Amazon Photos On Devices Team
description:
Are you ready to revolutionize how millions of customers interact with their personal photos through voice? We're seeking a Software Development Manager to own the end-to-end voice experience stack for Amazon Photos, bridging the gap between Alexa endpoints and the backend services that power seamless customer experiences. You'll lead the orchestration of voice, touch, and agent interactions across the Photos ecosystem, solving complex technical challenges at the intersection of Alexa and Photos.

This is more than a management role, it's an opportunity to reimagine architecture that has been optimized for delivery but needs evolution for long-term scalability. You'll drive innovation in how customers interact with their photos across all Alexa endpoints including devices, web, and mobile. Your work will directly impact how customers perceive and interact with their most personal content, making this a stage for breakthrough innovation in voice-enabled experiences.

Key job responsibilities
- Define and execute the technical vision for voice orchestration between Alexa systems, Photos backend services, and Alexa endpoints, ensuring low-latency, deterministic interactions across all customer touchpoints
- Lead the backend modularization initiative to create clear component boundaries, reduce operational overhead, and enable faster feature delivery across the Photos voice experience stack
- Build and nurture a high-performing team of 10+ engineers through strategic hiring, performance management, mentoring, and career development while fostering an inclusive culture of innovation
- Collaborate with Product Managers, Software Development Managers across Photos and Alexa, and Technical Program Managers to balance tactical delivery with strategic architectural improvements
- Drive architectural decisions for end-to-end intent orchestration, partnering with cross-functional teams to migrate APL components and establish unified agent architecture that scales across devices, web, and mobile endpoints

A day in the life
You'll start your day reviewing system metrics and orchestrating priorities across your team of engineers. Mornings often involve design reviews where you challenge technical approaches and guide architectural decisions for voice intent handling. You'll meet with Product Managers to align on roadmap priorities and with peer Software Development Managers from Photos and Alexa teams to resolve cross-team dependencies. Afternoons are dedicated to one-on-ones where you coach engineers on technical growth and career development. You'll also identify resourcing challenges and work with Technical Program Managers to ensure your team has the support needed to deliver high-impact features that enhance how customers interact with their photos through voice.

About the team
Our mission is to enable customers to discover, control, and personalize Photos on devices through fast, reliable voice and direct interactions. We own end-to-end intent orchestration across Alexa and Photos systems, acting as the control plane that routes customer requests from voice, touch, remote, and text inputs to the appropriate backend services. We ensure interactions are low-latency, deterministic, and predictable across all devices.

We're focused on building a unified agent architecture that provides consistent Alexa experiences regardless of endpoint. Our 2026 strategic initiatives include the bcakend modularization effort to create better team autonomy and the migration of APL components into on-device applications. This allows us to invest more deeply in voice orchestration innovation. We collaborate closely with backend, device platform, front-end teams to mitigate dependencies and deliver seamless experiences. Join us in shaping the future of how customers experience their personal content through voice technology.

You will build MCP-enabled AI interfaces that let AI agents create and run data pipelines on Spektr at 99%+ success rate, directly shaping how GenAI discovers and consumes data across Amazon Ads. You will design and operate high-scale Java services on AWS-native infrastructure (Spark, EMR Serverless, Kinesis, Step Functions), processing petabytes of data daily at 99.9% availability. You will also drive deployment automation, replacing manual release cycles with CI/CD pipelines that accelerate delivery velocity for a platform serving Tier-1 advertising data systems.

A day in the life
- Focus on core engineering opportunities to guarantee system availability that matches our data growth
- Work with a skilled team of engineers, managers and decision makers to consistently meet customer demand

About the team
The mission of the Ads Datalake team is to provide data that helps the advertising organization make informed analyses and decisions for our customers and to determine and deploy investments for future growth via a set of central and unified products and services.
Our team focuses on simplicity, usability, speed, compliance, cost efficiency and enabling high-velocity decision making so our customers can generate high quality insights faster.

description:

Nominal is building the connected test and operations platform powering the world's most advanced hardware systems, from spacecraft and autonomous vehicles to next-generation defense programs. Our platform gives hardware engineering teams a single place to ingest data, analyze performance, automate test execution, and collaborate across every phase of development, so they can move faster without sacrificing safety or precision. We're a fast-moving team that owns problems end-to-end, works across disciplines, and thrives at the intersection of hardware and software.

We serve top-tier commercial and defense customers, from autonomy leaders like Anduril and Shield AI to next-generation aerospace teams like Hermeus and REGENT, and performance engineering teams like Pratt Miller Motorsports, alongside mission partners within the U.S. Navy and U.S. Air Force on programs where failure isn’t an option. We’re backed by Sequoia, General Catalyst, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, and Lightspeed. Our team draws from SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Applied Intuition, and other leading companies, united by a common mission: giving hardware engineers the tools to build the future with speed, safety, and confidence.

We're looking for students with solid engineering fundamentals who are interested in a 12-week Summer 2027 internship and on track to graduate by Summer 2028.

You'll see what it takes to deploy software into a live test environment, write code that gets customer data flowing, and turn what you learn into product feedback that shapes what we build next.

title: Software Engineer (AI Data Engineering)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SOFTWARE ENGINEER (AI DATA ENGINEERING)

Be a member of the Artificial Intelligence Data Engineering Software team, building AI-powered tools and automation that solve real engineering problems for our launch vehicles and spacecraft.

Our team builds software that takes recurring, time-consuming work off engineers' plates so they can focus on hard engineering, from automated review of flight and test data to AI agents that help engineers prepare for missions and investigate anomalies. Your work will directly accelerate rapid reuse of the Falcon launch vehicle, support the world's largest satellite communication and AI constellations, and contribute to the development of the world's largest rocket capable of sending humans to Mars.

You will work side-by-side with engineers across avionics, propulsion, structures, and more to find where their time goes and build tools that give it back, using agentic AI systems, MCP servers, RAG-based search, data pipelines over large telemetry datasets, and traditional automation where it is the right answer. You will own problems end-to-end: scoping the solution with the engineers who have the problem, rolling it out, measuring the time it saves, and maintaining it as the vehicle and processes evolve.

Aerospace experience is not strictly required - we are looking for smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on an inspiring mission.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Partner directly with engineering teams to identify their most time-consuming, repetitive, or error-prone work, then design and build tools that automate it
  • Build automation that processes large volumes of engineering data, including telemetry, hardware design databases, configuration files, and manufacturing and test records, to automate data review, flag anomalies, and surface insights
  • Design agentic AI systems, multi-agent workflows, and MCP servers that let engineers query, analyze, and act on data across many internal systems
  • Integrate tools into CI/CD pipelines, mission workflows, and review/sign-off processes so automation runs where engineers already work
  • Build internal web dashboards that give engineers a clear view of mission status, open work, and data review results
  • Rapidly prototype and iterate, then take tools to a production-grade, maintainable state
  • Thoroughly test and validate all tools, including evaluating AI outputs against known-good results, so engineers can trust them in a flight-critical environment
  • Prioritize work by return on investment and track the engineering hours saved

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, data science, engineering, math, or physics; OR 4+ years of professional experience building automation for practical engineering use cases in lieu of a degree
  • 1+ years of experience in software engineering with a focus on automation tools and/or AI integrations (professional and personal projects are applicable)
  • 1+ years of programming experience in Python

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Track record of building tools that engineers or other end users actually adopted, including gathering requirements directly from users and iterating on their feedback
  • Comfort processing and analyzing large engineering or scientific datasets (time-series telemetry, sensor data, logs, etc.) using tools such as pandas and NumPy
  • Built code or configuration generators that turn a source of truth (design databases, spreadsheets, schemas) into validated outputs
  • Hands-on work building complex agentic AI systems and multi-agent workflows, including prompt and context engineering, tool/function calling, and MCP servers or agent skills
  • Ability to design evaluations for LLM-based tools, and the judgment to know when a deterministic script is a better fit than an AI model
  • Skilled at integrating with many systems through REST APIs, and quickly learning unfamiliar internal tools and data sources
  • Working knowledge of relational (PostgreSQL), non-relational, and vector databases, with strong SQL skills
  • Full-stack experience building web applications or dashboards (e.g., React/TypeScript frontends with Python backends such as FastAPI or Flask)
  • Proficiency developing on Linux, with a solid understanding of Git, testing, CI/CD, and monitoring
  • Familiarity deploying containerized applications using Docker and Kubernetes
  • Familiarity with hardware engineering concepts (electrical schematics and wiring, sensors, propulsion, controls, or test and manufacturing processes), or a background as a hardware or test engineer who moved into software
  • Strong communication skills and ability to explain technical tradeoffs to engineers in other disciplines
  • Self-directed and comfortable owning ambiguous problems from initial idea through long-term maintenance

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed
COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 1: $125,000.00 - $160,000.00
Level 2: $145,000.00 - $195,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

The primary responsibilities of this role include designing and developing an operational intelligence analytics solution using technologies like Solace/ Kafka, C#/ Java, Kubernetes, and MongoDB, while enhancing existing analytics applications. The role also involves supporting real-time applications, delivering customer insights, developing front-end solutions with modern frameworks, and collaborating with UX/UI designers and stakeholders to create functional, user-friendly interfaces. This position offers the chance to contribute to innovative solutions, supporting the Club's mission to deliver world-class wagering services.

  • Develop, enhance, and maintain frontend components to visualize and interact with real-time data analytics, addressing new or changing requirements
  • Contribute to the design and architecture of a user-friendly interface for the messaging framework, ensuring effective integration with Solace
  • Collaborate with vendor delivery teams to ensure their contributions align with the frontend design and user experience goals
  • Liaise with other development teams and stakeholders to build intuitive and functional components that meet user requirements and business needs

title: Recreation Supervisor
description:
RECREATION SUPERVISOR - for more detail please see job brochure.


DEFINITION


Under general direction, plans, organizes, supervises, and evaluates recreation programs, facilities, and services, including youth and adult sports, camps, classes, aquatics, special events, senior services, facility rentals, and other community recreation programs. Supervises part-time, contract, and volunteer staff while ensuring safe, high-quality recreation services. Oversees the daily operation of the City's aquatic facility, recreation programming, budgets, scheduling, and administrative functions. Evening, weekend, and holiday work may be required based on operational needs.

SUPERVISION RECEIVED AND EXERCISED


Receives direct supervision from the Recreation Manager. Exercises direct supervision over part-time staff, seasonal employees, contract instructors, and volunteers.

CLASS CHARACTERISTICS


This is the supervisory classification, performing recreation supervisory duties in the Recreation Department. Assignments are performed in support of the Recreation Department.

EXAMPLES OF TYPICAL JOB FUNCTIONS (Illustrative Only)

Management reserves the right to add, modify, change, or rescind the work assignments of different positions and to make reasonable accommodations so that qualified employees can perform the essential functions of the job.


  • Oversees the daily operation of the City's aquatic facility, including staffing, scheduling, safety, risk management, regulatory compliance, and operational readiness.
  • Ensures the City's aquatic facility operates in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local health and safety regulations; develops and implements operational procedures to promote a safe environment for participants and staff.
  • Supervises, schedules, trains, evaluates, and provides direction to part-time staff, seasonal employees, contract instructors, and volunteers. Participates in recruitment, hiring, coaching, performance evaluations, and disciplinary processes.
  • Develops, implements, and enforces safety and risk management procedures for recreation programs and aquatic operations; ensures proper documentation and follow-up.
  • Prepares and administers contracts for recreation programs and services; coordinates with contract instructors and service providers; monitors contract compliance; and submits agreements to the Recreation Manager for review and approval.
  • Oversees budgets for assigned programs and events. Develops budget recommendations, monitors expenditures, completes cost recovery analyses, and recommends future budget needs based on program goals and operational priorities.
  • Assists with departmental planning, goal setting, policy development, and implementation of new recreation programs and services.
  • Addresses participant concerns, resolves conflicts, and exercises independent judgment in resolving operational issues.
  • Plans and coordinates City-sponsored special events, including scheduling, logistics, vendor coordination, staffing, volunteer coordination, permits, and interdepartmental communication.
  • Assists the Recreation Manager with the City's Special Event Permit process for low-impact events, including application review, coordination, and communication with event organizers.
  • Plans, organizes, supervises, and evaluates a variety of recreation programs, which may include youth and adult sports, fitness classes, senior programming, aquatics, contract classes, seasonal camps, special events, and facility rentals.
  • Collaborates with other City departments to coordinate logistics, facility operations, special events, emergency response, and departmental initiatives.
  • Tracks attendance, registration, budget, and cost recovery data for assigned programs; prepares reports and recommendations to support operational and budget decisions.
  • Coordinates scheduling and use of recreation facilities and athletic fields for City programs, public rentals, and community groups.
  • Oversees marketing and promotion of recreation programs by coordinating program guides, flyers, digital communications, social media, website content, and community outreach.
  • Builds and maintains relationships with the school district, local preschools, community organizations, contractors, and partner agencies to promote programs, encourage participation, and support collaborative efforts.
  • Performs duties independently using sound judgment and initiative while operating within established policies and procedures.
  • Provides friendly, professional customer service in person, by phone, and via email; assists with complex concerns and represents the department in a positive and professional manner.
  • Uses digital tools for registration, facility scheduling, marketing, communication, staff scheduling, and program administration.
  • Demonstrates a commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion by supporting accessible, welcoming programs that reflect the needs of Calistoga's diverse community.
  • Contributes to a positive, team-oriented work culture that reflects Calistoga's commitment to service, community, and professionalism.
  • Participates in trainings, workshops, and other professional development opportunities to maintain and enhance skills related to recreation management and service delivery.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

Knowledge of:

  • Recreation registration systems, staff scheduling software, marketing platforms, and the administration, configuration, and maintenance of those systems.
  • Program evaluation, data tracking, cost recovery analysis, and program trend monitoring.
  • Administrative principles and practices, including planning, budgeting, and supervision.
  • Principles and practices of employee supervision, including work planning, assignment, review and evaluation, and the training of staff in work procedures.
  • Modern office practices, methods, financial programs, and computer equipment and applications related to the work.
  • English usage, grammar, spelling, vocabulary, and punctuation.
  • Functions, principles, and practices of recreation services.
  • Principles and practices of aquatic facility operations, risk management, and regulatory compliance.
  • Applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulatory codes, ordinances, and procedures relevant to assigned areas of responsibility.
  • Techniques for providing a high level of customer service by effectively dealing with the public, contractors, community organizations, and City staff.



Ability to:

  • Plan, organize, supervise, and evaluate recreation programs, facilities, operations, and assigned staff, including providing training, direction, and leadership.
  • Interpret, apply, and explain policies, procedures, and regulations.
  • Prepare, administer, and monitor program budgets.
  • Assess and prioritize situations while remaining calm and using sound, independent judgment.
  • Obtain necessary information from individuals in stressful or emergency situations.
  • Compile and summarize information to prepare accurate, clear, and concise reports.
  • Organize work, set priorities, and meet critical deadlines.
  • Evaluate emergency situations and act decisively and effectively to resolve the situation.
  • Use tact, initiative, prudence, and independent judgment within general policy and legal guidelines in sensitive situations.
  • Establish and maintain positive and effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.
  • Communicate effectively in person, over the telephone, and in writing.
  • Oversee recreation facilities and aquatic operations while ensuring compliance with applicable health and safety requirements.
  • Possess flexibility to work with varying personalities, age groups, and work schedules.

Education and Experience:

Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain the required qualifications would be:

Four years of increasingly responsible experience in one or more of the following areas: recreation, aquatics, community services, parks, youth and community programs, hospitality, or a related field that demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform the duties of the position.

Licenses and Certifications:

  • Possession of a valid California Driver’s License.
  • Possession of, or ability to obtain within six (6) months of hire, CPR, First Aid, and AED certification.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Lifeguard certification.
  • Lifeguard Instructor (LGI) certification.
  • Bilingual English/Spanish skills.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Must possess mobility to work in a recreation and standard office setting and use standard office equipment, including a computer; vision to read printed materials and a computer screen; and hearing and speech to communicate in person, before groups, and over the telephone. Finger dexterity is needed to access, enter and retrieve data using a computer keyboard or calculator and to operate standard office equipment. Positions in this classification occasionally bend, stoop, kneel, reach, push, and pull equipment. Employees must possess the ability to lift, carry, push, and pull materials and objects necessary to perform job functions.

Employees must possess the ability to lift, carry, push, and pull materials and objects up to 50 pounds and standing for periods of time at a minimum of 60 minutes at one time.



ENVIRONMENTAL ELEMENTS



Employees work both in an office and open environment with moderate noise levels, cold and hot temperature conditions, and direct exposure to the sun. Employees may interact with upset staff and/or public and private representatives in interpreting and enforcing departmental policies and procedures.

The City of Calistoga is an Equal Opportunity Employer. In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, Calistoga will provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities and encourages both prospective and current employees to discuss potential accommodations with the employer.

title: Data Engineer (MS Fabric)
description:
Build great solutions. Solve real problems. Work with people who know their craft.

We're a global technology consultancy helping organisations solve complex challenges through modern software solutions, data platforms, AI and intelligent automation.

We're looking for a hands-on Data Engineer with MS Fabric experience to join our NZ team. Whether you're an experienced contractor or looking for your next permanent opportunity, we're open to finding the right fit.

This is an opportunity to work on meaningful client engagements, solve interesting technical challenges and help shape how modern data engineering and AI are applied in real-world environments.

We're not just looking for someone who knows the technology. We want someone who knows how to use it to deliver great outcomes for customers.

What does the role look like?

You'll spend your time doing what good engineers enjoy: building, problem-solving and delivering solutions that work.

Working across Microsoft Fabric engagements, you'll turn business requirements into reliable, scalable data solutions. One day you might be developing pipelines and transformations, the next troubleshooting a data issue, optimising a Lakehouse architecture or working with analysts to deliver meaningful business insights.

But this isn't a role where you're handed a ticket and disappear until it's complete.

You'll work closely with engineers, technical leads and clients, asking good questions, challenging assumptions and taking ownership of your delivery. We value people who communicate clearly, bring ideas to the table and understand the business problem behind the technical work.

We're also embracing AI-native engineering and want people who are actively exploring how AI and agentic tools can improve development, productivity and quality.

What we're looking for

Strong, hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience is essential. This isn't a role for someone looking to learn Fabric from scratch.

Technically, you'll bring:

  • Practical experience with Microsoft Fabric, including Lakehouses, Warehouses, OneLake, Pipelines and Notebooks.
  • Strong SQL and PySpark skills, including data transformation and troubleshooting.
  • Experience with medallion architecture (Bronze/Silver/Gold) and Delta Lake.
  • Familiarity with Power BI, Fabric Semantic Models and DirectLake.
  • Experience with Git, Azure DevOps or GitHub, and CI/CD practices.
  • At least 2 years' relevant engineering experience, with demonstrated delivery capability.

Experience with dbt, data governance, Microsoft Purview or relevant Microsoft certifications is a bonus.

Beyond the technical skills...

We're a consultancy, and how you work matters just as much as what you know.

You'll be someone who:

  • Communicates well: Builds trust with clients and explains technical concepts clearly.
  • Takes ownership: Follows through, delivers quality work and doesn't need constant direction.
  • Thinks commercially: Understands the business problem, not just the technical task.
  • Adapts and solves problems: Thrives on variety, takes initiative and brings solutions, not just problems.
  • Embraces innovation: Actively explores GenAI and modern engineering practices.
  • Works well with others: Collaborative, approachable and comfortable engaging with different stakeholders.

Consulting or professional services experience is highly valued, but the right mindset and proven client-facing delivery experience matter more.

Why Provoke?

You'll join a collaborative team working with clients across different industries and markets, tackling diverse technical challenges and helping shape the next generation of data and AI solutions.

We value curiosity, accountability and people who get things done. You'll have the flexibility to work your way, support from experienced colleagues and opportunities to keep learning and growing.

A few important details:

  • Location: Anywhere in New Zealand. You must be NZ-based.
  • Engagement: Contract or permanent.
  • Working arrangements: Some availability required to collaborate with US-based clients (Pacific Time).

Interested?

If you're a capable Microsoft Fabric engineer who enjoys solving problems, working with clients and taking ownership of delivery, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now and let's talk.

title: Email Deliverability Specialist
description:
About

Over 9,000 companies — from scrappy startups to global brands — use our platform to send billions of emails, push notifications, in-app messages, and SMS every day. powers automated communication that people actually want to receive. We help teams send smarter, more relevant messages using real-time behavioral data.

About the role

Hi, my name is Caitlin, Senior Manager, Technical Support at , and I'm looking for an Email Deliverability Specialist to join our deliverability program within Technical Support. You'll help customers reach the inbox by diagnosing sending issues, advising on best practices, and guiding senders through an email ecosystem that keeps changing.

You'll be one of several deliverability experts on a team that shares knowledge across Technical Support, so your work reaches well beyond your own queue. You'll partner with Customer Success, Technical Support, and Engineering: taking customer calls, equipping CSMs for customer conversations, working through complex technical cases alongside Engineering, and turning what you see in tickets into documentation, training, and better processes.

You'll thrive here if you think about the health of the whole program, enjoy improving how work gets done, and are equally comfortable digging into a detailed case and having a direct conversation with a customer about acceptable use.

What we value

Empathy and curiosity: You approach every customer with patience and a desire to dig deeper, especially when a conversation gets uncomfortable.

Clarity: You explain complex technical concepts simply and help others do the same.

Collaboration: You build strong partnerships across Support, Customer Success, and Engineering, and you treat customer outcomes as a shared goal.

Thinking at scale: You look at how we do things today and see what could work better for the whole organization, then you help make it happen.

Continuous learning: You stay ahead of evolving standards and see change as a chance to improve how we work.

What you'll do

  • Act as a trusted deliverability advisor to customers, handling complex cases through to full resolution and leading customer calls when a conversation needs it
  • Audit sender setup and monitor reputation across IPs and domains, using authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and BIMI, DNS configuration, and provider tools like Google Postmaster Tools, Yahoo Sender Hub, and Microsoft SNDS to diagnose blocklists, spam traps, and engagement drops
  • Work through highly technical issues with Engineering, taking ownership of the investigation first and sharing trends from customer cases with Product and Engineering
  • Identify acceptable use policy violations and spam complaints, hold clear and direct conversations with customers about compliance, and keep up with evolving standards (Gmail and Yahoo sender requirements, CAN-SPAM, GDPR)
  • Equip CSMs and Technical Support with the knowledge to handle deliverability conversations, through coaching, documentation, and training
  • Improve processes, tools, and one-to-many resources, such as help content, Academy course and proactive customer guidance, so deliverability support scales across the organization

What we're looking for

  • 2-4 years of experience in email deliverability at a mid-size or large ESP, B2B SaaS company, or marketing automation platform, with exposure to deliverability at scale
  • Deep understanding of email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI) and infrastructure (SMTP, MTAs, DNS), with the technical comfort to work through complex issues with Engineering
  • Proficiency with provider data feeds (Google Postmaster Tools, Yahoo Sender Hub, Microsoft SNDS) and third-party deliverability monitoring tools like Everest, MXToolbox, or similar, and the analytical skill to turn bounce, engagement, and blocklist data into clear recommendations
  • Working knowledge of email compliance and acceptable use standards, and comfort having direct conversations with customers who are sending outside of them
  • Experience building or improving processes, documentation, or training that help a support or deliverability team scale
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including comfort leading customer calls and simplifying technical concepts for any audience
  • Located in the United States or Canada
  • Bonus: participation in deliverability communities (M3AAWG, ESPC, or similar) and experience partnering with Customer Success teams

Compensation & Benefits

We believe in transparency. Starting salary for this role is $102,000 - $110,000 USD (or equivalent in local currency) depending on experience and subject to market rate adjustment.

We know our people are what make us great, and we're committed to taking great care of them. Our inclusive benefits package supports your well-being and growth, including 100% coverage of medical, dental, vision, mental health, and supplemental insurance premiums for you and your family. We also offer 16 weeks paid parental leave, unlimited PTO, stipends for remote work and wellness, a professional development budget, and more.

See full benefits here →

Our Process

No gotchas, no trick questions - just a clear, human process designed to help both of us make an informed decision.

  • 30-minute video call with a Recruiter
  • 45-minute video call with the Hiring Manager
  • 60 minute Case Study Review call with Cross-Functional Partners
  • 30 minute video call with potential Team Member
  • 30 minute final video call with Senior Leadership

All final candidates will be asked to complete a background check and employment verifications as part of our pre-employment process.

recognizes the stifling impact of systemic injustice on diverse communities. We commit to using our influence to increase inclusion and equity within the tech industry. title: Reliability Engineer
description:
A Plant Reliability Engineer is responsible for ensuring the continuous, efficient, and safe operation of plant equipment and systems. They develop and implement strategies to minimize unplanned downtime, extend asset life, and improve overall equipment effectiveness (OEE).

Key Responsibilities

  • Reliability Strategy Development: Design and implement preventive and predictive maintenance programs to reduce equipment failures and unplanned downtime.
  • Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Lead investigations into equipment failures and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
  • Asset Management: Monitor and analyze equipment performance data to identify trends and prioritize maintenance activities.
  • Maintenance Planning: Collaborate with maintenance and operations teams to schedule and optimize maintenance activities.
  • Continuous Improvement: Drive reliability improvement initiatives using methodologies such as RCM (Reliability-Centered Maintenance), FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis), and Six Sigma.
  • Capital Projects Support: Provide reliability input during the design and commissioning of new equipment or plant modifications.
  • KPI Tracking: Monitor key reliability metrics such as MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures), MTTR (Mean Time to Repair), and equipment availability.
  • Training & Mentoring: Support and train maintenance technicians and operators on reliability best practices.

Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, or Industrial Engineering (or related field).
  • Experience: 3–7 years of experience in a manufacturing or process plant environment.
  • Technical Skills: Proficiency in CMMS, vibration analysis, thermography, lubrication management, and other predictive maintenance tools.
  • Certifications (preferred): Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE), CMRP (Certified Maintenance & Reliability Professional).
  • Soft Skills: Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills; ability to work cross-functionally.

The base salary for this position is between $110,000 to $130,000.

title: GTM Analytics Lead
description:
About the role

This role leads GTM Analytics within the Revenue Strategy function and reports directly to the Head of Revenue Strategy & Operations. You will own how Thatch measures GTM performance, understands channel economics, and governs the data foundation behind commercial decisions.

The role covers three areas: GTM performance and channel economics, GTM data strategy and governance, and analytical support for forecasting, planning, and executive reporting. Your work is the analytical engine behind all three.

You set the analytical agenda for your areas. You decide which questions matter most, focus effort on the highest-value work, and turn findings into recommendations that change where Thatch invests. You will partner closely with Marketing, Data Science, Finance, and RevOps.

What you'll do

GTM Performance and Channel Economics

  • Build performance frameworks that show GTM health across the full customer lifecycle, from lead through close, onboarding, retention, and expansion.
  • Own the framework for comparing Thatch's GTM motions: win rates, CAC, payback, and conversion by segment, geography, and channel, plus broker attribution and quoting performance.
  • Partner with Marketing on funnel and attribution, with Data Science on modeling and segmentation, and with Finance on unit economics and scenario analysis.
  • Spot emerging trends early and recommend where to invest and where to pull back, including clear tradeoffs.
  • Prioritize the analytics roadmap by business impact.

GTM Data Strategy and Governance

  • Own the GTM data strategy and set priorities for the integrity, scalability, and evolution of the GTM team’s data foundation, in partnership with Data Science.
  • Define and govern core GTM metrics, business logic, and data standards so every standing number is consistent, auditable, and reconciles with Finance.
  • Set governance for definitions, lineage, quality, and usage in partnership with RevOps, Data Science, Engineering, and Finance.
  • Define GTM business requirements before technical work begins. RevOps and Engineering keep ownership of technical build.
  • Prioritize GTM data initiatives and make sequencing recommendations based on dependencies and business impact.
  • Make sure data assets support critical use cases, including forecasting, pipeline management, planning, compensation, and performance measurement.
  • Drive adoption of governed metrics and BI across GTM teams.

Forecasting, Planning, and Reporting Support

  • Build and maintain the analytical inputs behind the forecast: pipeline snapshots, coverage, stage conversion, and pacing.
  • Supply the data and models that feed target setting, capacity planning, and compensation analysis.
  • Deliver complete, accurate analytics for board, QBR, and MBR materials on every cycle.
  • Flag when the data signals risk to the forecast or plan.

Strategic Decision Support

  • Break down ambiguous GTM questions, combining data, financial implications, and operational context.
  • Lead high-stakes segment, channel, and territory analyses from problem definition through recommendation.
  • Present findings, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to senior leadership.

Background we're looking for

  • Experience. 5 to 8 years in GTM analytics, RevOps, BizOps, strategy, or FP&A at a high-growth B2B company, with direct partnership with sales, marketing, and finance leadership.
  • Technical depth. Expert SQL. Deep experience with sales and product telemetry data, mainstream business intelligence tools.
  • Data governance. Experience owning metric definitions and data standards, and turning business requirements into technical specs in a modern data stack.
  • Systems thinking. You understand dependencies across CRM, warehouse, BI, and GTM execution, and how a field change flows through to a board metric.
  • Commercial judgment. Command of GTM and SaaS metrics, including win rates, conversion, attribution, CAC, payback, and retention.
  • Cross-functional influence. You align Marketing, Data Science, Finance, and RevOps on shared definitions and priorities without formal authority.
  • Executive communication. You deliver answers, not dashboards, and turn complex analysis into clear recommendations.
  • Ownership. You own the numbers, catch errors first, and raise risks early.

Experience we’d be particularly excited about

  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment, balancing speed and rigor with limited resources and evolving data

What to expect

We interview rigorously based on integrity, talent, and drive; the trust we display in our teammates from day 1 is a reflection of the confidence we have in this process. We aim to evaluate the things you’ll be doing every day as best we can, and we move quickly. Here's what to expect:

  • 30 minute video meeting with our founders to discuss your approach to culture and our operating principles

title: Cybersecurity Analyst
description:
Overview

The Cybersecurity Analyst supports day-to-day operations with strong experience in the NIST Risk Management Framework (RMF) to also support the security authorization, compliance, and continuous monitoring of federal information systems. This role provides technical guidance to management, system owners, and engineering teams on cybersecurity risk, control implementation, and authorization activities. In this position, the Cybersecurity Analyst will develop and maintain RMF documentation, conduct risk and vulnerability assessments, support security control assessments, and help systems obtain and maintain an Authority to Operate (ATO). The position requires knowledge of FISMA, NIST publications, federal cybersecurity policies, and agency-specific guidance, along with sound judgment, strong technical writing, and the ability to translate requirements into actionable security practices.

Work Location: Washington, DC

Work Arrangement: Onsite

Clearance: Must have an active Top Secret clearance and able to obtain a SCI

Responsibilities

  • Lead RMF life-cycle activities, including system categorization, control selection and validation, assessments, authorization, and continuous monitoring.
  • Develop and maintain RMF documentation, including SSPs, SAPs/SARs, POA&Ms, risk assessments, PIAs, and continuous monitoring artifacts.
  • Conduct risk assessments, control gap analyses, and vulnerability reviews; evaluate impact and recommend risk-based remediation.
  • Coordinate with system owners, network engineers, and administrators to implement and document NIST SP 800-53 controls and support daily operations.
  • Support the ATO process by preparing authorization packages, tracking findings, coordinating assessor requests, and briefing stakeholders on residual risk and remediation.
  • Monitor compliance with FISMA, NIST, agency policies, and contractual cybersecurity requirements.
  • Support internal and external audits through evidence collection, control mapping, interviews, and corrective action tracking.
  • Analyze vulnerability scans, security tool outputs, and operational data to identify trends, validate control effectiveness, and support continuous diagnostics and mitigation.
  • Provide cybersecurity guidance and training to system owners, administrators, and users on requirements, secure practices, and documentation.
  • Develop cybersecurity policies, procedures, standards, and governance processes to strengthen compliance and risk management.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in IT, Computer Science, or a related field preferred; equivalent combination of education, certifications, and relevant experience will be considered.
  • Active Top Secret Clearance with ability to obtain a SCI.
  • 3–5 years of Cybersecurity experience supporting RMF, compliance, assessments, or ISSO functions in federal or regulated environments.
  • Knowledge of NIST SP 800-37/53, FISMA, FIPS 199/200, and related federal guidance.
  • Knowledge of DISA CCIs and NIST SP 800-53 mapping.
  • Experience maintaining RMF documentation, authorization packages, and continuous monitoring.
  • Ability to assess risk, interpret scans, prioritize remediation, and communicate technical risk.
  • Familiarity with vulnerability management, SIEM, endpoint security, CDM, and eMASS or similar platforms preferred.
  • Strong technical writing, documentation, presentation, audit, and executive reporting skills.
  • Ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and collaborate across teams.

Preferred Qualifications (must have at least 2):

  • CompTIA Security+ CE
  • ISC2 CGRC
  • CompTIA CySA+
  • CISSP or CISM
  • DoD Manual 8140.3
  • IAT Level II

Benefits:

  • Competitive salary: $190,000 -200,000
  • Paid Time Off & Holiday Pay
  • Medical Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • Disability, Life Insurance, and AD&D
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Pre-Tax 401K and/or After-Tax Roth IRA (with employer matching contribution)
  • Tuition and Technical Training Reimbursement

  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Collaborative and dynamic work environment

title: Director, Community Programs
description:
About the California Academy of Sciences

Founded in 1853, the California Academy of Sciences is a globally renowned, AZA-accredited non-profit scientific and cultural institution located in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park. Home to a world-class planetarium, aquarium, rainforest, research institute, and natural history museum—all under one living roof—our mission is to regenerate the natural world through science, learning, and collaboration.

Our living collection reflects Earth’s vast biodiversity, consisting of nearly 60,000 animals representing over 800 species. Our research collections are the largest west of the Mississippi, spanning nearly 46 million plants, animals, fossils, and cultural artifacts from across the globe and throughout history. Our diverse team includes leading biodiversity scientists, educators, storytellers, designers, and communicators who are passionate about advancing knowledge and catalyzing action through science and storytelling.

Whether you're conducting research behind the scenes or engaging the public on the museum floor, your work will help connect people to the natural world and empower them to protect it.

About the Opportunity

Reporting to the Chief of Education and Learning, the Director of Community Programs is responsible for the strategy, conceptualization, implementation, and assessment of programs at the Academy offered to local communities including internships for high school and undergraduate students, volunteers, and San Francisco residents. The Director works most closely with managerial leaders in the Education and Learning Division, and collaborates with teams from other Divisions such as IBSS, MarComms, Exhibits, and Guest Experience to ensure that we are catalyzing the Academy’s mission and meeting short and long goals for the Education Division. As a member of the Academy Leadership Team, this individual will participate in strategic-level decision making for the Academy as a whole, in addition to representing the Academy externally to board members, donors, and partners.

We are committed to ensuring diversity, equity, accessibility, and inclusion are intrinsic to Academy culture and operations, from recruitment and retention to science and advocacy. Explore Our Commitment to Racial Equity to learn about our intentional engagement of traditionally excluded groups in an effort to spark interest in or foster pathways to scientific careers.

Organizational Culture

When you join the California Academy of Sciences, you become part of a mission-driven community that values curiosity, collaboration, and innovation, and celebrates its accomplishments together. Staff share a commitment to executing a new strategic plan that will strengthen the organization's financial foundations, cultivate a vibrant internal culture, and foster smart growth to secure the Academy’s future.

We hope you are inspired by what we do and are motivated to contribute to our mission. The Academy is looking for candidates who do great work, and we know they may come from a number of different backgrounds and experiences. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every qualification for the position.

This position is based in San Francisco, California. The specific onsite/hybrid schedule for this position is listed below.

Key Responsibilities

  • In partnership with the Chief of Education, devise, articulate, and implement an innovative strategy and vision for 21st century learning experiences offered to high school and undergraduate students, local residents, and San Francisco diasporas, to maximize our impact with local youth and communities, increase our position as leaders of innovative learning experiences, and meet the educational impacts set for our audiences such as increased science learning, climate and biodiversity literacy, and sustained commitment to agency for the natural world.
  • Creatively and strategically expand the Academy’s portfolio of community programs by providing project and staff management, along with state-of-the-art and foundational resources, structures, and expert guidance to the Social and Environmental Justice, Education Volunteer, Internship & Mentorship Education, and Careers in Science teams as they innovate new impactful ways to interpret the Academy’s mission and deliver transformative education.
    • Guide and support the Social and Environmental Justice team as it designs, implements, and evaluates impactful and innovative programming offered through the lens of Social and Environmental Justice, with key audiences being San Francisco local diasporas and communities, and California-based Native American youth.
    • Guide and support the Education Volunteer team and its portfolio of educational volunteer opportunities, including the Docent Program, Education Research Volunteers, and other approved volunteer programs.
    • Guide and support the Education Internships & Mentorships team, which partners with the IBSS Internships & Mentorships team and the Dean of Education to increase internship opportunities in social sciences research.
    • Guide and support the Careers in Science team and its programming with junior and senior high school students.
  • Research, evaluate, and propose new pedagogy, media, technologies, formats, tools, and modalities to create and deliver human-designed transformational learning experiences and programs for members of local communities through internships, mentorships, volunteerism, and community educational convenings.
  • Collaborate with IBSS and Exhibits leadership to explore, identify, and consolidate pathways to integrate Academy’s original scientific work into programming for communities and youth that is offered on the museum floor and that centers climate and biodiversity literacy and action.
  • Enhance the quality and modalities of authentic, transformative learning experiences in which local communities and San Francisco residents from underrepresented diasporas can participate---before, during and post-visit, creating holistic experiences that inspire individuals of all ages and backgrounds to take action towards regeneration of the natural world and about the human-nature connection.
  • Effectively leverage AI as a support tool for developing educational programs and for science learning.
  • Inspire, direct, lead, mentor, and manage approximately 10 staff from 3 distinct teams, each composed of managers and staff of various levels and experiences
  • Allocate and manage the budget for the department and supervise adequate management of each team’s budget, including tracking all expenses, creating spending plans, and guiding staff to adequately request and assign resources.
  • Collaborate with Membership and Marketing and Communications to effectively develop and market community and youth programs to help increase public awareness, participation, and support for the Academy.
  • Help lift the Academy’s profile and impact - locally and beyond - as an innovative educational leader by developing strong external strategic program partnerships.
    • Develop and maintain these external partnerships with organizations and donors that will support the community and youth engagement strategy of the Academy and our attendance and utilization goals.
    • Develop and implement success metrics and evaluation tools to assess the alignment of designed programs with Transformative Education, measure learning goals set for community and youth audiences, and desired external impact.
  • Identify and materialize opportunities for growth for the department’s staff in order to increase their expertise and knowledge on niched areas and expose them to new emerging trends.
  • Act as a thought partner with the Director of Events, Director of Science Operations, and Manager of Academy Volunteers, on strategy level decisions regarding programming and experiences as educational volunteerism, internships, mentorships, and convenings.
  • Follow all Academy safety regulations and complete all People and Culture (PACT) assigned trainings
  • Support the Academy’s mission, vision and Academy-wide initiatives
  • Other duties as assigned

Minimum Qualifications:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education and/ or Experience:

The ideal candidate will possess a combination of the following education and/or equivalent experience

  • BA/BS; preferably in science and/or environmental education, and 14+ years’ experience.
  • Preferred MA/MS in science, science communication, informal education, museum-based education, youth programming or the equivalent of 12+ years’ experience.
  • Minimum of 7-10 years experience in designing and delivering informal science and action-focused education, including a minimum of 2 years’ working experience in programs that deliver informal educational programming to community and youth audiences.
  • Combined minimum of 7-10 years’ supervisory, leadership experience over teams of informal educators and public-facing staff and volunteers at a zoo or aquarium (AZA accredited institution) or at a science center or museum.
  • 5+ years’ managing volunteers and/or volunteer programming.
  • 3-5 years’ experience in securing funding for public programming through grant writing and/or donor solicitations.
  • 3-5 years’ experience in developing and cultivating multi-organizational partnerships focused on family or general public science or environmental learning.
  • 2-3 years’ of special event and/or festival programming experience desired.

Skills & Abilities:

  • Expert in developing innovative and engaging science content and solutionary-based learning experiences for all ages for use by museums, aquariums, z planetariums and/or other informal science learning organizations.
  • Passionate and skillful conceptualization and design of programs that center communities and individuals, particularly those historically marginalized.
  • Demonstrated knowledge and track record of working with San Francisco-based communities and youth, with a deep understanding of the challenges and opportunities to engage with these audiences.
  • Expert in developing learning experiences that integrate complex science within accessible content, experiences, and interactions that strengthen the human-nature connection and increase commitment to agency and stewardship.
  • Excellent leadership skills and commitment to positive team dynamics including developing leadership and growth opportunities within teams.
  • Demonstrated experience in developing, implementing, and evaluating exciting in-person programs that merge informal science with action-oriented information, targeted for all ages and types of audiences.
  • Ability to review content for all the public, through a scientific lens to confirm accuracy and rigor, and to provide feedback on structure and content when needed.
  • Outstanding budget management skills for individual teams and department level operations, including creating financial projections for proposed projects and programs.
  • Ample knowledge of, and demonstrated implementation of, progressive science interpretation, science communication, and solutionary-design approaches for public, volunteer, youth, and internship programs.
  • Excellent communication skills: employs tact and diplomacy to communicate complex issues to highly diverse audiences.
  • Demonstrated commitment to safety, specifically in regards to working with youth and volunteers.
  • Ability to develop, operationalize, and implement program strategy.
