title: Security Supervisor
description:
Security Supervisor

Wage: $20.00/ hour

Schedule: 1st shift, 5:30am-1:30pm

Experience Required:

  • Security Experience
  • Computers
  • Customer service

  • 2 Years of Supervisor Experience


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  • Functions as a supervisor of Security Officers, Lead Officers, and other company personnel assigned to one or more posts at client site(s); acts to ensure that all post orders are followed, that established rounds are completed, and that required reports are filed; notifies proper authorities and client in emergency situations.
  • Coaches and disciplines personnel as appropriate; seeks advice from company management or designated representatives as appropriate; meets personally with employees and documents coaching and disciplinary actions.
  • Trains Security Officers and other company personnel; reviews post orders and other details of assignments with subordinates.
  • Assists in the submission of payroll and personnel information to the company as designated.
  • In conjunction with company management or designated representatives ensures adequate coverage of all posts and positions.
  • Prepares, files, and submits various reports as required.
  • Inspects posts as scheduled and meets with subordinates to outline tasks and responsibilities.
  • Meets with client representatives as scheduled or as needed to provide assurance that all security requirements are being met and to provide quality customer service.
  • As assigned, in accordance with applicable company policies and procedures and in compliance with state and federal laws, carries out supervisory duties that can include some or all of the following: interviewing, orienting and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; coaching and appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems; and, making hiring and termination recommendations.
  • May perform the duties of a Security Officer in accord with post orders and company policy.

Education/Experience: High School Diploma or G.E.D. and 2 years of related experience, or an an equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to perform the essential functions of the job, as determined by the company. Minimum 2 years of experience in retail preferred.

Competencies (as demonstrated through experience, training, and/or testing):

  • May be required to hold and continue to meet the requirements for any applicable state, county and municipal license for Security Officers.
  • Knowledge of security operations with an emphasis on patrol, inspection and response services.
  • Knowledge of supervisory practices and procedures.
  • Ability to provide positive direction and motivate performance.
  • Understanding of a variety of security and safety devices and controls.
  • Ability to learn quickly and carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or diagrammatic form.
  • Ability to track and maintain schedule assignments.
  • Ability to be an effective team member.
  • Ability to maintain professional composure when dealing with unusual circumstances.
  • Courteous telephone manner.
  • Ability to adapt to various sites and changes in post procedures.
  • Ability to write routine correspondence, including logs and reports.
  • Good organizational skills.
  • Strong customer service and results orientation.

  • Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact effectively with clients, at various social levels and across diverse cultures.

WORKING CONDITIONS (Physical/Mental Demands)

With or without reasonable accommodation, requires the physical and mental capacity to perform effectively all essential functions. In addition to other demands, the demands of the job include:

  • Maintaining composure in dealing with authorities, executives, clients, staff and the public, occasionally under conditions of urgency and in pressure situations.
  • May be exposed to stressful situations, such as challenging individuals who are in or approaching an unauthorized area.
  • Must undergo and meet company standards for background and reference checks, controlled substance testing, and behavioral selection survey, in addition to any mandatory licensing requirements.
  • Directing and disciplining staff in a positive manner.
  • May be required to work overtime without advance notice.
  • Required ability to handle multiple tasks concurrently.
  • Keyboarding, basic computer usage, and operating controls.
  • Seeing, hearing, speaking and writing clearly in order to communicate with employees and clients, observe and report incidents, and direct others.
  • Frequent sitting, standing, and walking, which may be required for long periods of time, and may involve climbing stairs and walking up inclines and on uneven terrain.
  • Occasional reaching with hands and arms, stooping, kneeling, crouching and crawling.
  • Frequent lifting and/or moving up to 10 pounds and occasionally up to 25 pounds.
  • Close vision, distance vision, and ability to adjust focus.
  • Regular use of vehicle for the performance of duties.
  • On occasion may be required to perform stressful and physical activity.
  • Depending upon assignment may be exposed to inclement weather or be required to work in environments or under conditions that require the use of protective gear and devices and/or awareness of personal safety and safety of others.
  • May be exposed to or required to handle sensitive and confidential information.

description:
PPG's Aerospace Business is looking for a passionate Quality Control/Assurance Chemist at our Los Angeles, CA location! Your expertise will help determine the conformance or non-conformance of materials, using your understanding of material formulation. title: Task Force Director of Food and Beverage
description:
JOB SUMMARY

The Task Force Director of Food and Beverage is a highly mobile leadership position responsible for providing hands-on interim leadership, operational coverage, performance improvement, and strategic Food & Beverage support at Company properties on assignment. This role partners closely with hotel General Managers, Executive Chefs, property-level F&B leaders, and the property's designated Executive Committee leader to ensure consistent execution, financial performance, and guest experience standards across all outlets, including restaurants, bars, banquets, catering, and room service, while maintaining consistent communication with the Corporate Director of Food and Beverage.

Primary duties consist of performing office or non-manual work directly related to management or general business operations. Work includes the exercise of discretion and independent judgment with respect to matters of significance.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

  • Manages and supports all aspects of Food & Beverage operations in accordance with Company and property standards.
  • Oversees and directs restaurant, bar/lounge, banquet, catering, room service, and other food and beverage operations as applicable to each property.
  • Serves as the Food & Beverage lead during leadership vacancies, property openings and transitions, operational turnarounds, training initiatives, and other special projects as assigned, providing interim leadership and operational coverage.
  • Implements and maintains a consistent service and management philosophy that guides leaders and Team Members and strengthens the guest experience.
  • Builds innovative, memorable dining and event experiences while developing knowledgeable, engaged front-of-house teams.
  • Drives financial performance through disciplined P&L oversight, budgeting, and forecasting, and monitors labor costs, cost of sales, scheduling, staffing, inventory, and daily service execution.
  • Conducts operational walk-throughs, property tastings, and quality evaluations to ensure consistency and excellence; maintains an active presence throughout restaurants, bars, kitchens, and event spaces; leads line-ups and department meetings and participates in BEO meetings.
  • Leads, coaches, and develops restaurant and Food & Beverage supervisors and managers; identifies talent and creates opportunities for growth and advancement.
  • Assists with interviewing, hiring, training, work assignments, performance management, mentoring, recognition, and problem resolution.
  • Partners with hotel leadership to meet or exceed budget expectations, with particular focus on payroll, labor productivity, cost of sales, and overall profitability.
  • Partners with Executive Chefs and culinary leaders on menu development, pricing, product quality, and operational execution.
  • Builds strong relationships with guests, meeting planners, in-house clients, and contracted groups to drive repeat business and guest loyalty.
  • Analyzes financial and operational performance metrics, P&Ls, forecasts, and operating results; identifies performance gaps and implements corrective action plans to achieve or exceed established goals.
  • Partners with Operations and Sales leadership and the property's designated Executive Committee leader to drive achievement of scorecard Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and property performance goals.
  • Communicates property progress, risks, wins, and recommended next steps to the Corporate Director of Food and Beverage and Company leadership on a consistent basis.
  • Regular, reliable attendance and punctuality is a key component of this position.
  • Maintains a professional appearance in accordance with Company standards; wears the appropriate uniform or attire.
  • Maintains open and effective communication with team members and management.
  • Attends and participates in team meetings.
  • Adheres to established safety and emergency procedures and protocols, this includes Company, federal, and state specific regulations and guidelines.
  • Completes all required Company training/compliance courses as assigned.
  • Adheres to Company standards and maintains compliance with all policies and procedures.
  • Performs other related duties and responsibilities as assigned.

EDUCATION

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited university or equivalent in related field.

EXPERIENCE

  • A minimum three (3) years of experience in related field required.
  • A minimum three (3) years of supervisory experience in the hospitality/hotel industry required.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Oversees and coordinates the department's activities, with a focus on supervisory and organizational goals. While a portion of the time may involve performing tasks similar to those of direct reports, the primary responsibilities are related to management and coordination. Analyzes and resolves issues, establishes work methods, ensures regulatory compliance, and maintains productivity. Uses judgment within established procedures and policies to make appropriate decisions and take necessary actions.

Specific supervisory duties include, but are not limited to the following:

  • Determines and creates policies, procedures, and manuals for direct reports.
  • Establishes objectives and goals for the team.
  • Assigns, monitors, and reviews work; evaluates direct report's performance.
  • Recruits and interviews.
  • Orientates and trains.
  • Issues corrective action and makes recommendations for termination.
  • Investigates and resolves concerns and complaints.
  • Creates department work schedules.
  • Approves time records and time off requests; submits payroll.
  • Proactively assesses risk to establish systems and procedures to protect organizational assets.
  • Ensures compliance with safety regulations.
  • Develops and oversees the department's budget.
  • Ensures accurate and efficient management of inventory.

LICENSES & CERTIFICATIONS

  • Food Handler's Card - must obtain as required by applicable state or local regulations.
  • Alcohol Awareness Training Certification - must obtain as required by applicable state or local regulations.

SKILLS & ABILITIES

This position requires the capability to understand and follow both oral and written directions, as well as the ability to communicate effectively with others in English and interact successfully with internal and external customers.

  • Comprehensive culinary knowledge, including regional and international cuisine trends and evolving guest preferences.
  • Strong knowledge of wine, spirits, and beverage program development.
  • Deep operational expertise across both front-of-house and back-of-house environments.
  • Advanced understanding of F&B operational metrics, including COGS, labor management, sales metrics, KPIs to measure operational outcomes, and P&L analysis.
  • Strong understanding of financial concepts, budgeting, and forecasting.
  • Skilled in leading change initiatives and influencing cross-functional teams to implement best practices and performance improvements.
  • Proficient in time management; the ability to effectively organize and manage multiple priorities.
  • Recognizes an emergency situation and takes appropriate action.
  • Emotional intelligence and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build strong working relationships with team members at all levels.
  • Skilled in building and motivating a team, fostering a collaborative environment and inspiring high performance.
  • Analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Performs well with frequent interruptions and/or distractions.
  • Able to communicate appropriately and effectively with all levels of management and external stakeholders.
  • Business acumen, including but not limited to financial management, budgeting, cost control, and revenue optimization.
  • Ability to effectively listen, understand, and resolve challenges and concerns from management, team members, and/or customers (internal/external).
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills to include coaching, counseling, and mentoring.
  • Able to identify and seize revenue-generating opportunities while effectively managing costs and resources.
  • Knowledge of key industry trends, best practices, regulations, and the current industry landscape.
  • Proven ability to drive revenue growth, optimize costs, and achieve financial targets.
  • Able to engage diplomatically and effectively with third party operators and owners, empathizing, and reacting appropriately to partner feedback and helping resolve issues where necessary.
  • Basic math skills.
  • Proficient in Google Docs/Microsoft Word.
  • Proficient in Google Sheets/Microsoft Excel.
  • Proficient in Gmail/Microsoft Outlook.
  • Proficient in Micros Symphony, Aloha, and Toast.
  • Ability to adjust effectively to evolving work environments and shifting customer (internal/external) requirements.
  • Able to maintain a positive and professional working environment.
  • Fosters a culture of excellence.
  • Able to work effectively in a culturally diverse environment and support diversity and inclusion within the organization.

TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS

  • 75% travel required.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

  • Reaching: Extending hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction.
  • Standing: Particularly for sustained periods of time.
  • Walking: Moving about on foot to accomplish tasks. Specifically, for long distances or moving from one work site to another often.
  • Pushing: Using upper extremities to press against something with steady force in order to thrust forward, downward, or outward.
  • Pulling: Using upper extremities to exert force in order to draw, haul, or tug objects in a sustained motion.
  • Lifting: Raising objects from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position-to-position. Specifically, if it occurs to a considerable degree and requires substantial use of upper extremities and back muscles.
  • Grasping: Applying pressure to an object with the fingers and palm.
  • Feeling: Perceiving attributes of objects, such as size, shape, temperature or texture by touching with skin, particularly that of fingertips.
  • Talking: Expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word. Those activities in which they must convey detailed or important spoken instructions to other workers accurately, loudly, or quickly.
  • Hearing: Perceiving the nature of sounds at normal speaking levels with or without correction. Ability to receive detailed information through oral communication and to make the discriminations in sound.
  • Hands to Fingers: Picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working, primarily with fingers rather than with the whole hand as in handling.
  • Repetitive Motion: Substantial movements (motions) of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers.
  • Close Vision: Clear vision at 20 inches or less. Required to perform an activity such as preparing and analyzing data, transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, extensive reading or visual inspections.
  • Color Vision: Ability to identify and distinguish colors.
  • Focus Ability: Ability to adjust the eye to bring an object into sharp focus.
  • Light Work: Work that requires frequent walking or standing and may involve some pushing, pulling, or lifting of objects weighing up to 20 pounds. Positions that are mostly seated may still be considered light if they require use of arms or legs for controls or equipment that demand greater effort than sedentary work.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Excessive Noise: Exposure to sufficient noise (caused by machines, music, voices, etc.) that warrants shouting in order to be heard above ambient noise level.

title: Portfolio Management Associate
description:
ACX is a vertically integrated private real estate investment firm with primary offices in Stamford, Connecticut and Denver, Colorado. The firm focuses on grocery-anchored and necessity retail shopping centers in the Top 25 MSAs across the United States. ACX’s growing nationwide portfolio includes 26 properties totaling approximately 4 million square feet, approaching $1 billion in assets under management. The firm is actively investing in value-add and core-plus transactions on behalf of its institutional investors.



Position Overview



ACX is seeking a full-time Portfolio Management Associate to help strengthen the firm's investor reporting, portfolio management and capital-markets capabilities. The Portfolio Management Associate will play a central role in ensuring that investors and leadership receive accurate, timely and decision-useful information about portfolio performance. This role will report to the Head of Investor Relations and manage recurring reporting processes, monitor debt and portfolio performance, coordinate information across operating teams, and provide forward-looking analysis to support investment and capital decisions.

This is a high-ownership role for someone who combines strong financial and analytical skills with the ability to drive work across multiple teams and consistently deliver against deadlines.

What You Will Obsess Over



Serve Investors with Accuracy & Responsiveness
Deliver high-quality reporting and respond reliably to investor, lender and diligence needs.



Maintain Portfolio & Debt Intelligence
Understand portfolio performance, capital structures and upcoming obligations well enough to surface risks and opportunities early.



Drive Reporting & Planning Execution
Coordinate people, information and deadlines so recurring reporting, budgeting and planning processes happen accurately and on time.



What Success Looks Like

A successful Portfolio Management Associate:

  • Delivers investor and lender reporting accurately and on schedule.
  • Produces work that is thoroughly reconciled and rarely requires correction or clarification.
  • Keeps debt obligations, covenants, maturities and extension options visible well in advance.
  • Understands material portfolio variances and can clearly explain what is changing and why.
  • Drives internal reporting deadlines without requiring senior leadership to chase inputs.
  • Anticipates upcoming portfolio and capital decisions and provides useful analysis before decisions become urgent.
  • Progressively takes full ownership of recurring workstreams and reduces the amount of day-to-day oversight required from senior leadership.



Core Responsibilities

  • Manage the firm's portfolio and investor-reporting calendar, including internal deadlines and coordination across Asset Management, Leasing, Construction, Property Management, Accounting and other teams.
  • Prepare quarterly investor reports, capital account statements, portfolio dashboards and annual meeting materials.
  • Respond to investor requests, due diligence questionnaires and consultant submissions and maintain diligence materials and the investor data room.
  • Support fundraising activities through portfolio analytics, track-record information, investor materials and diligence responses.
  • Monitor loan covenants, compliance requirements and lender reporting.
  • Track debt maturities, extension options and interest-rate exposure and support refinancing and financing activity.
  • Coordinate with lenders, servicers, counsel and internal teams on financing documentation and lender requests.
  • Analyze asset- and portfolio-level performance against underwriting, business plans and budgets and explain material variances.
  • Build and maintain models supporting valuations, hold/sell analyses, refinancing scenarios and capital planning.
  • Support annual budgeting, reforecasting, business-plan updates and Board/Investment Committee materials.
  • Produce forward-looking analysis that helps leadership identify capital needs, portfolio risks and value-creation opportunities.



Requirements

  • 4+ years of relevant experience in real estate private equity, real estate investment banking, commercial real estate lending, portfolio management or institutional investor relations.
  • Strong Excel and financial-modeling skills; Argus experience is a plus.
  • Strong understanding of commercial real estate economics, including NOI, leases, valuations and capital structures.
  • Strong written communication skills and experience preparing institutional-quality materials.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage detailed recurring processes and deliverables with a high degree of accuracy.
  • Ability to coordinate and influence colleagues across functions without relying on direct reporting authority.
  • Strong judgment, curiosity and attention to detail.
  • Ability to move between immediate execution needs and longer-term portfolio considerations.
  • Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, real estate or a related field.
  • Retail real estate experience preferred.


Compensation and Benefits

  • Base salary range: $115,000 - $125,000, commensurate with experience
    Annual performance bonus
  • Benefits: Health, Dental, Vision insurance; Life and AD&D, Short Term Disability and Long Term Disability insurance; 401(k); Paid Time Off; Paid Parental Leave, Fertility Reimbursement Program


How to Apply

Please submit your resume along with “10 Things We Should Know About You.” Any format is fine.

Applications Close January 4th, 2027

We offer medical, dental, and life insurance, parental leave for you, your spouse/domestic partner, and children, and a 401k with company match. Check out our benefits pages for more information.

description:
The Diving Superintendent will work closely with the Global Diving Manager and will be expected to progressively take on greater responsibility within the diving department as experience is gained with company equipment, procedures, systems, and operations.

Travel may include project support and visits to other company facilities or depots to inspect diving equipment, review maintenance and certification status, verify equipment-control processes, assist with repairs, and help maintain consistent diving-equipment standards throughout the company.

This is a hands-on position requiring strong commercial diving, mechanical, equipment-maintenance, and warehouse experience.

Position Responsibilities

  • Oversee and perform inspection, maintenance, repair, testing, certification, and general readiness of commercial diving equipment maintained at the Fort Lauderdale facility.
  • Coordinate preventive maintenance, annual inspections, equipment certifications, repairs, and return-to-service requirements in accordance with manufacturer recommendations, company procedures, and applicable industry standards.
  • Prepare diving equipment for project mobilizations, including equipment selection, load-out coordination, verification of required equipment, and tracking of equipment assigned to projects.
  • Inspect and process diving equipment returning from projects, ensuring required cleaning, repairs, maintenance, certification, documentation, restocking, and equipment accountability are completed before return to service.
  • Maintain accurate equipment records, inspection documentation, certifications, inventories, and asset status using company-approved asset tracking systems and other operational software.
  • Provide technical support and troubleshooting for diving equipment and assist facility or project personnel with equipment maintenance and operational readiness.
  • Assist with warehouse operations, equipment handling, shipping and receiving, loading and unloading, and movement of project equipment as required.
  • Support continuous improvement of diving-equipment maintenance procedures.

Technical Experience

  • Candidates should have substantial hands-on experience with commercial diving equipment, including:
  • Surface-supplied diving systems
  • Kirby Morgan commercial diving equipment (including helmet and first stage inspection, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair)
  • Low-pressure breathing-air compressors (including compressor repair, maintenance, and operational testing, filtration systems, and volume tanks)
  • Diving umbilicals and breathing-air hoses (including hose inspection and pressure testing)
  • Diving communications systems
  • Pneumatic and hydraulic diving tools
  • Diving equipment inspection, maintenance, certification, and recordkeeping

Physical Requirements:

This position operates in warehouse, marine, and project environments and requires standing, walking, bending, kneeling, crouching, reaching, and climbing to inspect, maintain, and handle diving equipment. The employee must be able to use hand and power tools and lift, carry, push, or pull equipment and materials, with assistance or mechanical lifting equipment when needed. Work may involve outdoor conditions, uneven surfaces, heat, humidity, and noise while wearing required personal protective equipment. title: Skipper

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. Xometry’s digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity.

Senior Software Engineer (Thomas)

Thomasnet, part of Xometry, is the industrial platform where millions of buyers find and source from North American manufacturers and suppliers.

We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer to join Thomas engineering. Thomas is moving from a traditional supplier directory to AI-assisted sourcing, where buyers describe what they need and the platform does the matching. You will build and maintain the systems behind that shift, from the product experiences buyers and suppliers use every day to the AI-powered features at the center of our strategy. You will work closely with a product manager and peer and senior engineers.

How You'll Contribute

  • Hands-on technical leadership. Lead by example by actively coding, reviewing, and troubleshooting. Set good coding patterns and designs for the team.
  • Lead projects end-to-end. Own the design and delivery of features within your team, from problem to production and largely independently, including the AI-powered capabilities at the center of our strategy: features that use LLMs, retrieval, and search, with the evaluations and guardrails that keep them accurate and safe.
  • Mentorship and code review. Guide and mentor engineers on the team; do thorough code review and raise the bar for how others review.
  • Operational excellence. Own testing and reliability for what you ship. Deliver software that meets customer expectations and business timelines.

What You'll Bring

  • 6+ years of software development experience, focused on outcomes over output, with a habit of helping shape the team's direction rather than only building to spec.
  • Strong full-stack skills that transfer to our stack: backend services in TypeScript and Node.js with GraphQL APIs, a React and Next.js frontend, PostgreSQL, and search such as OpenSearch. Comparable experience in another modern stack counts just as much; prior experience with our exact tools is not required.
  • Hands-on experience building AI-powered product features: LLM applications, retrieval-augmented generation, vector search, or search relevance. We hire AI-native engineers who build with these tools and judge their output rigorously, whatever the specific frameworks.
  • Bonus points: experience with multimodal (image and text) embeddings and search, agent orchestration frameworks (e.g. LangGraph, LangChain), and fine-tuning or adapting models for a domain.
  • A fast learner with high agency who works fluently in an AI-native development environment and shares what they learn. We are all still learning how to build with AI, and we want people who help the team learn faster.
  • Strong execution, debugging, and communication skills. Prioritizes unit and integration testing.

title: Security Shift Supervisor
description:
Security Shift Supervisor

**Security leadership experience is A+**


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Education/Experience: High School Diploma or G.E.D. and 2 years of related experience, or an an equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to perform the essential functions of the job, as determined by the company. Minimum 2 years of experience in retail preferred.

Competencies (as demonstrated through experience, training, and/or testing):

title: Administrative/Buyer Assistant Position
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:

This position provides administrative, organizational, and operational support to the Purchasing Department. The role coordinates daily office activities, maintains documentation and contract files, supports contract intake and routing, and ensures clear, timely communication with internal stakeholders and external vendors. As a backup Buyer, the position assists with purchasing tasks, including preparing requisitions and purchase orders, obtaining quotes per policy thresholds, following up with suppliers, and ensuring adherence to County procurement procedures and audit requirements.

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES:

Essential Functions

The duties and responsibilities of this position include, but are not necessarily limited to:

  • Provide comprehensive administrative support, including scheduling, recordkeeping, mail processing, document preparation, and filing to ensure smooth department operations.
  • Maintain organized electronic and physical files, and manage department logs, trackers, and routine reports.
  • Assist with contract intake, tracking, routing for review and approval, and maintain complete and accurate contract files.
  • Monitor workflow milestones and provide timely status updates to staff and stakeholders.
  • Serve as a backup Buyer and prepare and submit requisitions and purchase orders in the County ERP system.
  • Coordinate supplier communications for quote requests, confirmations, delivery follow‑ups, and assist in routine purchasing decisions in alignment with County procurement procedures.
  • Resolve routine procurement issues such as documentation gaps, purchase order modifications or cancellations, receiving updates, and support audit readiness by ensuring complete and compliant records.
  • Ensure compliance with County procurement policies, contract administration procedures, records retention standards, and audit requirements.
  • Assist with drafting, updating, and organizing department standard operating procedures.
  • Support responses to Right to Know Requests.
  • Communicate professionally with internal departments and vendors to facilitate timely, accurate information sharing and issue resolution.
  • Provide logistics support and assist with special projects as assigned by the Director and/or Deputy Director.

MINIMUM EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Associate’s Degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, or closely related subject.
  • Four years of experience in advanced administrative office experience.
  • Any equivalent combination of experience and training which provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities.

MINIMUM KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Demonstrate strong organizational and follow‑through skills, with the ability to plan, prioritize, and complete assignments independently.
  • Detail oriented, proactive, and able to manage multiple tasks effectively.
  • Working knowledge of ERP systems for requisitions, purchase orders, receiving, and reporting, or a strong willingness and ability to learn.
  • Analytical thinking and sound judgment, with the ability to interpret and consistently apply basic procurement procedures.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, with the ability to produce clear, accurate documents and spreadsheets.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills, along with strong interpersonal abilities to build effective working relationships with staff, County departments, vendors, and the public.
  • High ethical standards and a commitment to confidentiality.
  • Ability to follow written and verbal instructions with precision and initiative.
  • Ability to meet deadlines and manage time effectively.
  • Ability to handle stress.
  • Physical presence in the office is required.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Work involves standing, walking, sitting, lifting, carrying, talking, hearing, and reaching with hands and arms. Vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 40 pounds a distance of 15 feet or less.

WORKING ENVIRONMENT:

Normal cubicles and individual office environment. Work is primarily performed during regular business hours; however, occasional evening or weekend work may be required based on the department’s needs. Travel within the assigned service area may be required. The position may require working in moderately noisy to loud environments, including cubicles and communal workspaces, and participating in frequent collaborative team meetings. The work environment may include a fast-paced setting with frequent interruptions, changing priorities, and interactions with employees, the public, and other stakeholders.

This position description serves as a guideline for communicating the essential functions and other information about the position to the applicant/employee. It is not intended to create a binding employment contract nor cover every detail of the position and may be changed where appropriate.

title: HR Programs Partner-Specialist
description:
Summary

The HR Programs Partner administers Sunward’s performance management cycle and owns leave administration and employee movement, interpreting and applying HR practices and employment law to resolve routine to moderately complex issues independently.

Working under general guidance from the Director, Talent & Performance Management, this role exercises independent judgment and discretion on matters of significance, including leave eligibility determinations, FMLA designations, accommodation recommendations, and policy interpretation for managers. This role escalates the highest-risk or precedent-setting situations. The role also supports succession planning and leadership development by preparing leaders, delivering training, and following through on outcomes.

This role is a strategic partner to the managers it supports, helping them connect individual people decisions to Sunward’s broader deliverables. It brings a growth mindset to the work, treating every performance cycle, leave case, and talent conversation as a chance to improve how Sunward does it.

Success in this role requires sound judgment, discretion with confidential information, and the ability to manage competing priorities across multiple HR functions.

Essential Functions:

Performance Management

  • Administer the performance cycle within the approved framework and timeline: launch each phase, monitor progress, and keep goal setting, check-ins, and year-end reviews on schedule.
  • Serve as the first point of contact and strategic partner to managers during the cycle, resolving questions on process, content, and appraisal quality.
  • Coach managers on writing clear, specific, and defensible feedback, and translating department priorities into measurable deliverables their teams can act on.
  • Review submitted appraisals for completeness, consistency, and appropriate performance language. Resolve routine issues directly with managers and escalate rating concerns, potential bias, and calibration questions.
  • Identify patterns across the cycle, including missing documentation, inflated ratings, and vague goals, and bring them forward with recommended fixes.
  • Recommend refinements to forms, timelines, and job aids based on what each cycle surfaces.
  • Support performance improvement plans in partnership with Employee Relations, advising managers on process and documentation.

Succession & Talent Planning

  • Partner with managers to maintain the critical role list and keep succession and readiness data current and accurate, surfacing the capability gaps that put a critical role at risk.
  • Prepare readiness data and successor timelines for talent review conversations, and ensure leaders are prepared.
  • Document talent review outcomes and follow through on the development actions leaders commit to.
  • Maintain the career path and internal mobility documentation that shows employees what growth looks like at Sunward.

Leadership Development

  • Build participant materials, slides, handouts, and workbooks in partnership with the Director and the Learning & Development team.
  • Compile participation and feedback data, identify the themes worth acting on, and recommend adjustments to session materials.
  • Keep the leadership hub resource library up to date and prepare communications.

Leave & Accommodation Management

  • Own the leave process end to end: FMLA, short-term disability, personal leaves, and military leave, deciding routine cases independently and escalating denials and higher-risk matters.
  • Determine eligibility, designate leave, and decide return-to-work timing, guiding employees through the process with clarity and care, including those who do not qualify for FMLA.
  • Send required notices within legally mandated timeframes and maintain accurate case tracking.
  • Lead the ADA interactive process and recommend accommodations, partnering with Employee Relations.
  • Direct Payroll on leave-related pay and accrual treatment.

Employee Movement & Job Changes

  • Advise managers on the timing, sequencing, and communication of promotions, transfers, lateral moves, and title changes.
  • Partner with Compensation on pay decisions for job changes and recommend the approach where the situation is not covered by an existing structure.
  • Own separations end to end: conduct exit interviews, read the trends worth acting on, and bring recommendations forward.

HR Team & Process Improvement

  • Resolve escalated employee and manager questions related to performance, leave, and job changes, interpreting policy to reach the answer and escalating anything precedent-setting.
  • Own, document, and revise the standard operating procedures for the processes this role runs, testing improvements and measuring whether they worked.
  • Contribute to HR initiatives such as engagement work, new technology rollouts, and cross-department projects.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Experience

  • Two to four years of progressive, programmatic HR experience, with hands-on work in performance management administration, HR program support, or leave administration.
  • Experience with HRIS (Paylocity a plus).
  • Practical experience using AI tools for everyday work such as drafting, summarizing, or organizing information, and the judgment to keep confidential employee information out of them.
  • Credit union or financial services experience is a plus, not a requirement.

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in human resources, business administration, or a related field. Equivalent experience will be considered.
  • PHR, SHRM-CP, or similar certification preferred.

Knowledge

  • Working knowledge of employment law, including FMLA, ADA, and USERRA, and the judgment to apply it in real situations.

Skills/Abilities

  • Straightforward communicator who can explain a process clearly to someone hearing it for the first time.
  • Comfortable working with leaders at every level, answering questions directly and knowing when to escalate.
  • Detail-oriented, the kind of person who catches a missing signature or an inconsistent date before anyone else does.
  • Discreet with confidential information, always.
  • Organized under pressure, able to move between a leave case, a training roster, and a talent review packet in the same afternoon.
  • Strong Excel skills
  • Growth mindset. Curious and improvement-minded, more interested in building the better process than defending the current one, and open to feedback.

Physical Requirements/Work Environment

  • Hybrid work schedule, with regular in-office presence required to support in-person employee and leader interactions and maintain access to confidential records and systems.
  • Standard indoor office environment with moderate noise levels; standard business hours with occasional flexibility needed to meet deadlines.
  • Ability to communicate clearly in person, by phone, and virtually with employees and leaders at all levels, including sensitive conversations.
  • Regular use of a computer, keyboard, and phone, with visual acuity sufficient to review documents, data, and system screens for extended periods.
  • Primarily sedentary office work; requires sitting for extended periods at a desk and computer workstation.
  • Occasional travel between Sunward locations for in-person meetings.
  • Regular handling of confidential employee information, requiring discretion in a shared office workspace.
  • Occasional lifting and carrying of files, binders, or other materials up to 15lbs.

title: Project Coordinator
description:
GENERAL ROLE DESCRIPTION

The Project Coordinator supports the execution of project-related technical workstreams by building, coordinating, and tracking tasks within project management systems. This role works under the direct management of the Enterprise Project Manager to translate project direction into structured, actionable plans, ensuring work is clearly defined, organized, and progressing as expected.

This position focuses on project setup, task coordination, and follow-through to support efficient delivery across systems, tools, and development-related work. The role plays a key part in ensuring projects are accurately structured from the outset and maintained throughout execution to reduce delays, confusion, and rework.


RESPONSIBILITIES/KEY PERFORMANCE AREAS:

These are the important areas where you'll show your success in each appraisal time period. They include foundational work as well as specific tasks that align with project initiatives. You'll be evaluated on how well you perform on the targets in each area.


Primary Functions

Support the execution of project-related workstreams by translating approved project direction, plans, and priorities into clearly structured and maintained project systems. The Project Coordinator builds and maintains project structures in designated project management systems, coordinates tasks and follow-up, tracks progress, maintains project documentation, and supports communication among project stakeholders.

The Project Coordinator works under the direction of the Enterprise Project Manager and supports the effective execution of project plans. The role does not hold primary responsibility for project strategy, scope, prioritization, project planning, or project management decisions. Instead, the Project Coordinator ensures that approved plans are accurately reflected in project systems and that the information, tasks, documentation, and follow-up required for execution remain organized and current.

Company And Product Knowledge

  • Become knowledgeable of the company's history, mission, vision, and products
  • Maintain knowledge as products are revised and/or new products are introduced
  • Maintain knowledge of project management best practices

Departmental Processes

  • Goal Setting: Collaborate with the team to set and achieve departmental goals.
  • Process Improvement: Improve processes to enhance team effectiveness.
  • Scheduling and Development: Plan personal work schedule and recommend training or education needs.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Project Setup & Structure: Configure projects in designated project management systems using approved plans, templates, standards, dependencies, and timelines. Ensure projects are accurately and consistently configured so teams have a clear, reliable structure from which to execute their work.
  2. Project Coordination : Coordinate day-to-day activities associated with active project workstreams, including communication and follow-up with internal teammates, cross-departmental stakeholders, systems/resources, and external development partners.
    Keeps project work organized, aligned, and moving according to plan.
  3. Task Tracking & Progress Monitoring: Maintain accurate assignments, deadlines, statuses, dependencies, blockers, and next steps; identify and escalate risks or delays.
    Provides visibility into progress and prevents work from being delayed or overlooked.
  4. Communication & Follow-Up: Follow up with stakeholders, clarify established next steps, and ensure project information and decisions are documented and communicated.
    Reduces delays caused by miscommunication and keeps work moving forward.
  5. QA & Release Support: Coordinate testing, issue tracking, system updates, and release activities; escalate issues requiring technical, product, or project-management decisions.
    Supports quality and reduces the risk of errors in delivered work.
  6. Project Systems & Process Support: Maintain project systems and records, perform quality checks, and support consistent use of established project standards and processes.
    Improves consistency, reliability, and visibility across project work.
  7. Documentation Support: Maintain clear and organized documentation related to technical tasks, updates, and processes.

    Ensures continuity, consistency, and accessibility of project information.


    MINIMUM ROLE REQUIREMENTS

    1. 1–3 years of experience in coordination, administrative, or project support roles
    2. Strong organizational and time management skills
    3. Experience using project management tools (e.g., ClickUp, Asana, Monday) preferred
    4. Proficiency in standard workplace software (e.g., Google Workspace)
    5. Ability to translate high-level direction into structured tasks, timelines, and workflows
    6. Clear written and verbal communication skills
    7. Comfortable working with digital tools and systems
    8. Ability to learn and work within technical environments (no coding required)
    9. Detail-oriented with strong follow-through

    PHYSICAL DEMANDS

    • Working at a stationary desk with sit and stand options available
    • Typing on QWERTY-style keyboard
    • Viewing of a lighted computer monitor
    • Video chat/teleconferencing
    • Reaching, bending, and lifting up to 20 pounds

    CORE VALUES

    • Family - We value the essential role families play in their students' lifelong learning. Our commitment to families is shown in our products, services, and customer support. We also promote the well-being of our team members and their families by fostering a supportive work/life culture. Our goal is to prioritize families in order to contribute to a better community.
    • Trust - We believe in people making ethical choices, having faith in their good intentions, and recognizing their ability to learn and grow. We prioritize building a culture where trust is a shared commitment, creating a positive environment within our team, and lasting partnerships with our customers and vendors.
    • Simplicity - We believe in simplifying complex problems into easy-to-use solutions. We foster a culture of iterative improvement, focusing on clarity and quality. This enhances process efficiency, resulting in simplicity for our team and our customers.
    • Shared Success - We believe in mutual prosperity, that a win-win is achievable, and that we can all share in our success. We believe in supporting each other and celebrating every win as a team. Our success is not just our own; it's built on the achievements of our customers, vendors, and coworkers.
    • Growth - Our products add value to our customers, so we want more customers to use them. That means we have to invest our resources in our products and our team to keep growing and serving our customers.

    EOS QUALITIES

    These three qualities are important because they contribute to a team member’s success and satisfaction in a role. When an employee "gets it," they are more likely to be engaged in their work and make positive contributions to the company. When an employee "wants it," they are more likely to be motivated to go above and beyond. And when an employee has the "capacity to do it," they have the skills and abilities necessary to perform the job effectively.

    • Get it - An employee truly understands the job role. He or she knows what is expected, comprehends your culture, and is in line with your company’s Vision and Core Values. This is an employee who truly “gets it”.
    • Want it - An employee who wants to work with you. He or she is interested, has the desire, and is motivated by your core values to do the job to the best of his or her ability. This employee wants to make a difference.
    • Capacity to do it - The employee must have the knowledge, experience or education to be able to do the job. He or she must be willing to put in the time, and have the physical, emotional and mental capabilities necessary. Some employees can be trained to improve his or her capacity. Others cannot.

    REQUIREMENTS FOR ALL EMPLOYEES

    • Use your best efforts to do your work and tell your manager when you’re unable to work at your best
    • Demonstrate behavior consistent with company values, policies, standards, and procedures.
    • Communicate with your manager as soon as possible when you don’t understand your work, require more resources or training, or otherwise can’t complete your work for any reason when you encounter obstacles that will stop you from achieving your work to the required quality or within specified deadlines.
    • Continuously work to improve the systems and processes you are a part of. Share examples in the comment section.
    • Maintain knowledge of company news, processes, and information. Complete assigned training and participate in ongoing education for your role and expertise as needed. Share examples in the comment section.
    • Foster a workplace culture of respect, in which ideas and constructive criticism are both delivered and accepted with care, kindness, and grace and in the spirit of improving products, processes, and customer experience.

title: Logistics Lead
description:
Solstice Advanced Materials is seeking a LATAM Logistics Manager to lead logistics execution and strategy across the Latin America region.

The role will be responsible for developing and executing the regional logistics strategy, improving customer service and cost-to-serve, increasing asset productivity, and strengthening logistics processes and provider performance across LATAM.

Reporting to the Global Logistics Director, the LATAM Logistics Manager will work closely with Commercial, Customer Experience, Supply Chain Planning, Procurement, Operations, Finance and Trade Compliance to ensure logistics supports the growth and changing requirements of the business.

Regional Logistics Strategy and Leadership

  • Develop and execute the LATAM logistics strategy aligned with business growth, customer requirements and the global logistics strategy.
  • Serve as the primary regional point of contact for Logistics across LATAM and the key interface with regional Commercial, Customer Experience, Planning, Operations and Finance teams.

Operational Performance and Customer Service

  • Lead logistics performance across road, ocean, rail, air and intermodal transportation, as well as regional warehousing operations, within and into/out of LATAM.
  • Manage regional logistics providers, including carriers, freight forwarders, rail providers, warehouses and terminals, establishing clear performance expectations and escalation processes.

Cost, Productivity and Asset Management

  • Own initiatives to reduce regional cost-to-serve and deliver logistics productivity.
  • Develop and implement savings opportunities in partnership with Logistics Procurement and regional stakeholders.

Trade Compliance and Regional Requirements

  • Partner with Trade Compliance and the business to support customs, import/export, quota and other regulatory requirements affecting LATAM logistics.
  • Ensure logistics processes appropriately address country-specific documentation and operational requirements.

Process Improvement and Transformation

  • Develop and standardize regional logistics processes and SOPs.
  • Establish clear performance management and governance with freight forwarders, carriers, rail providers, warehouses, terminals and other logistics partners.

Experience and Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Logistics, Supply Chain, Business, Engineering or a related discipline with a minimum of 5 years of relevant logistics or supply chain experience; OR a minimum of 10 years of relevant logistics or supply chain experience in lieu of a degree.
  • Full professional proficiency in English and Spanish is required; proficiency in Portuguese is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience managing transportation and logistics operations, ideally across multiple countries or complex international supply chains.
  • Experience with ocean and road transportation; exposure to rail, warehousing, air, intermodal, customs or international trade flows is advantageous.
  • Experience managing logistics providers and using KPIs to drive performance improvement.
  • Experience managing Dangerous Goods (DG) transportation and associated regulatory requirements is strongly preferred.
  • Strong understanding of logistics cost, service, working-capital and operational trade-offs.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and communication skills.
  • Experience with SAP or similar ERP systems and logistics reporting or analytics tools is advantageous.

Professional Attributes

  • Strategic mindset with the ability to translate business requirements into practical logistics solutions.
  • Strong ownership and ability to operate independently in a complex regional environment.
  • Comfortable challenging existing processes and driving change.
  • Strong stakeholder-management skills across multiple functions and levels of the organization.
  • Able to balance immediate operational priorities with longer-term strategy and continuous improvement.
  • Strong commercial awareness and ability to understand the impact of logistics decisions on customer service, cost, working capital and business growth.
