title: Gametech Innovation Technical Lead
description:
WHAT YOU WILL BE WORKING ON

The Gametech Innovation team builds the tools and systems Gameloft’s game teams work with, from AI in production pipelines to art pipeline optimisation across Unity and Unreal. We are looking for a Tech Lead to take technical ownership of that work as the team continues to grow its scope. You will be responsible for the architecture, establish quality standards, and work directly with the studios using the team’s solutions.

What it means on a daily basis

  • Evaluate new engine features, technologies and AI capabilities, then define the architecture and technology choices the team commits to across Unity and Unreal projects
  • Work closely on complex features and essential systems using C++ and C#
  • Own technical quality: coding standards, code reviews, build and release pipelines, and how AI is integrated into both our tools and our own development workflow
  • Mentor developers on architecture, design decisions and code quality, through reviews, pairing and technical discussion
  • Work with studios to understand what actually slows them down, turn that into feasible technical scopes and estimates, and flag technical risks early enough to do something about them

What success will look like

In the beginning, it means getting familiar with the codebases, connecting with the studios the team supports, and identifying the most urgent areas to address. As you settle in, you will have set the architecture direction for the team’s main projects and established how technical quality is held. Later on, the benchmark is straightforward: studios use the team’s tools every day, and the developers around you are making more effective technical choices without needing much guidance.

Who you would be working with

You will be reporting to our Gametech Innovation Manager, and collaborate very closely with other Developers from the Gametech Innovation team across multiple studios worldwide, including Paris, Montreal, Bucharest, and others, offering opportunities to collaborate with colleagues from diverse backgrounds and perspectives. Day to day you will work with game programmers, technical artists and producers on Gameloft's game teams internationally.

Your recruitment journey

  • Recruitment interview: A conversation to explore how the role aligns with your background and to address your main questions.
  • HM interview: You will meet a Hiring Manager to discuss your experience, vision, and how you approach game technology topics at a broader level.
  • Test: You will receive a short case study to complete.
  • Tech interview: You will meet members of our technical team to present your test and talk through your approach, reasoning, and methodologies in more depth.

Where this role can take you

Over time, and depending on your interests and the team’s needs, this role can grow in two directions: towards people management as the team expands, or towards architecture and technical direction across our projects and studios. Training, mentorship and coaching programmes are available along the way, and Talent Move lets you look at internal opportunities elsewhere at Gameloft.

WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED

  • Advanced proficiency with Unreal Engine and/or Unity, including their editors and extensions, and solid proficiency in C++ and C#
  • Experience building and launching tools or systems that other teams relied on and kept using
  • Advanced debugging, profiling and performance optimisation across complex systems, together with the ability to write clean, maintainable and self-explanatory code
  • Solid understanding of CI/CD, build infrastructure and version control at scale
  • Practical use of AI in real development work, both as coding assistants in your own workflow and as services integrated into the tools you build

WHO YOU ARE

  • Curious: you enjoy digging into unfamiliar problems and exploring new engines, tools and approaches
  • Solution-driven: you turn ambiguous requests into workable technical paths and treat constraints as problems to solve
  • A mentor: you raise the technical level around you through code review, pairing and design discussion, and explain your reasoning clearly in English to technical and non-technical people alike

WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU

Benefits

  • Remote work: Up to 2 days per week, plus up to 1 month of full remote work from anywhere in France and up to 1 month abroad each year.
  • Access to Wellpass (formerly Gymlib)
  • Employee Savings Plan (PEG)
  • Standard benefits: meal vouchers, 50% reimbursement of public transportation costs (Navigo pass), and health insurance

Life at Gameloft

We believe that great work starts with a stimulating and supportive environment. That's why we offer flexible working hours, unlimited coffee and tea, fresh fruit, and monthly breakfast gatherings to help kick-start the day.

Our offices are also designed to encourage collaboration and team spirit, with dedicated spaces for video games and board games, foosball and ping-pong tables, as well as weekly futsal sessions. And of course, you'll have plenty of opportunities to connect through our regular company events!

Ready to join the game? Apply now!

title: Senior Program Manager II - Laser Communications
description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we’re building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, laser communication terminals, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR PROGRAM MANAGER II - LASER COMMUNICATIONS

Laser communication is the backbone of the constellations of today and tomorrow, and demand for it is growing fast. We are scaling industry-leading optical communication terminals to meet it: high-performing, affordable, and available at the volume commercial and government constellation operators need. Based at Rocket Lab’s global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, you are the customer’s champion and the delivery lead for our optical communication terminal programs. You own the customer outcome: the day-to-day relationship, delivery commitments and schedule at rate, milestone and acceptance reviews, risk, and program health. You build on a proven, standard terminal product and partner closely with our Product team on configuration, pricing, and new customer needs. You’ll work alongside the teams that build the spacecraft, the components, and the rockets, so the people you need to solve a problem are down the hall, not under another contract. This is a high-impact, customer-facing role: you connect the customer, our engineering teams, the production line, and the business across two continents, and you’re the person our customers count on.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

  • Lead Delivery: Lead terminal programs from award through qualification, production at rate, delivery, and on-orbit checkout, across current-generation production and next-generation variants. Hold each program to its plan and deliver on schedule, technical performance, and every customer commitment.
  • Lead the Team of Teams: Run multiple concurrent customer programs, work closely with Chief Engineers on link performance, data rate, SWaP, environmental qualification, and optical terminal interoperability, and dive in personally on the problems that matter most to delivery.
  • Deliver at Rate: Own each program’s delivery profile and protect it. Spot yield, supplier, and test-capacity risk early and drive it to closure with Operations and the Product team.
  • Forge the Supply Chain: Partner with Supply Chain to manage critical suppliers as strategic partners, building the relationships and accountability that keep every customer delivery on schedule.
  • Run the Program Lifecycle: Own program startup and baselining, milestone and qualification reviews, export and ITAR obligations with Trade Compliance, customer acceptance, and closeout across our U.S. and European sites.
  • Champion the Customer: Be the trusted point of contact for customers through milestone reviews, interoperability campaigns, acceptance, and delivery. Partner with BD & Strategy on proposals and with the Product team on pricing and configuration, bringing the voice of the customer to every decision.
  • Raise the Bar: Mentor the people around you, set a high standard for how we show up for customers, and help develop the program leaders who will run our next generation of laser communications programs.

QUALIFICATIONS YOU’LL BRING AS A SENIOR PROGRAM MANAGER II

  • Engineering Foundation: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Physics, or Math.
  • Technical Depth: Working understanding of free-space optical or RF communications: link budgets, pointing, acquisition, and tracking, modems and coding, and space or airborne environmental qualification.
  • 8+ years in space, aerospace, or photonics hardware programs, with multiple full program cycles. We weight the hardest thing you’ve shipped over the count.
  • Customer Delivery: A track record of leading a complex hardware program to delivery (customer, schedule, risk, and acceptance) and carrying it across the finish line under real pressure.
  • Production Delivery: Evidence you’ve moved real hardware from prototype to qualified, rate-production delivery to customers.
  • Program Financials: Experience managing program cost, EAC, and customer contract changes in partnership with finance and product teams on a program of meaningful scale.
  • Proof Point: You’ve delivered hardware at rate to a demanding customer and kept their trust through a hard moment, such as a slip, a test failure, or a contract change.
  • Clearance: U.S. Person status required (ITAR/EAR); ability to obtain a security clearance preferred.

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

  • Domain Authority: Direct experience with optical inter-satellite links or optical ground or airborne terminals.
  • Production Velocity: A proven playbook for taking low-volume, hand-built optical or electro-optical hardware into high-rate production without sacrificing reliability.
  • Constellation Fluency: Experience delivering to large commercial or defense constellation programs.
  • Customer Leadership: Experience as the primary customer interface for constellation operators or satellite primes, from kickoff through acceptance.
  • Global Leadership: Experience leading program work across geographically dispersed sites, including export-control and dual-use compliance.
  • Advanced Technical Credibility: A Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Optics/Photonics, Physics, or a related field.
  • Systems & Toolchain Fluency: You speak systems engineering (trade studies, interface control, requirement integrity) and use Jira, Confluence, and ERP/MRP to keep program health visible at speed.
  • AI Fluency: You put AI tools to work in day-to-day program management, from schedule and risk analysis to status reporting and customer communications, so you and your team spend more time on the problems that matter.

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

$166,800—$258,625 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

title: Senior Technical Product Manager
description:
Reports to: CTO
Type: High-agency individual contributor
Products: Single Brain + API Gateway
Location: Full-time, remote (Los Angeles a plus, not required)
Comp: $120,000–$150,000 USD / year

One-liner

Own what gets built and why across Single Brain and API Gateway — turn build → build → build into build → measure → iterate.

About the role

Single Grain combines marketing services, software, and AI. This seat owns product judgment for Single Brain and the API Gateway: which metrics matter, what is blocking them, and what engineering should build next.

Engineering owns how we build. You own what we build and why.

You report to the CTO. You work daily with a ~6-person engineering team. You do not manage that team as a people manager; you create clarity so their effort lands on the highest-leverage outcomes.

You should be an advanced AI user. Use AI for research, interview synthesis, analytics, specs, prototypes, experiment design, and competitive work so your product decisions get faster and better.

What you will own

  • Identify the highest-leverage product metrics across Single Brain and API Gateway (activation, usage, retention, expansion, revenue, time-to-value, Gateway/integration adoption).

  • Diagnose what is limiting those metrics.

  • Decide what engineering should build next, with clear hypotheses and success criteria.

  • Run strong weekly sprint kickoffs so the team leaves knowing: what metric are we moving, what are we doing to move it, and how will we know it worked.

  • Own customer discovery — talk to customers often; separate loud requests from high-leverage opportunities.

  • Own product analytics and instrumentation quality; no major initiative ships without a measurement plan.

  • Review launches against real results and choose iterate, expand, revert, or move on.

  • Keep the integration / Gateway roadmap intentionally prioritized.

  • Protect the team from low-impact or poorly defined work.

What success looks like

  • By day 30: deep product understanding; customer discovery underway; core journeys/funnels mapped; analytics audited; clear view of which metrics matter and where the biggest opportunities are.

  • By day 60: you own weekly sprint kickoffs; major initiatives have metrics and measurement plans; core funnels instrumented and visible.

  • By day 90: prioritized roadmap tied to measurable outcomes; multiple complete build → measure → iterate cycles; measurable improvement in at least one meaningful product metric. Failure = features still shipping without hypotheses, instrumentation, or post-launch learning.

  • By 6–12 months: durable product OS (Metric → Diagnosis → Hypothesis → Build → Measure → Learn → Iterate); customer discovery and post-launch measurement are standard; CTO is no longer the primary person deciding what engineering builds next; key product/business metrics improved materially.

Evidence we want to see

  • Experience owning a technical software product (APIs, integrations, auth, data fluency).

  • Metrics you personally owned and improved — with diagnosis, not feature lists.

  • Sprint leadership / prioritization with engineering teams.

  • Product analytics and instrumentation ownership (PostHog, Amplitude, Mixpanel, or similar).

  • Advanced daily AI workflows for product work.

  • High-agency ownership: you set roadmap direction; you are not a conduit or Jira admin.

  • Ideal: early-stage / growth-stage; developer tools, API, infrastructure, or AI products.

What this role is not

Not a project manager, not a backlog clerk, not “collect feature requests,” not “feature shipped = success,” not waiting for the CTO to dictate the roadmap.

How the process works

Application and evidence review → our standard six-question AI prescreen for selected candidates → live discussion / working session (metric → diagnose → propose build → mock sprint kickoff → measurement) → paid exercise if substantial work is required → references.

Benefits

Medical, dental, and vision; life insurance; 401(k) with 4% match; unlimited PTO; monthly UberEats; MacBook; home-office stipend/setup. Subject to plan terms and eligibility.

Apply

Apply with resume/profile and proof: a metric you moved, how you diagnosed it, what you built, and how you measured the result.

title: AI Delivery Lead | Technology Transformation | Frontier AI
description:
AI Delivery Lead Role

AI Delivery Lead - Enterprise AI & Transformation (Permanent)


AI, Data & Digital Delivery | Auckland, New Zealand

The Client


Our client is a well-established New Zealand Financial Services organization with a strong digital reputation and a growing portfolio of financial products used by Kiwi’s all over the country, including through bank and partner channels. They’ve already taken AI out of the pilot stage and into everyday frontline use. Now they’re scaling it into claims and underwriting, and they need someone to own delivery so the AI team can stay focused on building. Our client has moved into the building phase of an ‘Onthology’ so this is legitimate frontier work in the AI space.

The Opportunity


This is genuinely hands-on delivery leadership in a regulated environment. It’s not a role for someone who has only run traditional IT programmes, or who has only seen AI at demo stage. It suits a delivery or product leader who has taken emerging technology from prototype into production, and who knows what it takes to do that safely when risk, privacy and legal teams are in the room. This newly created role will suit someone who is deeply curious about how patterns (systems, people behaviours and thinking) work.

You’ll be the single point of delivery coordination across a multi-channel AI platform (web, messaging and voice) and the use cases that run on it, starting with claims and underwriting journeys. You’ll turn an agreed product roadmap into a delivery plan, keep engineering, data, architecture and the business moving together, and be the person who can tell a promising prototype from something ready to run on live customer claims. There will be opportunities that appear to be vague and almost hidden, those opportunities might not have the right voice or representative sponsorship but you will have an innate ability to see through all of that and then drive into a real-world offering.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Owning intake and prioritisation of AI use cases, and shaping them for value, feasibility, data readiness and risk.
  • Turning product priorities into a delivery roadmap with clear milestones, dependencies and capacity.
  • Coordinating product owners, business analysts, architects, platform and data engineers, testers and operations across multiple concurrent workstreams.
  • Building the backlog and driving work through discovery, prototype, pilot, production and scale.
  • Making sure experiments have clear hypotheses and explicit stop, pivot or scale decisions.
  • Embedding responsible AI controls, evidence and go/no-go reviews with risk, security, privacy and legal.
  • Managing delivery partners and vendors, and tracking cost, adoption and realised benefits with Finance.

What You’ll Bring

  • Strong programme, product or delivery leadership across complex, technology-enabled transformation (8+ years).
  • Proven experience taking AI, data or emerging technology from prototype into production and scaled use.
  • Confident working in a regulated environment, with risk, security, privacy and legal teams as everyday partners.
  • Enough technical fluency to challenge architects and engineers, and to spot when a prototype isn’t production-ready.
  • Practical understanding of generative AI, agentic AI and automation delivery, including evaluation and monitoring.
  • Experience with demand management, prioritisation, capacity planning and executive reporting.
  • A self-starter who takes ownership of a problem and drives it to an outcome.
  • Experience in insurance or financial services, and exposure to AWS and Snowflake, is strongly regarded.

Why Apply

  • Genuinely rare opportunity to lead AI delivery in a New Zealand household brand name that’s already past the hype and into production.
  • Real scope to shape how AI is governed and scaled, working directly with the Head of AI & Insights which means that you will have a voice at the table.
  • A strong, collaborative team and a business that’s growing through new partner channels.

How to Apply


For a confidential discussion about this role, contact Adam Roi at Walkersmith or apply with confidence via Seek. We look forward to hearing from you. We are only considering candidates who are currently in New Zealand with a Valid Working Rights.

title: Senior Scientist, Protein Sciences
description:
Company Overview:

Strand Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering programmable mRNA therapeutics to unlock the full potential of genetic medicines. Strand is applying its proprietary Signal Stack platform, which integrates EverScript circular RNA, AmpliScript self-replicating RNA, SignalPath targeted delivery, and logic-driven SignalLock genetic circuits to enable precise control of therapeutic activity across tissues and cell types and overcome foundational limitations in targeting, durability, and safety.

Strand is advancing a pipeline with an initial focus on oncology and autoimmune disease. Its initial program, STX-001, an intratumorally delivered LNP-encapsulated self-replicating RNA expressing IL-12, has demonstrated preliminary evidence of systemic immune activation and anti-tumor activity in patients with advanced solid tumors who have progressed on prior therapies. Building on this early clinical validation, intravenously delivered STX-003 is designed for tumor-targeted expression and avoidance of off-target expression. STX-003, which is expected to enter the clinic in mid-2026, has the potential to be a major step forward for the fields of genetic medicine and oncology. Strand is also advancing STX-005, an in vivo CAR-T program designed to enable controlled, durable expression and repeat dosing. Founded by MIT synthetic biology pioneers, Strand has raised over $250 million and is headquartered in Boston, MA.

Become the next standout single strand!

Job Summary:

Strand is seeking a highly motivated and innovative Senior Scientist of Protein Sciences to join our Platform Enabling Technologies team. This founding role will establish and lead protein science capabilities that enable the discovery, engineering, and validation of protein payloads, binders, and reagents for Strand’s programmable RNA medicines.

Reporting to the Associate Director of Platform Enabling Technologies, the ideal candidate combines deep expertise in nanobody or antibody engineering, computational protein design, high-throughput protein purification and characterization, and enthusiasm for building new scientific functions while remaining active on the bench.

This role integrates experimental protein sciences with AI-enabled design to discover and optimize antibodies, nanobodies, and other therapeutic proteins. Working closely with our computational biology, RNA biology, delivery, and translational teams, the scientist will define protein design criteria, lead experimental validation, and connect molecular attributes, including expression, folding, secretion, stability, activity, and developability as recombinant protein and following RNA delivery.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Establish and lead the Protein Sciences function by defining the scientific priorities, managing external vendors, selecting technology and instrumentation, and building workflows for binder discovery, protein engineering, production, and characterization.
  • Build antibody, nanobody, or other binder modalities & discovery capabilities that integrate computational modeling, library design/construction, display-based high-throughput screening, and downstream validation to discover and optimize single domain and other antibody-derived binders
  • Partner with Computational biology to develop an AI-enabled protein design platform by defining experimentally relevant design criteria, generating high-quality training and validation datasets, and testing model-generated candidates.
  • Lead binder discovery projects against therapeutically relevant targets by leveraging external partners and internal platform capabilities
  • Develop fit-for-purpose recombinant protein expression and purification workflows in in mammalian, yeast, and bacterial systems to support rapid design-build-test-learn cycles.
  • Establish biochemical, biophysical, and cell-based assays to evaluate binding kinetics, specificity, purity, stability, aggregation, activity, and developability.
  • Partner with RNA biology teams and delivery teams to optimize RNA-encoded proteins for translation efficiency, folding, intracellular trafficking or secretion, functional activity, duration of expression, and compatibility with the intended delivery modality.
  • Design orthogonal assays that distinguish RNA, delivery, and protein-level drivers of performance and use the resulting data to guide construct and formulation optimization.
  • Communicate data, risks, and recommendations clearly to multidisciplinary project teams and contribute to portfolio and platform strategy.

Qualifications:

  • PhD with 2-5 years of experience, or B.S/M.S. with 7-10 years of experience in Biochemical Engineering, Biotechnology, Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, or a related scientific discipline.
  • Demonstrated expertise in nanobody or antibody discovery and engineering including library design, screening and production, humanization, affinity maturation, and experimental validation.
  • Demonstrated expertise in high-throughput recombinant protein expression, purification, and characterization from mammalian, yeast, and bacterial systems including cell culture, chromatography-based separations, and affinity/developability assays.
  • Proven track record of developing biologics as therapeutics and delivering on projects to enable programs to progress toward IND submissions.
  • Experience with advanced protein characterizations methods such as LC-MS, SEC-MALS, and SPR/BLI.
  • Strong understanding of ML/AI enabled protein design methodologies and the experimental validation of resulting designs. Direct, hands-on experience in deploying methods preferred.

title: Operations and Project Coordinator
description:
Davidson College seeks applications for the role of Operations & Project Coordinator in the D.G. and Harriet Wall Martin Institute for Public Good. The Martin Institute integrates academic research, civic engagement, public policy, creative expression, and ethical leadership to foster collaboration that equips students to address society’s challenges and emerge as ethical public leaders.

The Operations & Project Coordinator provides direct administrative, project, and event support to advance the Institute's mission. Operating under the supervision of the Managing Director, the Coordinator manages complex event logistics, supports faculty and fellow programs, organizes central records, tracks project deadlines, provides occasional scheduling and logistical support for leadership. Because this role interacts with faculty, civic leaders, and external dignitaries, exceptional professional discretion, polish, and diplomatic communication skills are essential.

Reporting & Role Boundaries

  • Direct Supervision: Reports directly to the Managing Director, who advises on daily task prioritization, project assignments, and workload management. But, as the description shares, provides support across the institute
  • Workload Coordination: Operational support for Institute projects and faculty initiatives is coordinated through the Managing Director.
  • Financial & Unit Boundaries: All financial transactions, expense reconciliations, budget tracking, and routine purchasing continue to be handled by the Administrative Assistant.
  • Support Role Boundary: Executes operational and administrative tasks set by leadership; holds no independent authority to set strategic direction, establish policy, or approve budgets.

Responsibilities

Operational Support & Tracking - Supports the Managing Director in maintaining internal operational momentum, tracking administrative workflows, and driving central Institute and program area initiatives by:

  • Logistical Follow-Through & Event Support: Submit facility requests, coordinate vendor setups, and confirm logistics based on established master calendar dates and parameters set by the Managing Director.
  • Meeting Preparation & Logistics: Handle room bookings, catering arrangements, materials preparation, and basic setup for Institute working groups and administrative sessions.
  • Grant Data & Operational Reporting: Gather curriculum development grant updates, project metrics, and administrative data across all five program areas for central leadership review and operational tracking.
  • Campus Newsletter & Communications Support: Collect faculty and staff submissions, program updates to draft blurb entries for the VPAA Newsletter, Operations Reports, and internal campus announcements.
  • Institutional Records & Knowledge Management: Proactively collect, organize, and archive essential program materials, project summaries, and event documentation in central Google Drive folders; coordinate with faculty program directors and fellows to ensure routine administrative artifacts are stored properly.
  • Maintaining Tracking Tools: Keep central operational spreadsheets and status dashboards updated across Institute-wide administrative priorities.
  • Executing Daily Workflows: Handle administrative documentation, route general inquiries, and manage operational follow-through to keep assigned tasks moving on schedule.
  • Faculty Program Area Director Operational Support: Provide comprehensive operational and event logistics support to Faculty program area directors —handling room reservations through campus software, catering, AV/tech coordination, vendor arrangements, and setup execution for program-specific lectures, workshops, panels, and working groups.

Cross-Campus Initiative & Project Coordination - Executes administrative systems, survey tools, and logistical coordination for multi-stakeholder projects across campus. Delivers dedicated logistical, event, and resource coordination across program areas and for faculty fellow cohorts

  • Administrative Tools & Surveys: Build, distribute, and collect basic administrative tools (such as setting up online surveys for faculty research needs or event feedback) as assigned by leadership.
  • Faculty Grant & Project Support: Track project milestones, gather data, and provide logistical support for faculty-led grant projects across all five program areas as triaged and assigned by the Managing Director.
  • Cross-Campus Coordination: Schedule, convene, and manage meeting logistics involving faculty, staff, and institutional partners across campus for Institute initiatives.
  • Fellow Cohort Coordination: Coordinate administrative logistics specifically for Sabbatical Fellows and CE Faculty Fellows—including ordering and arranging regular fellow lunches, setting up orientation sessions, booking meeting spaces, and executing logistics for signature fellow gatherings.
  • Resource & Calendar Feasibility Assessment: Evaluate campus venue availability, resource constraints, and scheduling calendars to propose practical event options and prevent operational bottlenecks for program area and fellow initiatives before submitting setup requests.
  • On-Site Event Operations: Serve as the primary on-site operational contact during Institute events to oversee room configurations, catering deliveries, and facility readiness.

Key Skills & Competencies

  • Resource & Logistics Planning: Ability to analyze room availability, event calendars, campus resources, and vendor timelines to plan seamless event logistics.
  • Clear & Professional Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills; ability to represent the Institute with high polish, warmth, and professionalism when interacting with community leaders, politicians, local officials, and external dignitaries.
  • Patience & Diplomacy: Demonstrates high emotional intelligence, patience, and discretion when coordinating with faculty, fellows, busy executives, and external community partners.
  • Multitasking & Operational Execution: Strong organizational agility with a proven track record of managing competing priorities, shifting deadlines, and multiple concurrent logistical tasks smoothly.
  • Project & Operational Tracking: Strong skill in organizing project data, updating status tracking tools, and following up on action items across multiple concurrent initiatives.
  • Event & Logistics Coordination: Proven ability to manage physical setups, catering orders, room bookings, and administrative details smoothly.
  • Practical Tool Capability: Comfortable setting up and using basic administrative tools (e.g., Google Drive for folder organization, spreadsheets for project dashboards, Qualtrics/Google Forms for surveys, university scheduling software).

Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree required.
  • Experience: 2–4 years of administrative, project coordination, or operational experience preferably in higher education, public sector, or a complex non-profit environment.
  • Tech Skills: Proficiency with standard office productivity suites (Google Workspace / Microsoft Office), online survey tools, and standard university administrative systems.

Information about how to submit an application can be found at https://employment.davidson.edu.

  • Build Class II and III devices that directly affect patient lives

  • Collaborative, engineering-led culture
  • Hybrid working in a growing team

title: Senior Android Developer
description:
Waracle are looking for a Senior Developer for an exciting new role joining our world-class digital technology consultancy and home to a diverse, smart, curious and ambitious community of specialists in technology-driven transformation.

We work with ambitious clients to help them solve their biggest business and customer challenges. We help our clients to innovate and create intelligent digital products and services. We thrive on complex challenges and deliver business-critical IT transformation projects, moving seamlessly from strategy, design and delivery to operations.

This is a Hybrid role, offering the flexibility to balance your professional and personal life, with 2 days a week spent connecting with colleagues in our London officeoron client site

The Role

We are looking for a self- motivated Senior Developer, proficient in Android mobile development. In this position, you will drive the end-to-end craft of building, developing, and deploying high-performance Android components and services.

Whilst Android will be your core area of expertise, we’re looking for someone with a curiosity and willingness to work across the wider mobile ecosystem. Experience with, or an openness to working with, frameworks such as React Native and Flutter would be highly valued.

You don’t need to be an expert in every framework - we’re interested in developers who have strong engineering fundamentals, can adapt to different technologies and enjoy learning new approaches to solving mobile challenges!

Key aspects of the role include:

  • Technical Excellence & Delivery: Designing and delivering end-to-end features and small subsystems; optimising app performance, accessibility, and responsiveness; and being accountable for successful delivery of features.

  • Communication & Stakeholder Management: Explaining technical trade-offs in plain language; and presenting demos confidently to clients and stakeholders to shape tactical direction.

  • Leadership & Team Collaboration: Leading delivery of specific features or workstreams; and mentoring junior colleagues in both craft and process.

  • Culture & Community of Practice: Regularly mentoring others across the practice; and representing Waracle in interviews and recruitment panels.

  • Participating in ad-hoc duties from time to time as required by management.

Research shows that underrepresented groups tend to only apply for roles that they believe they meet 100% of the criteria for. At Waracle, we want to buck that trend! We hire for passion, potential and mindset as much as credentials.

What you'll bring:

  • Core Language & Framework Expertise: Exceptional proficiency in Kotlin and Java, backed by a deep understanding of the Android SDK, core threading, offline storage, and performance tuning.

  • Modern UI & Design Mastery: Hands-on experience building dynamic, responsive user interfaces with Jetpack Compose, coupled with a firm command of Google’s Android Design Principles and interface guidelines.

  • Architecture & Clean Code: Strong practical application of SOLID principles, working comfortably within a modularised codebase, and architecting robust solutions using MVVM/MVI alongside Android Architecture Components and Jetpack libraries.

  • Ecosystem & Optimisation: Broad knowledge of the open-source Android landscape—leveraging top-tier third-party libraries for common tasks, benchmarking, and fine-grained optimisation.

  • Quality & Engineering Practices: Proven track record in writing reliable UI tests, maintaining clean software development lifecycles, and working fluently with modern code versioning workflows like Git.

  • Cross-Platform Knowledge: Direct experience or familiar exposure with cross-platform mobile frameworks such asFlutter or React Native.

What to expect from our hiring process

1. First Hello: An informal chat with your dedicated Talent Attraction Partner to talk about Waracle, what you want out of your next move, salary, benefits, and office hybrid working model.

2. Craft Showcase: A chance to demonstrate your real-world expertise. Depending on the role, this will be a focused take-home task (capped at 2–3 hours to respect your time).

3. Talking Impact: A collaborative deep dive into how you solve problems, work with others, and raise the bar, guided by our core values and competency framework.

Your Talent Attraction Partner will be in your corner through every step right up to your Welcome Ritual on day one.

Our Benefits

We believe in supporting our team, inside and outside of work. Here's a glimpse of what you can expect:

  • Rest & Recharge: You'll receive 27 days of annual leave, plus 8 bank holidays, totaling 35 days of holiday to unwind and pursue your passions.

  • Financial Future & Security: Plan for retirement with our company-matched 5% pension contribution. For added peace of mind, we also offer a Death in Service benefit, providing 2 x your annual salary for your loved ones.

  • Health & Wellness: Our Medicash Health Cash Plans help cover everyday healthcare costs, complemented by an Employee Assistance Programme for confidential support, and Group Sickness Cover for peace of mind.

  • Flexible Working: We champion hybrid working, providing a home office setup budget to ensure you're comfortable and productive wherever you are.

  • Learning & Development: Invest in yourself with access to Udemy Business and a dedicated learning and development budget for continuous growth.

  • Lifestyle Perks: Make the most of our Cycle to Work Scheme, and enjoy exclusive gym and retail discounts.

  • Family First: Our enhanced parental leave policies include support for fertility journeys, recognising diverse family needs.

  • Community & Connection: We foster a vibrant culture with regular fun meet-ups and lunch on us in the office once a month. You'll also have the opportunity to make a local impact through Spirit of Waracle, our initiative for getting involved in charitable causes locally, building strong team bonds and giving back.

We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from all suitably qualified persons regardless of their race, gender, disability, religion/belief, sexual orientation or age.

title: CON 2026/34 - International Consultant for the Development of a Specialized Training Module for Labour Inspectors
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration


Project Context and Scope

Danish Western Balkans Regional Migration Governance Programme (RMGP) – Focus on Western Balkans and Republic of Türkiye – Outcome 2 (IB0537)
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) will support the development of a specialized training module to strengthen the capacity of labour inspectors to identify, respond to and refer cases involving indicators of trafficking in persons and labour exploitation. The module will be designed for integration into the initial and continuous training curriculum for labour inspectors, ensuring sustainability and institutional ownership.
The International Consultant will work as part of a team with the Local Consultant to ensure that the training module combines international standards, comparative practice and technical guidance with a strong understanding of the Albanian legal, institutional and operational context, including the roles and responsibilities of labour inspectorates, law enforcement institutions, referral structures and relevant case management procedures.
Working under the overall supervision of IOM Albania and in close coordination with the Labour Inspectorate and the Local Consultant, the International Consultant will first support an assessment of the current situation, existing capacities, training needs and operational priorities. The findings of this assessment will inform the technical development of the specialized training module for labour inspectors and the subsequent organization and delivery of the Training of Trainers (ToT).

Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing

Danish Western Balkans Regional Migration Governance Programme (RMGP) – Focus on Western Balkans and Republic of Türkiye – Outcome 2 (IB0537) 2:1:6:001
Tasks to be performed under this contract

The International Consultant will provide overall technical leadership, comparative expertise and quality assurance for the development of the specialized training module. The Local Consultant will complement this work by ensuring national contextualization and alignment with Albania’s legal, institutional and operational context. Together, the consultants will work as one team to produce a practical, sustainable and institutionally relevant training package for labour inspectors.
The consultant will be responsible for the following tasks:
• Provide overall technical guidance for the development of the specialized training module, drawing on international standards, comparative practice and relevant regional experience on trafficking in persons, labour exploitation and labour inspection.
• Work jointly with the Local Consultant to assess the current situation, existing capacities, training needs and contextual priorities for labour inspectors in Albania before moving to the development of the training module.
• Lead the drafting of the specialized training module, with inputs from the Local Consultant to ensure alignment with Albanian legislation and institutional practice.
• Provide technical inputs on key indicators of trafficking in persons and labour exploitation that may be identified during labour inspections, ensuring consistency with international standards and practical relevance for inspectors.
• Develop practical tools, exercises, case studies, checklists and guidance materials for labour inspectors.
• Contribute to the design of sessions on selecting, planning and conducting professional inspections in suspected cases of labour exploitation and trafficking in persons.
• Develop guidance on planning and conducting joint inspections involving labour inspectorates, police and other relevant institutions.
• Ensure that referral pathways and inspection case management procedures are accurately reflected in the module.
• Participate in selected consultations and validation meetings with labour inspectorates, police and other relevant stakeholders, in coordination with IOM and the Local Consultant.
• Co-facilitate the Training of Trainers in Tirana together with the Local Consultant.
• Incorporate feedback from IOM, the Labour Inspectorate and national stakeholders into the final training module and related materials.

Key deliverables (indicative):

No.

Deliverable

Working days

1

Assessment and inception note completed, outlining the current situation, training needs, methodology, workplan and agreed division of tasks with the Local Consultant.

4 days

2

Draft specialized training module prepared, incorporating assessment findings, international standards, practical tools, case studies, exercises and referral guidance.

4 days

3

ToT co-facilitated and final training package completed, incorporating feedback from IOM, the Labour Inspectorate, the Local Consultant and relevant stakeholders.

2 days

Total

10 working days

Performance indicators for the evaluation of results
• Assigned deliverables are completed within the agreed timeframe and meet IOM quality standards.
• Information and analysis are accurate, well-documented and directly relevant to the objectives of the assignment.
• Stakeholder consultations are conducted in a professional, respectful and inclusive manner, and outcomes are clearly summarized.

title: Panel Room Builder- Second Shift
description:
Summary/Objective

The Panel Room Builder is responsible for prepping and assembling all materials needed to build a press rig for pressing in the press room. Press rig construction involves cutting material to size, cleaning/surface prepping the materials, and stacking them together in a specified pattern. The press rig is then sent to the press room and loaded into a press where heat, time and pressure laminates materials together. This process is used to create a base panel, to laminate a cover onto an etched panel without leads under the cover, and/or to laminate bond ply, foil backing or other layers together.

Essential Functions


Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Determine daily priorities and direction from supervisor.
  • Cut material according to requirements in the work package.
  • Surface prep and clean materials as required.
  • Stack materials/build press rig according to specific instructions as required.
  • Deliver completed press rigs to specified area for pressing.
  • Deliver completed base panels to Dark room for processing.
  • Deliver covered panels (without leads) to Quality for inspection.
  • Check racks/specified areas for panels awaiting covers and back foil.
  • Use clicker die press to punch out covers and foil backing as required.
  • Use proper documentation to record lot numbers of raw material used.
  • Follow routine cleaning process for daily, weekly, monthly cleaning.
  • Build and maintain good working relationships with team members and management.
  • Participate in continuous improvement training and projects.
  • Support all internal and external audit activities as needed.
  • Always maintain safety when handling panel and press rig materials.
  • Follow all company policies, procedures and safety rules.




Competencies

  1. Direction following
  2. Attention to detail
  3. Organizational skills
  4. Teamwork
  5. Safety awareness
  6. Flexibility
  7. Accuracy/Technical ability
  8. Thoroughness
  9. Time management
  10. Reliability


Supervisory Responsibility

N/A


Work Environment

Production assembly environment. Clean room environment. Some of the work will require exposure to loud noises or fumes in the manufacturing environment. Potentially it could be required to improvise clothing and/or wear additional clothing (smock, hair/bread net, gloves, etc.) to adhere to cleanliness requirements.


Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand, walk, use hands to handle or feel, and reach with hands and arms. Position requires some degree of lifting (rolls of material and assembled press rigs). Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.


Position Type and Expected Hours of Work

This is a full-time position, and typical work hours and days are Monday through Friday, 7:00AM to 3:30PM. Saturdays as needed.

Your role as a Shift Lead is pivotal in ensuring a safe working and shopping environment. You’re the person who will oversee your shift to cultivate a great experience for both colleagues and customers daily. It’s B&Q’s ambition to make every customer count, so you’ll strive to ensure B&Q is a place colleagues love to work, and customers love to shop. In this role you will:

  • Be the heartbeat of the store day-to-day and ensure operations are running smoothly.
  • Make sure colleagues are deployed correctly to ‘make every customer count’ throughout your shift.
  • Be the first point of contact for customers and colleagues.
  • Make sure our stores are safe at all times.

What we need:

Our shift leads are key to running our business through their teams. In this role, we’re looking for the following qualities:

  • Passionate about customers and doing the right thing for them.
  • Like to have a global view and not be constrained to specific areas of the store.
  • Safety conscious and use an eye for detail to spot compliance opportunities.
  • Enjoy interacting with colleagues and working in a team.
  • Like to bring energy to each day and motivate those around you.
  • Confident to have autonomy and trust to make decisions for the customer at pace.

What's in it for me?

As part of a great team, you’ll be valued for who you are. We’re committed to making B&Q more diverse and representative of the communities we serve, where everyone can feel they belong and have equal opportunities. You will have access to a range of networks that represent our colleagues and allies and help us to continue to put diversity and inclusion at the heart of our business.

We also recognise that wellness means different things to different people, and we want to help colleagues be at their best and feel well by offering a range of benefits to help you. As well as a competitive salary, our benefits package includes

  • Award-winning pension scheme
  • ShareSave options
  • 6.6 weeks holiday
  • Payroll giving
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Shopping discounts
  • Colleague wellbeing benefits and lots more

If you require any additional support or reasonable adjustments to help you complete your application or throughout the recruitment process, please let us know. If you would like to be considered under the Disability Confident Scheme please contact us at recruitment@b-and-q.co.uk. If you meet the minimum criteria for the role, we'll consider your application in line with our Disability Confident commitments.

title: Fullstack developer (typescript & react) (hybrid)
description:
FULLSTACK DEVELOPER (TYPESCRIPT & REACT) (HYBRID PORTO)

Portuguese company hires for hybrid position

Location: Porto, Portugal

⚠️ Only candidates already based in Portugal will be considered

Work Model: Hybrid — 2 days per week in the office

️ Language Requirements: Fluent English required

Seniority: Júnior (1-3 years)

Rate Between €2200 - 2500 RV or unipessoal (gross value)

⚠️ Instructions: Please send your CV in English and make sure to include all skills and experience that match the requirements of the opportunity. This will significantly increase your chances of success.

About the Opportunity

We are looking for a Fullstack Developer to contribute to web applications using React, TypeScript, Node.js, and NestJS. You will work across frontend and backend development within a collaborative Agile team, with guidance to develop your technical skills.

Responsibilities

  • Develop responsive interfaces and reusable components using React and TypeScript.
  • Build backend services and REST APIs with Node.js and NestJS.
  • Integrate APIs, including data validation and error handling.
  • Contribute to database modelling, queries, authentication, and authorization.
  • Write frontend and backend unit tests.
  • Collaborate with Product, Design, and Engineering teams and participate in code reviews.

Requirements

  • 1–3 years in Fullstack, Frontend, or Backend development. Relevant internships, graduate programmes, and practical experience will be considered.
  • Hands-on experience with React and TypeScript, reusable components, and responsive design.
  • Experience with Tailwind CSS or similar styling frameworks, and backend development using Node.js and NestJS.
  • Understanding of REST APIs, HTTP, and error handling; familiarity with schema validation tools such as Zod.
  • Basic knowledge of PostgreSQL and ORMs such as Prisma, TypeORM, or MikroORM.
  • Understanding of OAuth2, OpenID Connect, and JWT.
  • Experience with Jest or Vitest, plus basic exposure to Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Familiarity with Git, CI/CD, code reviews, and Agile practices using Scrum or Kanban.

Preferred: Exposure to Playwright, Storybook, or Figma, and certifications in Cloud, DevOps, Platform Engineering, or Kubernetes.

Ideal Candidate Profile

A curious and proactive developer who communicates clearly, welcomes feedback, and seeks guidance when needed. Able to translate requirements into technical solutions with support, identify blockers, and gradually develop greater autonomy.

5 Questions for Candidates

  1. What experience do you have developing applications with React and TypeScript?
  2. Have you built REST APIs using Node.js and NestJS?
  3. What experience do you have with PostgreSQL, ORMs, and authentication mechanisms?
  4. Which testing frameworks, Git workflows, and CI/CD tools have you used?
  5. Are you fluent in English and available to work on-site in Porto 2 days per week?

Keywords

Fullstack Developer, TypeScript, React, Node.js, NestJS, Tailwind CSS, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Prisma, TypeORM, MikroORM, Zod, OAuth2, OpenID Connect, JWT, Jest, Vitest, Docker, Kubernetes, Git, CI/CD, Playwright, Storybook, Figma.

title: Sr. Software Engineer (AI Data Engineering)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. SOFTWARE ENGINEER (AI DATA ENGINEERING)

Be a member of the Artificial Intelligence Data Engineering Software team, building AI-powered tools and automation that solve real engineering problems for our launch vehicles and spacecraft.

Our team builds software that takes recurring, time-consuming work off engineers' plates so they can focus on hard engineering, from automated review of flight and test data to AI agents that help engineers prepare for missions and investigate anomalies. Your work will directly accelerate rapid reuse of the Falcon launch vehicle, support the world's largest satellite communication and AI constellations, and contribute to the development of the world's largest rocket capable of sending humans to Mars.

You will work side-by-side with engineers across avionics, propulsion, structures, and more to find where their time goes and build tools that give it back, using agentic AI systems, MCP servers, RAG-based search, data pipelines over large telemetry datasets, and traditional automation where it is the right answer. You will own problems end-to-end: scoping the solution with the engineers who have the problem, rolling it out, measuring the time it saves, and maintaining it as the vehicle and processes evolve.

Aerospace experience is not strictly required - we are looking for smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on an inspiring mission.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Partner directly with engineering teams to identify their most time-consuming, repetitive, or error-prone work, then design and build tools that automate it
  • Build automation that processes large volumes of engineering data, including telemetry, hardware design databases, configuration files, and manufacturing and test records, to automate data review, flag anomalies, and surface insights
  • Design agentic AI systems, multi-agent workflows, and MCP servers that let engineers query, analyze, and act on data across many internal systems
  • Integrate tools into CI/CD pipelines, mission workflows, and review/sign-off processes so automation runs where engineers already work
  • Build internal web dashboards that give engineers a clear view of mission status, open work, and data review results
  • Rapidly prototype and iterate, then take tools to a production-grade, maintainable state
  • Thoroughly test and validate all tools, including evaluating AI outputs against known-good results, so engineers can trust them in a flight-critical environment
  • Prioritize work by return on investment and track the engineering hours saved

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, data science, engineering, math, or physics; OR 4+ years of professional experience building automation for practical engineering use cases in lieu of a degree
  • 5+ years of experience in software engineering with a focus on automation tools and/or AI integrations (professional and personal projects are applicable)
  • 5+ years of programming experience in Python

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Track record of building tools that engineers or other end users actually adopted, including gathering requirements directly from users and iterating on their feedback
  • Comfort processing and analyzing large engineering or scientific datasets (time-series telemetry, sensor data, logs, etc.) using tools such as pandas and NumPy
  • Built code or configuration generators that turn a source of truth (design databases, spreadsheets, schemas) into validated outputs
  • Hands-on work building complex agentic AI systems and multi-agent workflows, including prompt and context engineering, tool/function calling, and MCP servers or agent skills
  • Ability to design evaluations for LLM-based tools, and the judgment to know when a deterministic script is a better fit than an AI model
  • Skilled at integrating with many systems through REST APIs, and quickly learning unfamiliar internal tools and data sources
  • Working knowledge of relational (PostgreSQL), non-relational, and vector databases, with strong SQL skills
  • Full-stack experience building web applications or dashboards (e.g., React/TypeScript frontends with Python backends such as FastAPI or Flask)
  • Proficiency developing on Linux, with a solid understanding of Git, testing, CI/CD, and monitoring
  • Familiarity deploying containerized applications using Docker and Kubernetes
  • Familiarity with hardware engineering concepts (electrical schematics and wiring, sensors, propulsion, controls, or test and manufacturing processes), or a background as a hardware or test engineer who moved into software
  • Strong communication skills and ability to explain technical tradeoffs to engineers in other disciplines
  • Self-directed and comfortable owning ambiguous problems from initial idea through long-term maintenance

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 3: $165,000.00 - $265,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to EEOCompliance@spacex.com.

title: Senior Cloud & DevOps Engineer
description:
About the role

As a Senior Cloud / DevOps Engineer embedded within a high-impact engineering squad, you will own cloud infrastructure, deployment pipelines, and security compliance for critical digital resilience and open banking platforms. You will design, build, and maintain a cloud-agnostic, portable infrastructure foundation targeted primarily for AWS Kubernetes (EKS).

Key responsibilities

  • Establish automated Terraform and Helm pipelines

  • Enforce strict vulnerability management

  • Integrate enterprise secrets management systems

  • Manage continuous delivery pipelines using feature flags for progressive beta rollouts

  • Partner closely with internal security teams to ensure releases align with strict penetration testing lead times and enterprise security governance

About you

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience provisioning, managing, and scaling production Kubernetes clusters on AWS (EKS)

  • Advanced proficiency with Terraform for Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and Helm for Kubernetes package management

  • Direct experience configuring, operating, and integrating HashiCorp Vault in production environments

  • Proven track record building CI/CD deployment pipelines utilizing LaunchDarkly (or equivalent feature flag tools) for progressive rollouts and feature kill-switches

  • Hands-on experience integrating Snyk vulnerability scanning and automated patching tools directly into CI/CD pipelines

  • Demonstrated background navigating enterprise security policies, vulnerability remediation, and formal penetration testing frameworks

  • Exposure to GCP infrastructure to support cloud-agnostic portability requirements

  • Operational familiarity supporting containerized backend services (Go/Java), PostgreSQL databases, Temporal workflow engines, or gRPC interfaces

  • Strong commitment to declarative infrastructure, strictly avoiding manual environment tweaks in favor of version-controlled modules

  • Proactive approach to secret management, vulnerability patching, and compliance integration across all release cycles

  • Available to commit to 4 weeks of onsite work within Melbourne CBD, with hybrid/remote following.
